# Welcome to Slate

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/index.md

Slate is one home for every AI coding tool you use. It shows every AI coding session on your Mac, live, and gives all 16 tools one memory, one set of skills and rules (Toolkit) and one set of connections (Connect).

Around them sit Projects, Tasks, Automations, Artifacts, Widgets and Activity, all in SQLite files on your Mac, one per workspace.

New here? [Getting Started](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/overview/getting-started.md) installs Slate and runs your first request. [Core Concepts](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/overview/concepts.md) is the mental model.

* **Every session, live.** [Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md) lists every AI coding session on this Mac, from any of the 16 tools. It shows who is working and who needs you.
* **One memory for all 16 tools.** Slate is an [MCP server](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server.md). Every connected [tool](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/brains.md) calls `recall` to load context and `remember` to save what it learned. A [filesystem watcher](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/session-capture.md) captures the sessions in your projects, so memory grows as you work. See [Memory](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory.md).
* **Skills and rules once.** [Toolkit](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio.md) writes one set of skills and instructions into each tool's own config. [Features by Agent](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/tool-features.md) says which tools it reaches today.
* **Sign in once. Your work never leaves your Mac.** You sign in with Google or GitHub at first launch, and the app then runs offline. The account holds your name, email and plan. Nothing of your work leaves your Mac unless you take an explicit action. See [Privacy & Security](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security.md).
* **Your own tools, no API keys.** Slate drives the CLI of any of [16 tools](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/brains.md) you already installed and signed in to. The first six are measured end to end. The ten newest are marked *unverified* where nobody has run a feature yet ([Features by Agent](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/tool-features.md)).
* **An agent inside Slate.** [Home](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent.md) reads and writes your workspace. [Curated MCP commands](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/mcp-commands.md) resolve a tool and prefill its arguments, so it runs well on a light model.
* **A real block editor.** [Docs](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/docs.md) are nested, drag-reorderable and keyboard-first. [Typed docs](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/docs/typed-docs.md) (plan, design, review, meeting…) give structure to real work.
* **Share a whole workspace, or none.** [Workspaces](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md) are containers. Everything in a workspace you share or join is read by its members, and other people's docs are read-only.

Free for individuals. Team plans are coming. See [Licensing & Updates](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/licensing.md).

> **Note:** Slate is in active development. It runs on macOS, with one app for Apple Silicon and one for Intel. Linux and Windows have early builds: see [Platform & Availability](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/platform.md).

---

# Getting Started

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/overview/getting-started.md

This guide takes you from a fresh install to a working workspace with cross-tool memory and a running agent.

***

## 1. Install

Slate runs on macOS 13.5 or later, Apple Silicon or Intel, with one app for each. The installer picks your Mac's. Linux and Windows have early builds, attached to each release from 0.1.58: see [Platform & Availability](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/platform.md). Install on a Mac with:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/install.sh | bash
```

The script downloads a prebuilt `Slate.app`, checks its checksum against the release's and its signature (a mismatch stops the install), quits a running Slate, installs to `/Applications` and opens it. Nothing compiles. Slate is not notarized by Apple, so a browser download would be quarantined by macOS, and `curl` avoids that.

To use [Home](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent.md) or give your tools one memory, install at least one **agent**: the [CLI of any of 16 tools](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/brains.md): Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Antigravity, OpenCode, Gemini, Cline, Grok Build, Kiro, Qwen Code, Droid, Hermes Agent, Goose, Kilo Code or Auggie. Slate drives the CLI you already signed in to, so there is no API key to enter.

**Sign in once. Your work never leaves your Mac.** The first launch asks you to sign in with Google or GitHub. This needs the internet once. The account holds your name, email and plan. Your work stays on this Mac. Slate keeps the sign-in on disk, so later launches open at once, even offline. The sign-in screen fills the window, so the app cannot be reached without it.

Slate then creates your Personal workspace at `~/Library/Application Support/app.slate.workspace/workspace.db`. Each workspace is its own SQLite file. You can copy it, back it up or open it in any SQLite browser: see [Your Data & Export](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/data-and-export.md).

Capture starts before setup. Slate finds the AI CLIs on your machine and starts reading their session transcripts when the window opens. The first setup screen names what it found. Nothing on your machine changes and nothing is sent.

Then a four-step setup runs: **Welcome, Agents, Integrations, Project**. Every step has **Skip setup** at the top. It ends setup the same way **Open Slate** on the last step does, and setup does not show again on the next launch. Everything can be changed later from the rail.

- **Welcome** shows who is signed in and what Slate is.
- **Agents** lists all sixteen tools, in the same order as Connect. A tool on this Mac reads *On this Mac · uses your own sign-in*: Slate can see the program but not whether you signed in to it, so it says what it relies on rather than asking you to sign in again. It has a switch that connects it and a choice of whether it runs Slate's own AI. A tool whose CLI is missing is greyed out, reads *Not on this Mac*, and offers only **Install**, which shows how to install it; after **Check again** finds it, it gets its switch. Ten of the sixteen read **Beta** beside their name: Slate works with them, but nobody has run a session on them yet to check every part (see [Features by Agent](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/tool-features.md)). Gemini reads *Needs a Gemini Code Assist licence or an API key*, because Gemini CLI no longer signs in personal Google accounts. Connecting registers Slate with the tool, which makes memory *shared*. It is the one time Slate asks before writing to another program's config. **Continue** waits until one tool is connected; **Skip setup** does not. Nothing is chosen for you. The choice is the same setting as Connect → Agents.
- **Integrations** connects the apps your work lives in, such as GitHub, Linear, Jira, Slack and Notion, with the same buttons as Connect → Integrations. You can go on without any.
- **Project** lists the git repositories in your home folder, most recently changed first, with nothing ticked. macOS may ask to let Slate see your Documents, Desktop or Downloads folder while it looks; Slate looks there only for git projects. A line says so while it looks, and another says so if it finds none. If macOS refused it a folder, a line names that folder and the setting that allows it (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Files and Folders), with **Scan again**. Tick the ones you work on, or choose another folder. Slate records only sessions that run in a project: work in other folders shows in Sessions under **No project** while it runs, where its row offers **Make a project**, and is not kept. A memory such a session writes is still saved, as global memory. Later, add a project from the project picker at the top of Projects. Under the folders, one line names what other tools keep on this Mac, such as *Found on this Mac: 1,200 observations in claude-mem, 4 projects in your editors.* claude-mem and agentmemory each get a **Preview** button there, so you can bring their memory in once your projects are added. See [Import](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/import.md).

Setup ends on **Sessions**, whether you finish it or skip it. Sessions shows every AI session on this Mac, live, even before an agent is connected. With nothing running, it offers **Connect an agent**. Every account is on the Free plan: everything Slate does on this Mac, with no card and no time limit. To hear when Team is ready, press **Tell me when it's ready** under Team in **Settings → Account**.

**Home** holds what setup skipped, in a **Set up Slate** card of three steps, each with one button:

1. **Connect an agent**: **Connect an agent** opens Connect → Agents.
2. **Start a session**: **New session** runs your tool in a folder.
3. **See your first memory**: **Open Memory** shows what a session decided or learned.

Each step ticks itself from what is in your workspace: a tool set, a session captured, a memory saved. The card shows how many are done and goes away when all three are, or when you press **Skip setup**. Under it, one line says: *A workspace holds your projects. A project is a folder you open.*

Sharing is not part of setup. It is in **Settings → Workspaces**.

## 2. Create your first docs

The left column is a permanent icon **rail**: Sessions, Home, Projects, Tasks, Memory, Activity, Artifacts, Widgets, Automations, Toolkit, Connect, Trash, Settings. Beside it is a **side panel** that switches with it. Click **Projects** for the [tree of your projects and docs](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/docs.md). The workspace mark at the top of the rail offers **New project…** and **Manage projects…**. The project picker under the Projects panel's title narrows the tree to one project, and its list ends with the same two. With no project yet, Projects' Overview says what a project is (a folder you open) and offers **New project**.

A new install starts with one doc, **Getting Started**. It lists where to start: connect an agent, start a session, add a project, and follow the **Set up Slate** card on Home.

Create a doc, give it an icon and title, and type. The editor is block-based (headings, lists, to-dos, code, quotes) with a slash menu and drag-to-reorder.

For real work use a [typed document](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/docs/typed-docs.md): a **group** to hold several projects, a **project** and a **branch** under it, and a **plan** or **design** doc under either. A project can stand without a group. Typed docs pre-fill a template.

Press <kbd>⌘K</kbd> any time to open the [command palette](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/search.md): jump to a doc, run an action, or search every title and body.

## 3. Connect an agent to your workspace

Open **Connect → Agents** and turn on the tools this workspace uses, choosing the account each one runs under. Every project or group inherits that and may override it. The CLIs Slate can drive, their models and defaults are on [Agents & Model Providers](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/brains.md).

Slate uses the CLI you already signed in to, so there is nothing to paste. If you keep separate work and personal CLI configs, set up a [project environment](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio/cli-profiles.md) for each.

## 4. Run your first request

Open **Home**, Slate's in-app [AI agent](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent.md). It reads and writes your workspace and calls any connected tool. Try:

* "Create a plan doc under my Slate project for the onboarding flow."
* "What did I work on this week?"
* "Summarize the open decisions across my projects."

The agent uses [curated commands](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/mcp-commands.md) to resolve the right tool and prefill its arguments, so these work on a light local model.

## 5. Connect Slate to your other agents

This is where Slate becomes a shared memory. Slate is an [MCP server](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server.md), so any of the 16 agents can read and write the same workspace:

1. Turn your tool on in **Connect → Agents**, or see [Connecting Your Agents](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/connecting.md).
2. Connected tools call `recall` to load context and `remember` to save decisions, into the same docs you edit by hand.

The [session watcher](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/session-capture.md) needs nothing turned on. It has read the transcripts of the tools you turned on since the first launch. Capture is measured on eight tools and unverified on the rest, see [Session Capture](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/session-capture.md).

[Toolkit](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio.md) then lets you write one set of instructions and skills and sync them to every tool.

***

## 6. Optional: share with a workspace

A **shared workspace** is a second store its members read. Create or join one in **Settings → Workspaces**, then switch into it from the top of the rail. The whole app follows, and everything you do there belongs to its members.

Sharing needs the Team plan, which is coming soon. Accounts that already shared keep sharing at no charge until Team ships. Every workspace has the same sharing switch, Personal included, and turning it on first counts what it would publish. A captured AI session's doc is never published. To share one project rather than a whole workspace, move it: its ⋯ menu offers **Move to <workspace>**, and the subtree goes with its memory. Nobody can edit your docs, whatever their role. See [Workspaces](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md).

***

## Where to go next

* [Core Concepts](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/overview/concepts.md): docs, memory and Toolkit.
* [Slate as an MCP Server](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server.md): the memory contract.
* [Privacy & Security](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security.md): what stays local and what does not.

# Core Concepts

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/overview/concepts.md

Slate is one home for every AI coding tool: every session live on your Mac, and one memory plus one set of skills and rules for all 16 tools. Six ideas underlie it.

## 1. Everything is a doc

The [doc](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/docs.md) is Slate's universal unit. A group, a project, a design doc and a captured AI session are all rows in one `doc` table, told apart by an optional `doc_type`. Docs nest in a tree (`parent_id`), order by a fractional `position` so drag-reorder never renumbers the tree, and hold their content as block-editor JSON. The same few operations (create, read, update, move, Trash) work everywhere, by hand or by AI.

## 2. Typed documents give work structure

A doc can be [typed](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/docs/typed-docs.md): `group`, `project`, `branch`, `plan`, `design`, `review`, `meeting`, `test-plan`, `bug-report`, `mission` or plain `general`. The type pre-fills a template and limits where the doc can live. A `branch` sits under a `project`. A `project` sits under a `group` or stands alone. Knowledge docs (plans, designs, reviews) hang off any of them, so memory tools resolve "the plan for the branch I'm on" without an id.

## 3. One memory, shared over MCP

Slate is also a [memory server](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server.md). It speaks [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io), so any of the 16 [tools](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/brains.md), or Slate's own [Home](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent.md), calls the same two verbs:

* **`recall`** at the start of a task loads the relevant context: the brief for your branch, project conventions, project memories.
* **`remember`** at the end saves a decision, result or preference, filed on the doc the hierarchy resolves to.

A [filesystem watcher](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/session-capture.md) captures the sessions themselves, so memory grows even when a tool forgets to write.

## 4. Agents drive your CLIs

Slate ships no model and asks for no API key. An [agent](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/brains.md) is a thin driver over a CLI you already installed and signed in to: **Claude Code**, **Codex**, **Cursor**, **GitHub Copilot**, **Antigravity**, **OpenCode**, **Gemini**, **Cline**, **Grok Build**, **Kiro**, **Qwen Code**, **Droid**, **Hermes Agent**, **Goose**, **Kilo Code** or **Auggie**. Slate launches it from Rust, so credentials stay in those tools. A light model works because code [resolves the tool and prefills its arguments](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/mcp-commands.md) and the model fills only the gaps.

## 5. Toolkit is one playbook for every tool

[Toolkit](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio.md) is where you write instructions and skills once, in `AGENTS.md` and `.slate/`, and project them into every agent's native config. Change the playbook, run `yarn studio sync`, and every tool picks it up. [Features by Agent](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/tool-features.md) says which tools it reaches today.

## 6. A workspace is shared or private as a whole

[Workspaces](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md) share by **container**. A team's workspace is the team's, and everything in it is shared. Your **Personal** workspace starts unshared and syncs only if you switch its sharing on. Each shared workspace is its own SQLite file; switch from the top of the rail. Nothing is marked doc by doc: private work stays in an unshared workspace.

Sharing is one-way, and each doc has one writer, its author. That keeps merge conflicts and version columns out of the design. A teammate's doc opens read-only in the real editor, with a line saying why.

---

# Uninstalling

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/overview/uninstalling.md

One command removes Slate and puts back what it changed:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/uninstall.sh | bash
```

**Your workspace is kept.** Removing it takes a second, explicit flag.

## See it first

`--dry-run` prints every step, lists the accounts it would clean, and changes nothing:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/uninstall.sh | bash -s -- --dry-run
```

Check the line that names your workspace and its size.

## What it removes

| | |
|---|---|
| **Slate's entries in your agents** | The plugin trees, the capture hooks and the MCP registrations, in exactly the accounts Slate wrote to |
| **`/Applications/Slate.app`** | The app itself |
| **The start-at-login item** | `~/Library/LaunchAgents/Slate.plist`, if you turned on Start Slate at login |
| **Logs, cache and webview state** | Three rebuildable directories under `~/Library` |

Slate installs itself into up to eighteen other products (the 16 agents, Claude Desktop and VS Code). Dragging Slate to the Trash leaves every entry behind, pointing at an app that is gone. So the app undoes its own work first, from a record of the accounts it wrote to. **An MCP server you registered yourself is never touched**, and neither is a plugin marketplace that only shares a name.

## What it keeps

Your data folder, `~/Library/Application Support/app.slate.workspace/`:

* `workspace.db`, your Personal docs and memory
* one file for each shared workspace
* `machine.db` (settings that describe this computer, the telemetry id and your choices about it)
* your cloud sign-in file
* the backups

It is plain SQLite, and reinstalling picks the same file up. Slate also leaves what Toolkit wrote into your own project folders (skill folders, instruction files): those belong to the project.

## Removing the workspace too

```bash
curl -fsSL https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/uninstall.sh | bash -s -- --delete-workspace
```

**This cannot be undone.** It removes the whole data folder; no other copy exists, locally or in the cloud. A shared workspace keeps the rows you published, for its members, until you withdraw them (**Stop sharing**) or remove them with **Erase my work**. Do that first, and export what you want to keep (Settings → Workspaces → the workspace → Storage). A Personal workspace you moved elsewhere stays where you put it.

## Options

| Flag | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | Print every step and change nothing |
| `--delete-workspace` | Also remove the whole data folder: workspaces, `machine.db`, sign-in file and backups |
| `--keep-connections` | Leave Slate's entries in your agents alone |
| `--prefix <dir>` | Look for `Slate.app` somewhere other than `/Applications` |

The script never asks a question, so the destructive half is a flag you type.

**It removes only Slate.** The script reads the bundle id of `Slate.app` first. If the id is not `app.slate.workspace`, or cannot be read, the app may be another product with the same name. The script then stops and removes nothing.

## If you already removed the app

The script still cleans the logs, cache and webview state, and reports that it could not remove the agent entries. They are inert. To remove them, reinstall Slate and run the uninstaller again.

## Doing it by hand

```bash
# 1. Quit Slate, so the running copy cannot write back what the next step removes.
osascript -e 'tell application "Slate" to quit'

# 2. The agent entries — this is the step that needs the app.
/Applications/Slate.app/Contents/MacOS/slate --list-connections   # see them
/Applications/Slate.app/Contents/MacOS/slate --disconnect-all     # remove them

# 3. The start-at-login item, if you turned it on. The first line may print an error when
#    it is not loaded; that is fine.
launchctl bootout "gui/$(id -u)/Slate"
rm -f ~/Library/LaunchAgents/Slate.plist

# 4. The app, and the three rebuildable directories.
rm -rf /Applications/Slate.app
rm -rf ~/Library/Logs/app.slate.workspace
rm -rf ~/Library/Caches/app.slate.workspace
rm -rf ~/Library/WebKit/app.slate.workspace

# 5. Your workspace — only if you mean it.
rm -rf ~/Library/Application\ Support/app.slate.workspace
```

* [Platform & Availability](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/platform.md)
* [Your Data & Export](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/data-and-export.md): get your docs out before you go
* [Connect](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md): what Slate writes into your agents, and when

# Sessions — the Live Tracker

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md

The **Sessions** tab lists every AI-CLI session on this machine, live, for the 16 agents. It shows who is working, who needs you and where each runs.

Nothing to install: any tool whose transcripts the capture watcher sees (non-default config directories too) is tracked. Claude Code lists its own sessions (`claude agents --json`), so its rows carry the real session id, the process and whether a background job finished. Other tools are read from transcripts and the process table. Measured on Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, Gemini, Hermes Agent and Goose; unverified on the rest ([Features by Agent](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/tool-features.md)). A row shows the session's [name](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/tabs.md#naming-a-session) when it has one.

**Sub-agents are not sessions.** The parent's row counts the live ones and expands to name them; on the map each is a pip around its session. Only recently active ones show, and none can be stopped (they run in the parent's process).

## What you see

The list shows live sessions on the whole computer. An ended session folds into **Just finished** and **Earlier today**. Each live session has one state:

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Needs you** | The tool finished a turn and is blocked on you. **⌘⇧J** goes to the one waiting longest, then the next. The tab header shows the count. Kinds: **Needs permission** (a tool call waits for your yes), **Asks you** (the turn ends on a question), **Finished** (the turn is a report) |
| **Working** | The session wrote a turn in the last 45 seconds. For Claude Code only a turn counts: the bookkeeping lines it adds to a transcript afterwards do not |
| **Idle** | Quiet, and you spoke last. A session that only waits is idle too, however fresh its transcript: its newest step is a running `sleep`, a shell loop that sleeps until something is ready, or a scheduled wakeup. The wait must be the whole command: `sleep 30 && npm test` is work. A Claude Code background job that finished but still runs its process is idle too, until **Stop** ends it (Claude Code keeps that process until `claude stop`). Grey dot, no pulse, flow word **Waiting** |

When a session starts waiting on a permission or question and Slate is not in front, macOS shows one notification with the question, once per wait (never for waits already there when Slate opened). A finished turn posts nothing; it waits on [Home](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent.md#what-home-shows). **Tell me when a session needs me** in Automations › Built-in turns it off. See [How status works](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/status.md).

## In the menu bar

A Sessions icon shows a count while a session needs you. Its panel lists sessions working or waiting on you, waiting first in Home's order (permission, question, finished), each with kind and tool, and its workspace (a small dot and the name) when they span more than one workspace. Click one to open it. The panel also has **Keep the computer awake**, **New session**, **Open Slate** and **Quit Slate**.

Closing the window only hides it; ⌘Q quits. A hidden window stops reading sessions and all timers and catches up on opening; the count, notification and keep-awake come from the server and keep working. A visible but unused window shows changes within 5 seconds, other timers at a quarter pace. Automations › Built-in has **Show Slate in the menu bar** (on) and **Start Slate at login** (off).

## Narrowing to a workspace or a project

The **workspace picker** under the side panel's title starts on **All workspaces** each time the tab opens. Pick one to keep only its sessions, in list and map. A session no workspace claims counts as Personal's. A **project picker** then appears (**All projects**); a project keeps sessions in it or in its git repositories and branches. Changing the workspace drops the project. The choice lasts while the window is open. **Just finished** and **Earlier today** follow both. Opening one of their docs, or **All past sessions**, from another workspace switches the window to it first.

## The map and the list

The map shows the machine as a radial tree, **group → project → branch → session**, in Slate's own greens, not a workspace's colour. The **rail** reads it out: a row per session with status dot, title, live line and meta line. Hovering one lights the other. Click a row to open the session in a temporary tab; **double-click** keeps it. Map, row, menu, parking and past sessions: [The map and the list](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/list.md). With nothing selected, the main area shows the map.

## A session's pull request

Slate reads `refs/pull/*` on origin, asking once a minute, and shows **#118** on the row once one points at the branch's tip. The trunk never shows one. The number may belong to a merged or closed pull request (refs cannot tell); a branch sharing its tip with another on origin shows none. Slate opens no pull requests: push and open one on the code host.

## The keyboard

Tab reaches the rail's rows (cloud rows included); Enter opens one. ↑/↓ or **j**/**k** move, **Home** and **End** jump to the ends (no wrap), **Escape** returns focus to the terminal; ↑ or **k** from outside enters at the last row. On the focused row **f** starts a second agent in its folder and **s** stops it (second press within four seconds); on a cloud row both do nothing, and **f** does nothing on a row with no folder. These letters act only with focus inside the rail and never in a text field; modified chords (⌘⇧J, ⌘K) pass through. From anywhere, ⌘K → **Focus the sessions list** focuses the first row (listed only while a row is on screen). All keys: [Keyboard shortcuts](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/shortcuts.md#sessions).

## Stopping a session

Each row whose session can end has an **End** button. The first click arms it: it turns red and reads **End?** (*Click End? or press s again to end it*), and stays shown while armed; the second click, or **s**, ends it. Mouse and keyboard share one arm, which resets after four seconds.

| Session | Stop does |
| --- | --- |
| Backgrounded Claude | `claude stop <handle>`: **keeps the conversation**, so you can attach again |
| Everything else | `SIGTERM`, so the CLI closes its own MCP subprocesses; the conversation ends |

A signal is refused when the process is no longer the reported tool (pids are recycled). It works on sessions Slate never started, such as a forgotten CLI in a distant terminal.

**Quitting Slate** ends the sessions it hosts. First, a Claude session not yet a background job gets its detach input and 1.2 seconds (one wait for all), so it lives on as a job; an existing job keeps running.

## More about sessions

- [The map and the list](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/list.md): map, rows, row menu, parking, past sessions.
- [Start a session](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/start.md): from the list or a doc, open a folder, chat, plain shell, take over, hand back.
- [Worktrees](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/worktrees.md): the form, ports, run preview, Pick, cleanup.
- [Cloud sessions and phone](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/cloud.md)
- [The terminal and the side panel](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/terminal.md): terminal, Conversation, Details, Turns, timeline.
- [Tabs, columns and names](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/tabs.md): side by side, naming, agents that know each other.
- [Review the branch](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/review.md): waiting branches, source control, whole-branch review, rewinding.
- [Files, memories and editing](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/files.md)
- [Session flow](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/flow.md): Overview, Plan, Build, Check, Land.
- [How status works](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/status.md): how a state is decided and kept current.
