# The map and the list

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/list.md

The Sessions tab draws one list twice, as a radial map and a rail. Use this guide to read a node, row or colour.

## The map

A radial tree with this machine at the centre: **group → project → branch → session**. A project on its own sits on the first ring; one in a group, a ring out. A session with no project and no branch hangs from **No project**. With work in several workspaces, a workspace ring sits inside the group ring. Each level splits its parent's angle by the sessions beneath. The map wears Slate's own greens, not a workspace's colour; the halo is status, and a node shows the most urgent state beneath it.

Chip names are cut in the middle at 16 characters (workspace), 20 (project), 18 (git repository); a branch keeps its start, cut at 15 (`fix/sessions-gr…`). Point at a node for the whole name. Hovering map or rail lights the other; pointing at a project or branch lights every row under it. The map always fits the panel: no zoom, pan or scroll.

- Click a group or project to centre it. The rail narrows to its sessions; a crumb trail names where you are, and any crumb jumps to that level.
- **All**, empty space or Escape returns to the whole machine.
- Drag a node to reorder it among siblings; **Reset layout** undoes it.
- Below about 1024px the map is dropped and the rail shows everything.

## The rail

Two levels: **group or project**, then **sessions**. A row names its branch, and its project when the group holds several. With two workspaces running, a heading names both (*Work / Beacon*). Order is urgency, then name: most blocked first, then busiest, then longest waiting; within a level, blocked, working, idle, longest-waiting first. Order holds still while the pointer or focus is in the rail.

A session groups under the group or project its folder is filed under. One in a git repository no project holds groups under that git repository's name. Anything else (plain folder, home folder, no folder) goes under **No project**. A session outside every project is shown while it runs and not recorded.

**A session is listed where its edits land.** An agent can edit another worktree of the same project by full path. Slate lists it under the worktree of its latest edit, with that branch and *from <folder>* naming its terminal's folder. Before any edit it sits under its start folder; edits outside the project do not move it. The same rule picks its briefing branch and memory doc.

## A row

| Part | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| Title | The **branch**, with what its checkout holds and its pull request (`ui/hotfixes ↑4`); also heads the doc and tab. Tooltip: what it was asked (or its name) and the branch goal. No branch: the name, else the opening prompt. Claude Code's default name (`slate-66`) counts as none. Home cards are titled by what was asked |
| Live line | The question when it waits on you; what it said it was doing when it works; the next unticked plan item when it went quiet with work left |
| Meta line | Tool mark, time since it moved, how it runs, context fill, [flow](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/flow.md) strip with its current word ("Build", "Check", "Waiting") or plan progress (`0/4`) before any flow. Terminal glyph: Slate runs it and you can type. Eye: your own terminal, Slate only follows. **Flagged** badge: an unseen transcript flag; point at it for each flag and its run |

**Colour.** Amber: needs you. Green dot: working, pulses three times at work start, then still. Grey: idle, and everything else. Green and red: added and removed lines. Red: **missing** and failures. Blue: live sub-agent count.

**Context fill** is read from the transcript. Codex states its window: bar and `8% of 258k`, darker from 75%. Claude Code and OpenCode show the count alone (`323k`). Gemini and Cursor record nothing per turn, so show nothing. A session's **tab** shows only status dot and name.

**Checkout marks.** `↑3` commits the checkout has that its base lacks; `↓1` how far the base moved on; grey ring: uncommitted work; **missing**: a worktree git lists whose folder is gone; **not read**: the folder is there but git did not answer in time (the last counts read stay when there are any). Level with base: nothing. A checkout with nothing running is listed as *checked out, nothing running*. `#118`: pull request. **owed** pill: real work, no memory recorded. **Review** tag: a branch waiting for you ([Branches waiting for review](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/review.md#branches-waiting-for-review)).

## Row actions

A click opens a temporary tab the next click replaces; **double-click** keeps it. Pointing at a row shows **⋯**, **End** (second click ends it), **what its branch changed** (the [whole review](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/review.md#reviewing-the-whole-branch), no session needed) and **+** (start a session there). **⋯** opens with the session's own acts:

- **Open beside** ([Sessions side by side](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/tabs.md#sessions-side-by-side)); ⌘-click does the same.
- **PR #118**, once origin has a pull request for the branch: opens it in your browser.
- **Hand back to my terminal**, on a Claude Code session Slate runs ([Moving a session back to your terminal](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/start.md#moving-a-session-back-to-your-terminal)).

Below a rule: **New session**, **New worktree** (project row with several git repositories), **Copy path**, **Make a project** (row in **No project**), **Copy resume command** (the tool's resume command, such as `claude --resume <id>`; first six tools only, the ten newest have none yet).

**Park** hides a *checked out, nothing running* checkout without removing it, in a **Parked · n** line at the end of its project with **Unpark** beside each. A checkout with a running session, or a [branch waiting for review](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/review.md#branches-waiting-for-review), is never hidden. Parked state is kept on this machine only.

## Finished and past sessions

**Just finished** sits dim at the rail's foot for ten minutes. A row shows tool mark and end time, with a tick only if its last turn finished; a session stopped mid-turn says "Stopped before it finished". A click opens its record, or the doc the work belongs to until the record is saved.

**Earlier today in \<workspace>** folds every other session from today (local day), minus Just finished and running ones; collapsed with its count. **All past sessions in \<workspace> →** opens the whole history, newest first, at `/sessions?past=1`, no time limit; each row has **Resume**.

A failure (failed Run preview, refused start, failed Stop) shows under its row, or at the head of the list when the row is off screen. The rail is the left side panel: drag its edge to resize; **⌘\\** hides it when a terminal wants the full width.

---

# Start a session

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/start.md

Point at where the work is and press **+**. The session starts on the tool and account of that project or group and opens in Slate.

## From the list

**Where you look is where it starts.** Pointing at a group, project or branch (map node, heading or rail row) shows **+**, titled **New session**.

1. Click **+**. A session starts there at once on the group or project's default tool, under its account, and opens. No picker.
2. A project also has **New worktree**, which opens the [worktree form](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/worktrees.md) for it.
3. A group or project with nothing to run in shows no control. A refused launch shows on the tab in its own words.

The **+** in the side panel's title row starts a session elsewhere or on another tool, in a tree of **group → project → branch** (a workspace level above when several have work). Click a row to start there; a row with its own folder shows it. A git project ends with **New worktree…**; a plain folder has none.

**A session runs as the workspace its project or group belongs to**, whichever the window shows (a work project picked in Personal uses the work agent and account). A refused start shows at the picker's top; every start, refusal and failure goes to `slate.log`. Sessions started from Slate always start in a project.

**Runs on**, above the tree, lists the agents connected in Connect → Agents for the workspace in focus (named when several have work). It starts on that workspace's default; another pick applies to this session only. The worktree form has it too. Groups and projects with no linked folder are not offered.

## Open a folder

**Open folder…** starts a session in any folder. A folder another workspace holds opens there. Otherwise it becomes a project in the workspace on screen, by the same rules as New project, onboarding and **Make a project**:

| Folder | Becomes |
| --- | --- |
| Worktree or subfolder of a git repository | That git repository |
| Already known | Its doc opens; a doc in Trash comes back |
| Inside a group | A project in that group |
| Plain folder holding two or more git repositories | Asks first; each git repository becomes its own project. **Group them** puts them in one group (named after the folder unless you type another name there); **Keep them apart** leaves each alone. The folder itself never becomes the group |
| Anything else | A project on its own |

Your home folder and the disk root are refused, because every session would file under them.

### You choose your projects

Slate makes no project itself. Setup's last step lists git repositories, newest change first, nothing ticked; ticked ones become projects. It never lists your home folder, temporary folders, an agent's own folder, Slate's data folder or a removed folder. A removed project stays removed until you restore its doc or add the folder.

**A session in a folder no project holds is not recorded**: no session doc, nothing in Docs. Memories it writes with `remember` or `record_decision` are still saved, as global memory. Adding the folder later (setup, **+** in Projects, or the session's row) records sessions there from then on and earlier ones whose transcripts remain on disk. Restoring a project from Trash does the same.

A row in **No project** offers **Make a project** under **⋯**. With several workspaces the menu names each (**Make a project in Work**), the session's own first. A folder no workspace claims goes to Personal, private by default.

## From a doc

A branch, project or group doc has **Start session** in its header. It runs the tool its group (or project) has connected, in the doc's folder, under the account its group or project assigns that tool, and opens it. A doc with a folder also has a plain terminal button.

A doc **Goal** is seeded into the CLI prompt with the next unchecked plan item (`Continue on feat/x: … — next: …`): typed, never sent, always one line (a newline would send). If a CLI's startup repaint swallows it, the terminal says so and offers **Insert it** or copy.

A refusal names the fix: *"Acme does not use gemini. Sessions under /code/acme use: claude. Add it in Connect → Agents to allow it here."* A doc with no folder is refused the same way.

**A doc shows what runs on it.** Sessions working towards it appear in its header as *needs you*, *working* or *idle*; click one to open it. This stops a second session starting on a branch that already has one working.

## A chat instead of a terminal

**Chat**, beside **+** on a group heading and map node and in a row's **⋯**, starts the group or project's tool but draws it as Home does: each turn, each tool step as it runs, an approval card where the tool needs your yes. A row's chat works in that row's checkout. It opens as a tab named for the group or project; its composer shows the folder.

Its tool is not Home's, so a chat never restarts Home's conversation. It lasts as long as its tab (**Close and end this chat** stops its tool, as does quitting) and is not recorded as a session. Use a terminal session for work to leave running.

## A plain shell

**⌃`** opens a plain login shell (your shell and environment) in the folder of the doc you are on, or your home directory when nothing names one. It is hosted like a session: it survives navigating away, opens in the Sessions tab, and the [terminal](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/terminal.md) features apply. It has no tool account and no hand-back.

## Taking over a session from your terminal

A session in your own terminal can be continued here. **Clicking its row only shows it**: its conversation, live, read from the transcript. Details and changes are in the window's panel. One button above it says what continuing would do; nothing on that screen types into your terminal.

| Session | Offer |
| --- | --- |
| Already a background job (Claude Code job, Cursor `persist`) | No button. The row opens it as itself with `claude attach` or `cursor-agent persist attach`; copies and interrupts nothing |
| Claude Code in a terminal, Codex, OpenCode | **Continue in a copy** (`--resume <id> --fork-session`, `codex fork <id>`, `opencode --session <id> --fork`): a second conversation with the whole history; the original keeps running |
| Cursor, Gemini | **Move here**. `cursor-agent --resume` appends to the original transcript, so two processes would write one file; the original is ended first, and the button asks twice because an in-flight turn is lost |

A copy has its own transcript, so the two never interleave. Its row says **Copy in Slate**. The original's tab keeps showing the original live, and its row offers **Open your copy** to read or stop the copy. Offers use the session's own account (another account would find nothing and quietly start a new conversation).

## Moving a session back to your terminal

**Hand back to my terminal**, in a row's **⋯** (*Keeps running; you get the command to resume it*), detaches a session Slate runs and leaves it running. Only Claude Code supports it, so the item shows only on a Claude Code session Slate runs.

1. Slate sends the tool's detach input (`/bg` for Claude Code), waits about 1.5 seconds and closes the session's terminal.
2. A message gives the resume command with **Copy resume command**: `claude attach <handle>`, prefixed with the account where there is one.
3. If Slate cannot name the command, the message says *It keeps running in the background*.

---

# Worktrees

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/worktrees.md

A worktree is a second checkout of a project on its own branch, so an agent works without touching your main folder. Use **New worktree** on a project or in the **New session** tree; a session then starts inside it.

## The form

Fields: **Branch**, **From** (local branches only, nothing fetched) and the **Folder** it will make, always a sibling of the project.

**Carry over** makes the folder usable: `git worktree add` copies tracked files only, so a fresh worktree lacks dependencies, `.env` and build output. The form offers what the project ignores at top level as chips; tick `node_modules`, skip `.DS_Store`.

- Mac: each folder is cloned copy-on-write (no disk cost until a file changes; changes never reach the original). Elsewhere: hard links. Nothing carried is tracked.
- A missing ticked path or failed copy: the worktree is made, the form names the path, holds the start and offers **Start anyway**.

| Setting | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Then run** | One command in the new folder once files are there (build, codegen, submodule fetch). Empty is normal |
| **On remove** | One command in the folder just before the worktree is removed, however it is removed: stop a dev server, drop a local database, free a port. If it fails the worktree stays and the error shows its output (up to 60 seconds) |
| Shell | `/bin/sh -c` on macOS and Linux, with your login shell's `PATH` and environment; PowerShell on Windows (`cmd` if missing); untranslated, so write for your shell |

**Carry over**, **Then run**, **On remove** and **Run preview** are saved on the project (so on its group for later worktrees) only when you press **Create and start**. Closing the form or **Back** saves nothing.

**A failed worktree is rolled back.** If carry-over or **Then run** fails, the folder, git's record and the port are removed and the error shows with the command's output. The branch goes too if Slate made it for this worktree and nothing moved it since; an existing branch stays. Fix the cause and press **Create and start** again with the same name.

## Ports and temp folders

Each worktree Slate makes gets a free port from 4100 to 4999, kept until removal and stored on this computer only. It is `SLATE_PORT` in **Then run**, **On remove** and every session terminal in or under that folder, so two worktrees can each run `vite --port $SLATE_PORT`. The row shows `:4101`. A hand-made worktree has none. Sessions there also get a temp folder outside the worktree (`TMPDIR`, `TMP`, `TEMP`), removed with it.

## Run preview

**Run preview** is the command that starts a checkout's dev server, such as `yarn dev`, offered in a session row's **⋯**.

1. Its terminal opens beside the session, so a failure says why.
2. When the server prints a local address (`http://localhost:5173`), it opens as a **Preview** tab in the strip.
3. The preview can reload, open in your browser, or **Stop**, which ends the server's terminal and closes the tab (the tab also closes when the terminal ends).

The first run on a project with no command asks for it; **Save and run** stores it. A checkout with no project runs it once and saves nothing.

**Pick** (crosshair) turns the preview into a picker. Point at anything to outline it, click, and its description is pasted at the prompt of the session in that folder: the doc it is on, a CSS selector, size and position, deciding styles, its HTML. Nothing is submitted; add the change and press Enter. No screenshot (other origin). The web page is framed through a small proxy on Slate's loopback port that adds one script and serves only a local dev server; hot reload works. Slate keeps proxies for the 16 most recently used dev servers; an older one is closed and starts again when you pick there again. Click the crosshair again for the plain preview.

## A worktree made for a session ends with it

When the session started in a new worktree ends (you exit the tool or press Stop; closing its tab is not an end), the worktree is removed:

| State | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Nothing uncommitted, branch merged or empty | Folder and branch go |
| Commits not merged | Folder goes, branch stays |
| Uncommitted changes | Asks once: **Keep worktree** or **Delete forever** |

First, what the session left running there is stopped: every process Slate started for that worktree whose working folder is still inside it (dev server, watcher, test run) gets a polite stop, then a forced one after 3 seconds. Slate knows its own by a mark it gives each session, setup and teardown line for that worktree, never by name or port. A process you started elsewhere is never touched, and shells, multiplexers (`tmux`, `screen`, `zellij`), editors and apps are spared even when Slate started them. macOS hides the environment of its own system programs, so one of those (`tail`, `ruby`) is left running. Windows cannot see another process's folder, so it stops processes whose command line names a path inside the worktree or that listen on its port.

A message at the window's bottom says what was returned, **Cleaned up · stopped :3000 · 11.2 GB freed**, and what happened to worktree and branch. It waits while another session still works in the folder. It never touches a worktree not made for a session: hand-made, another tool's, or one whose session was running when Slate quit. The folder is renamed aside at once and removed in the background.

**Removing a worktree by hand** is under the trash icon on a branch row in **New session**. It stops no processes and counts nothing. It refuses a checkout with uncommitted work unless you choose to discard it, and can remove the branch too. A dirty branch is marked before the click; a worktree whose folder is gone says **missing**, and one git did not answer for says **not read**, never clean.

Reviewing and merging a finished branch: [Review the branch](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/review.md#branches-waiting-for-review).

---

# Cloud sessions and phone

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/cloud.md

A cloud session runs on your agent's computer. A phone session runs here and you continue it in your tool's app. Both start from **New session**.

## Cloud sessions

**Claude Code** and **Codex** have them. Gemini and OpenCode have none; Cursor's cloud agents have a web API only ([agent features](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/tool-features.md)).

1. Open **New session → Cloud**.
2. Write the task, pick a project (git repositories only: the cloud works on a copy).
3. Press **Start in cloud**.

The form says what leaves your computer:

- **Claude** clones the project's GitHub remote at its current branch, so push first. With no GitHub remote it uploads the history and uncommitted changes to tracked files (not untracked).
- **Codex** runs in an *environment* you set up for the git repository at chatgpt.com/codex, on its GitHub remote at your current branch. Type its name; earlier names are offered and the last one used per project is prefilled.

It runs under the project's profile. Slate asks that account's CLI whether it can start one before Start enables. Claude needs a claude.ai sign-in (API key, token, Bedrock or Vertex accounts cannot; the form says so). Codex needs a ChatGPT sign-in; an expired one is told to run `codex login`.

**Find it** in the list under its project, with a cloud where the status dot sits. A Codex row says working, ready, applied or failed (Codex's list is asked once a minute while Sessions is open). Claude keeps no list; its row says the status is on claude.ai.

**Its doc** shows what you asked and every message sent, with the tool's controls:

| Tool | Controls |
| --- | --- |
| Claude | **Send** a follow-up (Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line; queued, answered on claude.ai). **Bring back** opens it in a new worktree with the whole conversation, as a normal session |
| Codex | No Send. **Show diff** (read-only). **Apply in a worktree** lands the changes, uncommitted, in a new worktree and opens its changes |
| Both | **Open on** the tool's site; **Remove from Slate** (it stays on the site). Neither tool offers Stop, and the doc says so |

**Removed on the tool's site.** Codex says so when asked, and the session leaves the list. Claude says so only on the next Send: the first Send to a session removed on claude.ai drops it, with a sentence why.

**Started somewhere else.** Claude has no command that lists cloud sessions, so Slate keeps its own record: sessions it started, and ones another Claude Code session started while Slate's hooks were connected (a scheduled task run with the RemoteTrigger tool, or `claude --cloud "<task>"`). The row appears within 15 seconds while the window is open, under the project holding the calling session's folder, labelled **started by a scheduled task** or **started from another session**. Codex lists only sessions Slate started. Not recorded: cloud sessions started on the web or phone, and scheduled tasks firing on their own schedule.

**Memory.** A brought-back Claude session writes a normal transcript once you send a message. A Codex session brings back changes only; applying it notes them on the project's doc. A running cloud session has no Slate hooks and cannot reach memory, so its decisions arrive as a record (ADR 0071).

## On my phone

A session can continue from your phone while it runs here. Slate has no phone app: you pick it up in your tool's app. Today that is **Claude Code**, in the Claude app (**Code** tab) or at claude.ai/code.

- **Start on the phone**: turn on **On my phone** in **New session**, above the options beside **Runs on**.
- **Move a running session to the phone**: **On my phone** at the top of its doc.

Either opens a card, **Ready on my phone**, with three steps and the session's claude.ai link (**Copy**, **Open**). The same button, now blue, reopens it; **Stop phone access** turns it off. A phone mark shows in the list and the header counts them. Slate reads this from the transcript, so it also shows a session you put on the phone with `/remote-control` in your own terminal.

The control is on every session, greyed out with a reason where it cannot work:

| Case | State |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code running in Slate | Works |
| Claude Code in your own terminal | Shown, not switched from Slate: type `/remote-control` there |
| Account that cannot (API key, token, Bedrock, Vertex, or off by your organization) | Greyed, with Claude's reason. Slate asks Claude (`claude doctor`) once per account |
| Codex | Not supported yet: it pairs your whole computer with the ChatGPT app, not one session |
| Cursor, Gemini, OpenCode | Cursor's phone control is in its app; Gemini and OpenCode have none |

**It still runs here**, so hooks, memory and capture work as always. While on, the conversation also goes through Anthropic (ADR 0072).

---

# The terminal and the side panel

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/terminal.md

A hosted session runs on a real pseudo-terminal, so the CLI behaves as in Terminal.app. A panel on the right shows what it did and changed.

## The terminal

The CLI runs on a pseudo-terminal the app owns (colours, spinners, the full TUI). Slate supplies folder, account and context and stays out of the conversation; the session is captured like any other. The CLI sees `TERM_PROGRAM=Slate`.

Claude sessions start as a **background job** (`claude --bg`, idle, no turn spent) with a view onto it, so any terminal can pick it up, even after Slate quits. Other tools start the ordinary way. Navigating away or reloading never ends a session; coming back replays what it said.

A session's tab has no doc chrome. One line above the terminal gives plan progress and the next item (`3 of 7 · Wire the totals`) and the **Terminal | Conversation** switch. A plain shell has neither.

**Conversation** is the transcript read back: each message formatted, each tool step as it runs, a prompt below.

- Enter sends at the terminal's prompt; Shift+Enter adds a line.
- `/` lists the skills the tool loads in its folder. `@` names a doc, session, memory, task, automation or report; its content goes before your words, as on [Home](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent.md#skills-and-mentions).
- Menus and permission dialogs the tool draws itself show only in **Terminal**. When the session waits on a call with no result yet, a bar above the prompt names it; **Open Terminal** switches.
- Every session opens on **Terminal**; picking Conversation holds for that session only.

**Focus mode, ⌘⇧M**, hides top bar, rail and sidebar, leaving one agent. The same chord, or *Exit focus*, restores them.

### What the terminal does

| Feature | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Theme | Follows your theme, including a retint from Settings → Appearance, while running |
| Keys ([list](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/shortcuts.md#terminal)) | ⌘F searches scrollback too; ⌘C, ⌘V, ⌘+/−/0 zoom (remembered). `Ctrl-C` still interrupts: every other app chord (⌘K, ⌘P, ⌘W) reaches the app, not the CLI. Shift+Enter adds a line. Option is Meta: ⌥←/⌥→ jump a word, ⌥⌫ removes one |
| Mouse | Selecting copies (a switch in Settings → Terminal); middle button pastes; right-click: Copy, Paste, Select all, Clear (⌥⌘K), **Remember on *doc*** |
| Scrolling up | Output keeps arriving; a **Newest output** pill returns you. Past the scrollback limit: *earlier output is no longer kept* |
| Links | A local server address (`http://localhost:5173`) opens in Slate's browser as a tab beside the session; other URLs open in your browser. A printed `slate://page/<id>` opens that doc beside the session. A printed path like `src/x.ts:42` opens that file at that line, resolved against where the session runs |
| Settings → Terminal | Font, size, line height, cursor shape and blink (only the terminal you type in blinks), copy-on-select, scrollback (5,000 lines default). Changes reach sessions on screen |
| Hidden terminals | Behind another tab or a hidden window they keep the last 1,000 lines; on return, full scrollback again |
| Remember a selection | A bar appears over the foot: **Copy**, or **Remember**, which files the selection as a memory under the session's doc. Nothing is captured automatically |

## The side panel

One panel on the right shows what the session in your active column (blue line on top) did and changed. Open by default and shared by the window; off only while that column holds no session (map, doc, plain shell).

- **⌥⌘B** or the button at the strip's end hides it. Hidden, a button at the tab row's end brings it back, showing files waiting to commit. The choice is remembered.
- Drag its left edge to resize, 280 px to 640 px (never over 60% of the window); double-click for 320 px.
- The map icon at the end of the workspace picker's row returns to the map.

| Tab | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Details** (ⓘ) | **⌥⌘I** in a session's column, or a click on the state words in its header, opens it here |
| **Changes** (⇄) | Count of files waiting to commit on its icon. What the session's checkout changed ([Review the branch](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/review.md#what-the-branch-changed)); a session started in the main checkout that edits a worktree reads that worktree's changes. **All files** opens Projects › Code for the session's project |
| **Turns** | Every prompt, newest first, with when. A click scrolls the conversation to it, or finds it in terminal scrollback. A prompt that changed files shows how many; open it for the files, each opening its change. Undo: [Rewinding a turn](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/review.md#rewinding-a-turn) |
| **The widget** (its name) | Only while a widget is made for Sessions ([Widgets](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/widgets.md)); one at most. It reads the session open beside it, and runs only while this tab is picked |

### Details

Four sections: **Environment** (tool, project, branch, folder, other agents there), **Progress** ([flow](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/flow.md) as one line such as "Check · 4 of 5", "27m in", and a bar), **Context** (fill; for a tool that states no window, past 200k tokens is read against a 1M window) and **Links**. The foot holds what the branch is for (doc, goal, documents under it), **Changed**, **Recorded** and **Given**. A session ends from its tab.

**Links** is what the branch is attached to. Shut: `PR #142 · #138`. Opened: a row per source mark (GitHub, Jira, Linear, Slate); click to open. The PR number comes from your remote with no sign-in. A PR's title, checks and reviews, and a GitHub issue, are read with your own `gh` only after you press Connect on GitHub's card; before that the card shows the number alone.

- **The pull request**: title, checks (passing, failing, running), reviewer count, open/merged/closed. The number comes from origin; the rest is read with `gh`. Without `gh`, the number alone.
- **The issue**: a branch named for a Jira or Linear key (`SLT-138-…`) shows that item from Tasks; otherwise the GitHub issue the pull request closes, or the one whose number starts the branch name (`fix/138-…`).
- **The branch's doc in Slate.**

Nothing attached: no card.

**Recorded** lists memories this session filed, and whether on its own or after Slate asked. No commits are listed (matching by time would count a concurrent agent's work). An unjudged session stays silent.

**Given** lists memories Slate gave the session, each once: **At start** (session brief) or **On your prompts**. Green dot: the session used it (replies repeated its rare words). Outline: not used. Dashed outline: not judged yet (after the session ends). Five rows per group, then a count; click one to open Memory. Nothing given: no **Given** section.

## The timeline

**Conversation** shows what the session did, in order: each prompt, what the agent said, every tool run with its target on one line (file, command, search).

- Click a step for its output. An edit opens onto the lines it changed, as in the branch review. A failed step says *failed*.
- The agent's plan (Claude Code's todo list, Codex's plan) sits on top with items done.
- Last 60 turns shown. Step output over 4,000 characters keeps its first and last 2,000.
- Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and OpenCode record each call with its output. Cursor records calls only; its timeline says so.

A [receipt](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks.md#receipts) is read from the same timeline.

---

# Tabs, columns and names

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/tabs.md

A session you open is a tab in the same strip as your docs. Columns show several at once; a name makes one easy to find.

## Several sessions at once

A session's tab shows status where a doc's icon sits, with changed lines and context fill beside the name. Files, a branch's changes and previews are tabs in the same strip. Every open tab stays mounted, so switching tears no terminal down.

While a session's tab shows, the rail stays on **Sessions**. Clicking a row opens a **temporary** tab (italic) that the next click replaces; a session you launch gets a kept tab. Tab gestures and keys: [Tabs](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/search.md#tabs).

**Closing a session's tab ends the session, after asking.** The ×, middle-click and ⌘W all ask *End qa?*, naming the tool still running.

| Choice | Does |
| --- | --- |
| **End session** | Stops the tool, closes its terminal, removes it from the rail |
| **Close tab only** | Closes the tab of a hosted terminal; the session stays on the rail as "In Slate · no window" |
| **Cancel** | Keeps the tab |

Close others, Close to the right and Close all ask once, listing every session they would end. A refused stop keeps the dialog open with the reason. A session in your own terminal is not Slate's to end: closing its view leaves it running. A session replaced in a temporary tab keeps running as **In Slate · no window**; click its row to bring the tab back. On close the neighbouring tab takes over; with none left you land on the map. Escape, or the back arrow on a transcript, returns to the map without closing anything. **Sessions** in the rail returns to the session tab you were last on.

**⌘-click any tab** to open it in its own column: two sessions, a session and its doc, an agent beside the dev server.

### Sessions side by side

**Open beside** in a row's **⋯**, or ⌘-click on the row, shows that session in a new column right after yours. The main area holds up to **4 columns**; with four, Open beside adds a tab to the column next to yours.

- **Each column has its own tabs.** Your working column has a blue line on top; click another to work there. The list marks each session on screen with its column: **left**/**right**, **middle** with three, **column 1** to **column 4** with four.
- **Drag the line between columns** to widen one; double-click a line to equalise all. Widths are saved per workspace and survive relaunch.
- **Back to one view:** **Unsplit** at the top of the last column, or ⇧⌘\\. All tabs are kept. Closing a column's last tab closes the column.

## Naming a session

**A session has one name**, shown on its tab, list row and memory doc. Right-click the tab, **Rename…**; Enter or clicking away keeps it, Escape keeps the old one. One line, up to 80 characters.

A session with no name, or one that reads as none (blank, "session", "untitled", a raw id), shows **"\<Tool> session in \<project>"** in list, tabs, map, ⌘K and the notification. A name taken from the opening prompt leaves out what the tool wrapped round it: `<pasted_content …>` around a paste, Cursor's `[Image]` and `<user_query>`, a Codex preamble; a tag you typed, like `<div>`, stays. An agent run's session is named for its run.

Renaming the tab renames the session in its own tool, so its resume list shows the new name:

| Tool | How |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code, Codex, Cursor | `/rename <name>` typed into the session |
| OpenCode | Asked through its own server |
| Gemini | Keeps no names; Slate keeps it |

- Typed only when it cannot land in your words: the last turn ended and nothing is half-typed (if you typed and cleared, Slate waits for your next Enter or Ctrl+U).
- Cursor does not report turn ends: a running Cursor session gets the name when next opened in Slate (tab dimmed until then).
- A session in your own terminal gets it when next opened in Slate.
- `/rename` typed in any of the four CLIs updates tab, row and memory doc too.

## Agents that know about each other

With two or more sessions in one project, Slate tells each the others exist, once, at the start of a turn, in the message carrying the branch brief. The rail says so under the group: *Told about 1 other session here*, or the count of the others.

Each agent gets the other's **own words**: tool, branch, state, what it was asked and its last message, plus the doc id. The branch goal is omitted (agents on one branch share it). Slate never says a session **is running**, only *last active six minutes ago*. It asks for nothing; the agents decide.

An agent can leave one note for the others or send one to a particular agent, shown once on their next turn; **a reply is another note addressed back**. No inbox, scheduler or queue. Notes that only narrate progress are refused. Slate assigns nothing.

---

# Review the branch

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/review.md

A finished worktree branch is listed as waiting for review. Open it, read every changed line, comment, then merge, keep or discard. The Changes panel commits and syncs; Turns rewinds.

## Branches waiting for review

A worktree branch whose agent has finished, with commits `main` lacks, is waiting. Slate checks every project it knows. A worktree whose session has a turn open is not waiting.

Its row, under the project beside the branch, carries grey tags: **Review · n files ›**, **behind n** when `main` moved past it, and the wait time. The row shows even when nothing runs in the project; with a session on the branch, the tag sits under that session's row. In a project with several git repositories the row names the git repository first (*editor · feat-x*).

When git does not answer in time for a worktree, its row keeps the counts last read; a branch never read yet waits for the next check. The changed files and the review say git did not answer, never that the branch changed nothing.

A branch `main` moved past cannot merge until its session rebases. With nothing running in it, it folds into a closed line at the project's end, **Behind main · n** (named for the branch it left, such as `master`), closed on each rail redraw. Branches with a session, and kept ones, stay in view.

Click the tag, or **Review & merge** in **⋯**, to open the review ([Reviewing the whole branch](#reviewing-the-whole-branch)). The header counts waiting branches (**n to review**); click it for the one waiting longest. Actions above the review:

| Action | Does |
| --- | --- |
| **Merge into main** | Fast-forwards `main` to the branch, then removes the worktree (project's **On remove** runs first) and the branch. Grey until the review loads. No merge commit, no checkout. With no folder holding `main` only the ref moves; with one, it moves too, and the merge is refused if that folder holds uncommitted changes to a file the merge changes. Also refused: uncommitted work in the worktree, an open agent turn there, new commits since the review was drawn, and git not answering while it checks how far `main` moved |
| **Ask to rebase** | Replaces Merge when `main` moved. Pastes *Rebase this branch on main and run the tests again.* at that session's prompt (no Enter), or copies it |
| **Keep** | Leaves the branch; its tag becomes a grey **Kept**, out of the count; the button reads **Unkeep**. Kept is stored on this computer only. New commits from an agent make it waiting again |
| **Discard** | Lists every commit on no other branch that will be lost, and whether uncommitted work goes too. Confirming removes worktree and branch. Uncommitted work added after the confirm opened is refused, not removed unlisted. Also refused: open agent turn, new commits since the review was drawn |

Measure is against `origin/main` and local `main` (commits either holds are not the branch's work), in the tag, review, **Branch changes** and rail counts. The tag's count omits untracked files, so the review can list more.

After Merge or Discard the next waiting branch opens, oldest first. If `main` moved but the worktree cannot be removed (On remove failed, or it is locked), the merge counts and a notification says why. The project's main branch is never merged or discarded here.

## What the branch changed

**Changed** is one session's own work. The panel's **Changes** is everything the branch holds that its base lacks, whoever wrote it: the question before a merge. It counts from where the branch left its base (later base commits never count) and **includes uncommitted work**.

Changes shows the worktree of the agent you work in: branch once on its row, then source control. With no agent selected, each worktree with a session is a one-line section (branch, lines waiting to commit); **▸** opens it. The branch name opens the whole review. A worktree's files and search are in Projects' Code.

### Source control

Changes works like VS Code's Source Control; Slate runs the git.

| Part | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Count | Files waiting to commit, on the ⇄ in the header, the panel tab and the Changes title. Unpushed commits are not counted (that is **Sync changes**) |
| Fetch | Automatic on opening Changes when the last fetch is over five minutes old. No fetch button |
| Message box | One line, grows as you type; rows are 24 px |
| Main button | Files to commit: full-width **Commit N files**, **Commit & Push** in its ▾ (the only two ways to commit). All committed: **Sync changes**, with ↑ push and ↓ pull counts; pulls, then pushes. Never pushed: **Publish branch**. Nothing to do: no button, *Nothing to commit, and up to date.* |
| Commit | Message plus every file in **Changes** except unticked ones and the agents' MCP, hook and settings files (`.mcp.json`, `.claude/settings.json`…), which can hold secrets and start unticked. Nothing is staged: a file you staged stays staged and is not committed unless ticked. ⌘↵ in the message commits |
| File row | Icon, name, folder dimmed, git letter in colour (M, A, D, R); removed files struck through. Click opens the change. On hover: **Open file**, and ↺ restores the last commit's version (checkpoint taken first; no button undoes a discard) |
| Folded below | **Outgoing · N commits**, **Incoming · N commits**, and on a feature branch **This branch vs main · N files**. Never pushed: no upstream, so commits show as **Not yet published · N commits** against the base |

**Every write waits for the agent.** While a session works in the worktree, Commit, Sync, Publish and ↺ are off (*Claude Code is working here — waits for its turn to end*). Fetch moves no file, so never waits.

**Pull is a fast-forward or nothing; push never forces.** If branch and upstream both moved, Sync reports git's message and leaves the branch alone. Merge or rebase in the terminal. The tree has no rename, new file, removal or drag.

## Reviewing the whole branch

The branch name in a worktree's section, or pointing at a rail row, opens the branch as one doc: every changed file's lines in turn, measured from the same point. The header counts files and lines added and removed.

- **File tree** (left): every changed file in its folders. A click scrolls to it and unfolds it. Viewed files are drawn quieter.
- **Fold** a file by its arrow; **Fold all** / **Unfold all** for all. At most 2,000 changed lines open: a file that would pass that starts folded, a later smaller file that fits opens, the first file always opens. Seen files keep their fold when the doc re-reads. A binary file, a file over 3,000 changed lines and a new file over 512 KB are listed with a note instead of lines.
- **Viewed** folds and counts a file (*3/12 viewed*); the agent changing it again resets it.
- **Click a line number to comment.** Notes collect across files; **Send to the session** pastes them as one message at the prompt of the session in that folder, nothing submitted. A note on a removed line says *removed line*.
- A file's name opens the whole file, against the same point.
- The doc re-reads when a session in that folder acts or you return to the window. A failed read says why and offers **Try again**.

**Revert hunk** undoes one hunk; **Revert file** restores the file as the branch found it (a file the branch created is removed). A checkpoint is taken first, so **Turns** can undo it. Refused while an agent works in that folder or if the file changed after the doc was drawn (stated at the top). Only files change: nothing staged or committed, and nothing you staged is touched. Reverts count against the branch's cited memories ([files](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/files.md#what-agents-know-about-the-file)).

## Rewinding a turn

**Every prompt takes a checkpoint first.** When a new prompt appears in a live session's transcript, before the agent acts, Slate snapshots the session's start folder: tracked and untracked files inside it, not what the project ignores. Other folders of a larger git repository are not included.

- Works for every tool whose transcript Slate reads. Branch, HEAD, staged changes and stash never move.
- Stored under `refs/slate/checkpoints/<branch>/` (hidden from `git log` and `git push`; a linked worktree adds its own `wt-<name>/` folder, so worktrees never share checkpoints); newest 100 per branch and worktree kept.
- A turn that changed nothing takes none; nor does a folder outside any git repository.

**Turns**, in the side panel, lists them newest first, each named by its prompt and holding the files that turn changed (from its checkpoint to the next; the newest to now). A file opens showing what changed since the turn began. **Restore** needs a second click, then resets the session's folder to that checkpoint and removes files created since, touching nothing outside it. It first checkpoints the present (*Before restoring: …*), so a restore can itself be restored.

---

# Files, memories and editing

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/files.md

A file a session changed opens as a tab beside it. Read it with blame and history, see the memories citing its lines, send comments to the agent, or edit it.

## Open a file beside the session

**Changed**, at the foot of **Details**, lists every file the session's own tool calls wrote, read from its transcript. Another agent in the same folder never appears on it. Each file opens as a tab beside the session (icon by kind and language); the rail stays on Sessions. A path printed in the terminal opens at that line.

**⌘P finds a file by name in every checkout.** After two letters it lists, beside matching docs, files from every tracked project and each of its worktrees, grouped by checkout and branch (`FILES · acme · main`, `FILES · acme-feat-x · feat/x`).

- Uncommitted new files count; ignored ones (`node_modules`, build output) do not. A worktree outside every tracked folder is not searched.
- ⌘K lists the same files; **⌘⇧F** searches text inside them ([Search](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/search.md)).
- Picking a file opens it in its code: side panel to Projects → Code → Files, unfolded to the file.

Code opens highlighted, numbered, ⌘F-searchable and editable. Markdown opens rendered; **Read** is one click away. Images are drawn; SVG is picture and text. A view re-reads when a session moves; an **updated** pill says the text changed under you.

**Comment on changes, then send them.** In **Show changes**, put the cursor on a line (or select several), click **Comment on line 88** (*lines 90-93*), write, press **Add** or ⌘Enter. Notes collect under the header in line order. **Send to the session** pastes them as one message (`Review comments on <file>:`, then each note with its lines) at the prompt of the session in that file's folder (the deepest, if several); nothing is submitted. With no session in Slate there, the message is copied. Comments never change the file.

## Reading a file

The tab shows the file's name. The bottom bar shows the branch, **worktree** if the file is in one, and its path from the project folder.

| Control | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| Margin marks | Branch changes: green added, blue changed, red notch for removed lines. Click opens the change |
| Cursor line | After the line: when it last changed and in which commit; click for that change |
| **Blame** (end of bar) | Every line, down the left: commit age as the strength of one blue, time and subject once per run of lines. Pointing at a line lights its commit's lines |
| **Show changes** | Appears when the file differs from where its branch began; long unchanged stretches fold. **against**: where the branch began (default) or the last commit. **Back to the file** or Esc leaves |
| **Now** pill | File history: this branch's commits, a line where the branch left its base, earlier commits. Pick one for the file at that commit, read-only, with its change (pill turns amber); **Back to now** or Esc returns |

**[** and **]** step through changes; ⌥H opens the history.

## What agents know about the file

**A margin dot marks each line a memory cites**: any memory, decision or lesson whose `source_ref` names the file with a line range (`src/export/csv.ts:10-22`) or a symbol. The dot takes its kind's colour; point at it to read the claims. Moved code is found and the dot follows. A whole-file citation has no dot. Dots show at Now only.

**The header counts them**: *4 memories · 2 told to agents who touch it*, or *No memories yet*. The second number is the lessons and decisions given to an agent reading or editing this file ([lessons](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/recall-remember.md)). Click it, or a dot (that line first), to open the card above the text.

Each memory in the card shows its claim, kind, lines (click to go), ref (`m:7f3a2b1c`), use count and tools, and a check: *Matches the code*, *The code changed since — still true?*, or *Not checked against the code* (written before fingerprints).

| Action | Does |
| --- | --- |
| **Confirm** | Still true: counted as confirmed by you; fingerprint retaken from the file as it reads now; a moved line citation is re-pointed |
| **Correct** | Edit the claim in place; the new words replace the old memory (kept in history) and cite the same lines as they read now |
| **Retire** | Stops reaching sessions, as in Memory |
| **Remember line 7** (*lines 7–9*) | Card head. Type what agents should know; saved as your own project memory citing those lines, so it gets a dot and later a *changed* mark |
| **Ask an agent about line 7** | Card head. Pastes the lines and every memory on them (with ref) at the prompt of the session in the file's folder; add your question, press Enter. No session: copied. Over 200 lines are cut. Unsaved lines in that folder are saved first |

**Your acts teach the memory.** **Merge into main** of a reviewed branch confirms each memory its sessions cited; **Revert hunk**, **Revert file** and **Discard** contradict them (once per branch per memory). The branch's sessions are those captured in that checkout on that branch; acts on `main` blame nobody. **Saving an edit on cited lines** asks once on the card, *You edited these lines: still true?* (**Confirm** = yes; **Correct** or **Retire** = no). Each act shows on the card, here and in Memory, with branch or file and date; **×** undoes it. No single act retires a memory. Everything stays in your store; only what you paste at a session leaves the computer.

## Editing

**At Now, Read is editable**, no edit mode, as in VS Code. Changed lines are amber in the margin, the tab wears a dot, the bar counts unsaved lines with **Revert** and **Save** (⌘S). The agent is a second writer, so:

- **Save waits while an agent works in that folder** (*Waiting for Claude Code*); keep typing. It works when the turn ends.
- **Every save takes a checkpoint first**, so **Turns** can undo it. The *Saved* line also offers **Undo**.
- **A disk change under unsaved lines is merged.** Different lines are all kept, and a line says so. Same lines: each place shows *Yours* beside theirs; choose **Keep yours**, **Keep theirs** or **Keep both**. If the agent writes again before you choose, the merge is made again from what you typed; **Revert** drops your side and closes the choice. Nothing is written until Save.

**The editor uses VS Code's keys** ([list](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/shortcuts.md#files-and-the-editor)). Brackets and quotes close themselves; typing one over a selection wraps it. Matches of the selected word are lit; words in the file are offered as you type (Enter or Tab takes one); the margin arrow folds a block.

**Saved as written:** line endings (LF, CRLF, even mixed), indentation (tabs, or the spaces in use; four if none) and a leading byte-order mark are kept. No autosave, format, trailing-space trim or final newline. In Diff, **Revert** puts a change back as an ordinary edit you then save.

**The agent reads the disk, not your screen:** with unsaved lines and an agent in the folder, a line says it cannot see them yet. Review comments Slate sends save your unsaved files there first, and say if one failed.

**Unsaved text survives closing the tab and quitting**, in the app's own storage (never the file), and returns through the same merge, so an unanswered choice comes back as that choice. A past commit, Diff and Blame are never editable. No rename, new file or removal.

**Where files open.** Only inside a folder Slate has business in: a group, project or branch folder, or one a live session runs in. A file a live session changed opens wherever it is (a `/tmp` scratchpad too), since its Changed list names it. Up to 1 MB of text or 8 MB of image opens. Larger, a non-image binary, a file that is not UTF-8 text (Latin-1, Windows-1255), or a file outside those folders shows a sentence saying why and **Open in Finder**, which shows the file in Finder and never opens it. The small system icon on a file opens it with the system, except a program, script or installer, which Slate shows in Finder instead.

---

# Session flow

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/flow.md

A session's flow says where it stands in its work. Slate works it out from the transcript and git each time the tab reads it; the agent reports nothing and nothing is stored.

A build skill has five steps: **Overview, Plan, Build, Check, Land**. Research has three: **Asked, Published, Decided**. The flow shows in three places, never twice in view: on the row (a bar and the step's word, `▬▬▬▬▭ Check`), in the header ("● Working · Check"), and in Details under **Progress** (the goal, the bar, each step with what lit it).

## Reading it

**The word is the step the session is in now. The bar is how far it has got.** A session that ran its tests and went back to editing reads **Build** again, while its bar stays solid through Check.

**Waiting.** When the latest step only waits, the word is **Waiting**: a `sleep` still running, a shell loop that sleeps until something is ready, or a scheduled wakeup. An idle session mid-step reads Waiting too. Its status is Idle and nothing pulses. Details says what it waits on, such as "sleeping". Waiting on you is the amber status, and its step keeps its own word.

**The bar has one colour**, the accent: done steps are solid, the current step is lighter and breathes while it works, steps ahead are the grey track. Only these change a segment:

- **Red** on Check when the session stopped on a failed check. Build is current again, with "retry 1", and the words read "Check failed" (row) or "check failed" (header). While it still works, a failed check is not red: it is back at Build, fixing it.
- **Amber** on the current step while the session waits on you.
- **Green** on every segment once the work is on the default branch.

There is no percent and no time left, because steps take very different times.

## What lights each step

- **Overview**: the session started and is reading; it counts what it read and searched before it planned or edited. A session opened by an approved brief says "read the brief".
- **Plan**: plan mode approved in Claude Code, a todo list written (Claude Code's, Codex's `update_plan`), or an approved brief opened the session. Otherwise Plan is hollow: "no plan recorded". A session that hands work out (a message to another session, a scheduled run) is at Plan and counts its "hand-offs".
- **Build**: an edit to a file in the session's own checkout. A brief in the git folder, or a file outside the checkout, is not Build, so a session that only coordinates never reads Build. After a commit it says "committed". An edit after a check or a landing moves it back to Build.
- **Check**: a test or gate run: the project's own checks (scripts, pre-push hook) or a known test runner.
- **Land**: the work is on the default branch, origin's or the local one: its last commit, or the commit its `git push` moved it to. It is read from git even after the worktree was removed. Its last evidence is the closing card the session sends, "card sent".
- **Asked**: research was asked. **Published**: it published a doc (an artifact, a Slate doc or app). **Decided**: your reply after it published.

## Where the steps come from

Each skill lists its steps in its `SKILL.md` frontmatter, for example `flow: overview plan edit check land` (`edit` shows as Build). A helper skill for one part of another's work says `flow: step`. If the checkout is older than the skill's `flow:` line, the line in the git repository's main checkout is used.

The skill is detected (within the first five tools) from a slash command you typed, a prompt opening with a skill's run phrase, a Skill call, or the agent reading its `SKILL.md` (read tool, or `cat`, `sed`, `head`, `tail` in a `skills/` folder); `grep`/`ls` naming the file and tool-added skill lists do not count. A new skill's steps replace the old. With no skill, only steps that happened show, and no bar until there is more than the overview.

## Where the goal comes from

Slate takes the first it finds:

1. **The brief** whose path the first prompt names: its title is the goal, its checklist **Done when**. A Markdown file of at most 64 KB inside the session's checkout or git folder.
2. **The issue**: the branch is `fix/<n>-…`, or the prompt says `#<n>`.
3. **The branch's Plan doc** in Slate: its goal.
4. **The first prompt**, marked "as asked". After a slash command such as `/research why…`, the goal is what follows it. The notice Claude Code writes when you stop a turn is never the goal.

---

# How status works

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/status.md

Slate reads a session's state from its transcript, who spoke last, and whether a running CLI process vouches for it. This guide gives the signals, the blind spots and how the list stays current.

## How a state is decided

- A quiet transcript with no live process is a closed conversation. It leaves the tab and is never shown as **Needs you**.
- A process vouches for a session of its tool in the folder it works in (for `codex --cd <folder>` or `cursor-agent --workspace <folder>`, that folder). A session that moved on is still found by the folder it began in. Two spellings of one folder (`/tmp`, `/private/tmp`) count as one.
- A tool that lists its own sessions decides: an unlisted session is gone, but a listing alone does not prove one alive. A job the tool reports as `done`, `stopped` or `failed` is finished. The one exception is a widget's chat: Claude Code reports its session `done` after each turn while the session waits for the next message, so there `done` ends it only once its process is gone.

A turn's last write is what touches the transcript, so a session that just asked you something reads as **Working** for a 45-second window. For Claude Code the window and the row's time come from the last turn, not the file: Claude Code keeps adding bookkeeping lines (cost, artifact monitors, queued messages) to a transcript long after a turn, and those do not count. A session that ended is still dated by its last write. Three signals shorten the window:

- **The window title of a session Slate hosts.** If it stops moving, the session becomes **Needs you** in about ten seconds. Only a title seen to move counts; of the first five CLIs only Codex animates its title.
- **The tool's own listing**, when it reports the session busy.
- **A sub-agent still writing.** This reaches a session in somebody else's terminal.

For Claude Code the transcript settles it: a record with a tool call is mid-turn, one with only text is finished. A call with no result is **Working**, with three exceptions that read **Needs you**: a question to you (`AskUserQuestion`) once the 45-second window has passed; any call quiet for more than 30 minutes, which is a prompt nobody answered (a foreground command ends at its 10-minute timeout and writes a result); and, in a session Slate hosts, a quiet call whose terminal has drawn nothing (asking you to allow it). A moving title, the tool reporting busy, or a sub-agent still writing keeps it **Working**.

## Blind spots

- A permission prompt in a session Slate neither hosts nor can ask reads as **Working** for Claude Code, for up to 30 minutes, and as idle for other tools. The exception is a Claude Code session that `claude agents --json` reports as `waiting`: it reads as **Needs you**, however fresh its transcript.
- "Waiting for permission" and "answered, waiting for your next prompt" both show as **Needs you**.
- A tool whose title does not move and whose transcript Slate cannot read this way is judged on timing alone, so a turn's end can take up to the window plus a tick to show.

## How it stays current

The server pushes changes (`GET /sessions/live/stream`; `GET /sessions/live` is the one-shot); an idle machine sends nothing. A watch re-reads only the changed transcript (150 ms coalescing), plus `HEAD` of each live checkout and OpenCode's database. Timers run only while needed: 5 s time passing (flips a session to **Needs you**), 60 s full re-walk, 15 s process list. Your own acts (stop, closed terminal, hand-back) refresh at once (`POST /sessions/live/refresh`). Branch counts refresh at most every 30 s while sessions report, and on window focus (how an outside commit shows up).

---

# Memory

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory.md

Every agent you use shares Slate's memory. It is stored as docs you can read.

- **Slate is an MCP server.** A tool that speaks MCP (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Antigravity, OpenCode, Gemini, Cline, Grok Build, Kiro, Qwen Code, Droid, Hermes Agent, Goose, Kilo Code, Auggie) starts a session with the project's memory index, searches with `recall` and saves with `remember`. One workspace, many tools.
- **A watcher fills it in.** It reads the conversation files your agents already write and stores each session as a doc. It also reads the memory folders Claude Code, Gemini CLI and Codex keep for themselves, for the folders you added as projects.
- **Memory is your docs.** Sessions, decisions and other memories live in the same local SQLite workspace as everything else. Fix a wrong doc and the next `recall` reads the correction.

## In this section

| Doc | What it covers |
| ---- | -------------- |
| [Session Capture](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/session-capture.md) | The watcher that captures AI sessions as docs. |
| [Recall & Remember](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/recall-remember.md) | Search and citing, with links to the session brief, lessons, saving and tidying. |
| [Decisions & Memories](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/decisions-and-facts.md) | Logged choices with rationale, and durable knowledge ranked for recall. |
| [Memory Graph](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/map.md) | Memories on the files they cite, coloured by use. |

The tools every AI client calls are in [Slate as an MCP Server](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server.md).

`recall` reads the workspace on this machine that owns the working folder, and never leaves the machine. What you put in a [shared workspace](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md) is readable by colleagues and their AI through a separate verb, `recall_workspaces`, which asks the cloud.

---

# Session Capture

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/session-capture.md

A **watcher** reads the conversation files your tools already write, detects completed sessions and stores each as a doc in your workspace. A tool is read only once you turn it on, in setup or **Connect → Agents**; its sessions then appear on the next pass, a few minutes at most.

Memory you kept with claude-mem or agentmemory can be brought in as well; see [Import](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/import.md).

## Which tools

* **JSONL transcripts:** Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, GitHub Copilot (one folder per session, `~/.copilot/session-state/<session id>/events.jsonl`; the folder names the session).
* **SQLite, read-only:** OpenCode (`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`), Hermes Agent, Goose, Kilo Code, Kiro. Each session is rendered into the same shape.

Every tool gets the same digest, noise filtering and branch attribution. Capture is measured on Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, Gemini, Hermes Agent and Goose. For the other eight it is unverified or not built: see [Features by Agent](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/tool-features.md).

**Profiles and other configs.** Every profile a workspace or a project names is watched, wherever its folder is (`~/work/claude-cfg` as well as `~/.claude-work`), from the moment it is saved. Tools that follow `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` / `XDG_DATA_HOME` (OpenCode, Kilo Code, Goose, Kiro on Linux) are read there. Beyond those, the watcher suggests any agent writing JSONL transcripts under your home directory: a hidden config folder, or one under `~/.config` or `~/.local/share`, with a subdirectory (`projects`, `sessions`, `chats`, `tmp`, …) whose files parse as a role-tagged transcript. Tools Slate reads from a database are never picked up this way, so a leftover transcript folder does not double their sessions.

**A cloud session brought back.** A [cloud session](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/cloud.md#cloud-sessions) runs on the vendor's computer, out of the watcher's sight. When you bring it back and send a message, Claude Code writes the whole conversation to a normal transcript under the worktree, and the watcher captures it. Nothing is written before that first message, so an unused task is not captured. It arrives as a record of what was said, not saved memories (the cloud part had no Slate hooks). A Codex cloud session brings back changes, not a conversation; applying it notes the task on its project's doc with files and lines changed.

## What a captured session looks like

Each session becomes a doc with these properties:

| Property | Meaning |
| -------- | ------- |
| `prompt` | The originating request. |
| `summary` | A one-line summary. |
| `tool` | The agent that produced the session. |
| `tokens` | Fresh input, cache writes and output, each model response counted once. |
| `sessionId` | Stable id linking the doc to its conversation. |
| `kind` | `session` when a `sessionId` is present, else `note`. Derived, never asserted. |
| `model` | The model that ran. |
| `branch` | The git branch the work happened on. |

The doc **body** is the **digest**: every real human turn (asks and course-corrections, where decisions live) plus the final outcome. A session on a git branch is filed under the branch and linked from its session log. It opens read-only (**Session — read only** under the title).

`branch` comes from the transcript when the tool records it (Claude Code does); otherwise a fresh capture uses the project's current branch. Historical back-fill stays project-level.

`remember` writes each memory's doc through the same writer; with no conversation it has no `sessionId` or tool, so its `kind` is `note`.

## Other tools' own memory

Claude Code, Gemini CLI and Codex each keep a memory folder that the others do not read. The watcher reads them, so one tool's learning reaches the rest:

| Tool | Folder | Filed under |
| ---- | ------ | ----------- |
| Claude Code | `<config>/projects/<project>/memory/*.md` | The project the session transcripts beside it name. |
| Gemini CLI | `<config>/tmp/<name>/memory/*.md` | The folder `projects.json` maps to `<name>`. |
| Codex | `<config>/memories/*.md` | Not read: Codex keeps these per user, with no folder to add. |

A project's memory file is read once its folder is inside a project or group you added (skipped until then; the next pass reads it). Each file becomes one memory written by that tool, citing the file. A changed file replaces its memory; a removed file retires it. Index files (`MEMORY.md`, Codex's summaries) are skipped. Slate never writes to these folders.

## Keeping the watcher running

Capture runs inside Slate and stops when you quit; at next launch a historical scan picks up sessions run meanwhile. The switch is **Auto-capture** in **Automations › Built-in**: off stops capture at once and stays off after restart. The capture hook and the local capture port scripts can post to follow it.

> **Note:** The watcher reads files already on your machine and writes only to your local workspace. Session capture sends nothing to the network.

## Turning capture off for one project

A project's **Memory** settings can turn **Capture sessions** off: sessions in its folder are not saved as docs by any route (watcher, hook, local port) and the agents' own memory files there are not read, and an import from another tool skips the items it files into that project too (the preview and the result count them and say why). The import is not the live path: it files by the folder or project name each item carries, reads the policy of the scope that lands in, and does not refuse a folder no project holds, whose items go to global memory under the workspace's own settings. Turning it on resumes. See [What a project keeps](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/decisions-and-facts.md#what-a-project-keeps).

## See also

* [Recall & Remember](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/recall-remember.md): how captured knowledge is read back.
* [Activity & Analytics](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/activity.md): session history and stats built on captures.
* [Privacy & Security](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security.md): what stays local.

# Recall & Remember

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/recall-remember.md

A session gets memory three ways: an index at the start, a search it runs, and a lesson on the tool call it is about. At the end it calls `remember`. This guide covers search and citing.

| Guide | Covers |
| ---- | -------------- |
| [What a session is given at the start](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/session-start-brief.md) | Brief, index, other places it is given out, filter rules. |
| [Lessons](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/lessons.md) | Memory that arrives on the tool call it is about. |
| [`remember`](remember.md) | Saving, correcting, what is refused. |
| [Tidying and measuring memory](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/tidy-and-measure.md) | Tidy proposals, declines, lessons to skills, progress logging, measuring. |

## `recall` and `get_memory`: search in two steps

```
recall({ query, cwd })
recall({ query, cwd, as_of: "2026-08-01" })
get_memory({ refs })
```

`recall` searches the project's memories and docs and returns one line per memory with ref and citation. Default 8 results, 25 at most, memories at most half, docs the rest. When the query is about the branch (it names the branch, or asks what is open or in progress) the first result is the branch brief: goal, open items, recent sessions and commits, from records labelled with the branch and from git. A memory scoring under 0.7 of the best memory's score is left out; the best one always stays. A doc matches when its text holds all the query's words; a doc found by its title alone, and captured session docs, are not returned. `kind: "pages"` searches docs only, up to 20 results.

### How results are ranked

Memories are ranked lexically and locally with BM25. No model is called and nothing is downloaded.

* Each query word counts by its rarity among your memories. Sentence (counts most), tags, citation and reason are read; words match by stem ("refused" finds "refusal"), and case, accents and punctuation do not matter ("preproduction" finds "préproduction").
* Recent memories are lifted slightly; a newer near-tie on the same subject comes first.
* From 200 memories in a workspace, a match is lifted (at most doubled) by how close its words sit to the query's in your store (latent semantic analysis, fitted in memory). It only re-orders keyword matches; a memory sharing no word is never added.
* Your acts on the code move a match, at most doubled or halved: merges and Confirms lift, reverts and discards of the code its sessions wrote lower (see [Citing](#citing-how-slate-learns-what-helped)).

**Nothing found is an answer.** From 50 memories in a project, a memory covering too little of the query is not returned, so an unanswerable question gets none. A barely passing memory is marked `weak`. `citation: changed` or `citation: gone` (file missing) means read the code before relying on it. The cited file is read in the session's checkout first, then the project's folder, so a worktree session checks against its branch.

**Second search.** `also` takes up to three other phrasings; each is searched alone and results merged. Use after a thin first search.

**The past.** `as_of` answers from what memory believed at the end of that day (UTC; no zone means UTC), including claims replaced since; each carries `until`. Memories only (a doc keeps just its current text). Use it for "what did we decide back then", not for work you are about to do. It does not count as memory offered to a session.

### `get_memory`

| Field | Meaning |
| ----- | ------- |
| `reason` | Why it was written. |
| `source_ref` | The file or commit it is about. |
| `citation` | `same`: cited code unchanged (for a line range or symbol, those lines, found again after edits above; for a bare file, the whole file). `changed`: check the code first. `gone`: file missing. `unchecked`: nothing to compare. |
| `status`, `pinned`, `written`, `cited` | Active and pinned state; when written and last cited. |
| `evidence` | Counts of **confirmed**, **cited**, **contradicted**, and by which tools. |
| `history` | What it `replaced` (newest first) and its `replaced_by` (oldest first), each with until when it was believed. |

* **Confirmed:** another tool restated it, or you confirmed in the app (the writer repeating itself is an echo, not counted). Your Merge of a branch counts.
* **Cited:** a session named its ref in its own replies.
* **Contradicted:** your Reverts and Discards of branches whose sessions cited it.
* A claim several tools reached is surer. Each tool counts once per session (once a day with no session). Slate re-reading a source it holds (re-imported tool memory file, re-derived branch reading) never counts.

A ref naming no memory comes back under `unknown`.

## Citing: how Slate learns what helped

Agents **list the refs of memories that shaped their work** in `used`, accepted by `remember` and `log_mission_progress`. Each ref counts as a use at once and records the last-cited time. Refs never go in the reply; one written there anyway is counted when the session ends.

Your signal is what you do to the code:

* A Merge in review confirms the memories the branch's sessions cited.
* A Revert or Discard contradicts them.
* Saving an edit on cited lines asks whether the memory still holds (see [What agents know about the file](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/files.md#what-agents-know-about-the-file)).

Each shows on the memory's card with an undo. A memory your acts contradicted at least twice, with no confirmation, leaves the index and stops being added to tool calls as a lesson, unless pinned; `recall` still finds it, lower. A confirmation restores it. A memory nobody cites or restates for 30 days **rests**: it leaves the index, stays stored and searchable. Pinned memories and preferences never rest.

## See also

* [Decisions & Memories](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/decisions-and-facts.md): what `recall` ranks and returns.
* [Session Capture](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/session-capture.md): the automatic side, including other tools' own memory.
* [Slate as an MCP Server](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server.md): the tool surface.
