# Adding items in Toolkit

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio/adding.md

**+** in [Toolkit](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio.md) opens a form for the open kind (**New skill** on Skills). Where an item can go to several places, cards show each place with the tools that read it; tick any number.

A line under the cards names every tool that will read it.

**New skill** also opens from a kind of work in Tasks' **Workflow** ([Tasks](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks.md#workflow)) and an automation's **Follows** ([Automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/loop.md#what-it-follows)), with name and description filled in. **Create** writes the skill, binds it to what asked, and goes back. **Cancel** writes nothing.

## Skill

Name, what it does, and where: `.slate/skills` (when the project has one: every tool, with a group and a blank doc or a copy of a skill), `.claude/skills`, `.agents/skills`. Ticking `.slate/skills` greys out the others, since `.slate/` publishes into them. In tool folders it is written once and the others link to it.

**Who starts it:** you or the AI (default), only you, or only the AI. Claude Code reads that as `disable-model-invocation: true` (only you) or `user-invocable: false` (only the AI). Other tools let both start it.

## Command, subagent, rule, output style

Each takes a name, a few fields and the tools' folders, written in each tool's shape. A **Writes** box shows each file's header before **Create**.

* **Rule:** when it applies (**Always**, **When files match** with comma-separated patterns such as `packages/server/**`, **When relevant**, **Only when mentioned**) and a description. These are Cursor's four types (`alwaysApply`, `globs`, `description` in `.mdc`). Claude Code reads only always or by files, as `paths:` in `.claude/rules/<name>.md`, so the last two choices drop `.claude/rules`. A Codex rule is a command policy: the command's first words, the decision (**Allow**, **Ask first**, **Forbid**) and why.
* **Subagent:** when to hand work to it, model (**Same as the session**, **Fast**, **Strongest**) and tools (**All**, **Read only**, or picked from read, search, edit, run commands, web):

  | Tool | Written as |
  |---|---|
  | Claude Code | `model: inherit \| haiku \| opus`, `tools:` |
  | Cursor | `model: fast`, `readonly: true` |
  | Gemini CLI | `model: flash \| pro` |
  | Codex | `model_reasoning_effort`, `sandbox_mode = "read-only"`; file `.codex/agents/<name>.toml` plus an `[agents.<name>]` table (the description) in `.codex/config.toml` |
  | OpenCode | `mode: subagent`, a `tools:` map; keeps the session's model |
* **Command:** a description and, for Claude Code only, an argument hint. Gemini's is TOML (`description`, `prompt`); Cursor's a plain file.
* **Output style:** a description and **Keep coding instructions** (on: adds to Claude Code's coding instructions; off: replaces them).

## Instructions, MCP server, hook, plugin

* **Instructions:** the instructions files the project lacks.
* **MCP server:** name, command or URL, optional `NAME=value` variables, and tools to add it to, each in its format: OpenCode's command is one list and variables are `environment`; Gemini spells HTTP `httpUrl`; Codex uses a `[mcp_servers.<name>]` table. Each ticked tool shows its file. Variables are plain text in root files often committed, so keep real keys out of shared projects.
* **Hook:** tool (Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI), an event from its list, optional matcher such as `Bash|Edit`, command, timeout (seconds for Claude Code and Cursor, milliseconds for Gemini). A Claude Code hook can go in `settings.local.json` to stay on this computer. Codex hooks are not editable yet.
* **Plugin:** name and tools to enable it for: Claude Code `enabledPlugins`, Codex `[plugins."<name>"]`, OpenCode `plugin` list. Installing stays the tool's own command.

---

# Editing, removing and Your agents

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio/editing-and-agents.md

Part of [Toolkit](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio.md). A row opens its file on its own tab.

## Contents

- [Editing](#editing)
- [A `.slate/` skill](#a-slate-skill)
- [Removing](#removing)
- [Your agents](#your-agents)

## Editing

Markdown opens drawn: header fields on top, text below, a **Preview / Markdown** switch. A rule, subagent, command or output style shows the New form's fields above its text.

* A choice saves at once; text saves when you stop typing or leave the box; the rules file on leaving the box, ⌘S, closing the editor or quitting. A save that fails as the editor closes says so in a message.
* Only the keys a field writes change; other keys, comments and order stay. A model the three choices do not name (`sonnet`) stays until you pick one.
* A header that does not parse hides the fields until fixed in the text. A config that would no longer parse is not saved, parsed as its tool does: Gemini's `settings.json` and OpenCode's `opencode.json` may carry comments; Claude Code's and Cursor's JSON may not.
* With `.slate/`, editing the rules file syncs every tool.
* A rules or skill file that is a link to somewhere outside the project (or sits in a linked folder that leads outside) is neither shown nor saved; a message names the file. A link that stays inside the project, such as `CLAUDE.md` to `AGENTS.md`, works.
* A Config files row opens the file as on disk, so MCP variables show there; an MCP server's own row never shows them.

## A `.slate/` skill

It opens in a view that gives the editor the room. One row holds name, agents that read it, and a **⋯** menu: **Rename**, **Duplicate**, **Copy to project**, **History** (restore any commit; images and other binary files come back byte for byte, and a file over 16 MB is refused rather than cut), **Remove…** (the list's row menu offers the same). File name, **Preview** / **Markdown** and saved state share one row. A skill can hold more than one file.

The agents control shows marks, **N of M** and a chevron: N agents it is published to; M installed agents that can take it, plus any non-installed agent it reaches. It opens a checklist of the 16 supported agents: **Installed** first, a folded **Not installed** group, a search box, **All installed agents** on top. An agent that cannot take a skill is greyed with the reason.

A new skill goes to every installed agent. The choice is saved as the skill's `tools` in `.slate/config.toml`, omitted when equal to the project's own `tools`. A skill published to an agent outside that list still reaches it: sync, status and check cover every agent any skill names.

Two tools with different files under one skill name show **2 copies**. Open it to compare, then **Use this copy for all agents**.

## Removing

A trash icon titled **Remove <name>** asks first (**Remove <name>?**, **Keep it**, **Remove <name>**), naming files and tools reached.

| Kind | Removing it |
|---|---|
| Skill | From every tool folder that keeps it, with links. A `.slate/` skill also leaves `.slate/skills/`; discarding it in **Projects → Code → Changes** brings it back until you commit. |
| Subagent, rule, output style, command | Its file. A Codex subagent's `[agents.<name>]` table goes too. |
| MCP server | From every tool's file; the file stays. |
| Hook | All its commands; the file stays. |
| Plugin | Named in a config: turned off. A file in `.opencode/plugins`: no trash icon. |
| Instructions, Config files | Never removed here. |

A skill behind a tool folder linked to a shared folder elsewhere is not removed there; Slate names the folder.

An **MCP server** row lists each connected tool with **Remove from** (has it) or **Add to** (does not). It says when a server will not load yet: Claude Code waits for approval of a `.mcp.json` server; Codex reads `.codex/config.toml` only in a trusted project. Slate never approves a server. **Add to** keeps an SSE server SSE; Codex and Grok Build take only streamable HTTP, so an SSE server is refused there with the reason, and Suggestions never offers that copy. When the other tool has no place for a setting (`cwd`, `timeout`, a server turned off), the copy says which ones it left out. A JSON file with comments is never rewritten. A trailing comma or a byte-order mark is not a comment: that file is edited, the mark kept and the comma dropped. Variables and headers never reach the screen. A **hook** row opens its commands, each with **Remove**. The first click arms it (**Remove?**); the second removes. Remove checks that the command is still the one shown; if a tool or an editor changed the file since, nothing is removed and the list reloads.

## Your agents

What each agent keeps for every project, in its config folder and plugins, with the project tabs and counts. Home folders have no git and nothing to publish.

* **New skill** goes in the `skills` folder of the Claude Code account this workspace runs under (`~/.claude/skills` when it names no profile), `~/.agents/skills` (Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor) or both (written once, the other folder links to it).
* Chips atop each tab pick one profile (`~/.claude-personal`, `~/.codex`) or plugin, with its count. A profile that could hold the kind has a chip even when empty.
* A row opens its file to read or edit; a config saves only if it still parses.
* **+** adds to the picked profile on every tab where its tool keeps that kind (a subagent in `~/.claude-alt/agents`, a hook in its settings file, an MCP server in `~/.codex/config.toml`). Output styles exist only in Claude Code profiles.
* A row's trash removes it from that profile after a note that every project here stops seeing it. Removed files go to the Trash. Plugin-supplied skills and commands have no trash: remove the plugin.

Only the profiles the workspace uses are read; with none named, every profile on this computer. Claude Code's user MCP servers live in `.claude.json` (it also holds sign-in data), so Toolkit never lists, opens or changes it. Add them with `claude mcp add --scope user`.

---

# Usage counts, changes and sync

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio/usage-and-sync.md

Part of [Toolkit](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio.md).

## How often each item ran

**Skills**, **Commands**, **Subagents** and **MCP servers** rows show runs in this project's sessions over 30 days: **ran 4× · 3h ago**, then **1 failed** or **1 stopped by you**. Hover for runs by tool.

| Row says | When |
|---|---|
| **not run in 30 days** | Unused. |
| **not recorded yet** | No session in the project has ended. |
| **not run since** (a date) | Fewer than 30 days recorded. |
| **not measured** | No tool that reads the item records runs. |

| Kind | Tools whose sessions show it |
| --- | --- |
| Skills | Every agent: a slash command, a `Skill` call, or a read of the skill's `SKILL.md` |
| Commands | Claude Code |
| Subagents | Claude Code: the subagent type each `Task` call names |
| MCP servers | Claude Code and Codex, which name each call `mcp__<server>__<tool>` |

When a turn ends, Slate reads the transcript and stores one row per use, with the session's receipt, in this computer's workspace database. Rereading replaces a session's rows. A worktree session counts for the main checkout. No model call.

**Failed** is a call that returned an error (Cursor and skills record no results, so never fail). **Stopped by you** is an interrupted turn while the item ran (Claude Code interrupt, Codex aborted turn); it is not counted as failed.

After you accept an **Improve**, Slate keeps the 30 days before (runs, runs stopped). Thirty days later, hover shows: **The 30 days before: ran 6×, 4 stopped by you. The 30 days after: ran 4×, 1 stopped by you.** Until then it gives the end date. Only the latest Improve per item shows.

## The changes chip

With Toolkit changes the header shows **N changes to commit in Code** (opens Changes on that project). It counts every file Toolkit writes, live. Your agents has none (not in git). Files that can hold secrets or local paths (`.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, `.claude/settings.json` and the like) are listed unticked with a note; tick one only to commit it.

## The sync pill

With `.slate/`, the toolbar pill (**In sync**, **1 agent behind**) is the only place Toolkit shows whether agents match. Click for a popover listing only agents needing sync, with what is off (e.g. **Skills changed**), **Check again** and **Sync now**.

Slate watches `.slate/`, `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` and syncs shortly after any change, from Slate, a terminal, an agent or `git pull`. Editing a skill needs no sync (tools read through links); adding, removing or renaming one, or changing `config.toml` or the rules file, does. This sync writes only inside the project, and runs only in a project you chose: one you added, one you adopted Slate in, or one on its own. A project Slate only found in a group's folder (one you cloned there, say) is synced only when you press **Sync now**, until you add it or adopt Slate in it. **Sync now** and `yarn studio sync` also write MCP servers machine-wide ([Generated adapters](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio.md#generated-adapters)). A Toolkit step (a sync, a check, a skill change) that has not finished after 2 minutes is stopped, with whatever it started, and a message names the step.

---

# Suggestions

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio/suggestions.md

[Toolkit](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio.md) suggests changes to the project's AI setup, worst first. Nothing changes until you click.

Each says what was counted and has one button, plus **Dismiss** (**Keep** for a removal).

A dismissed suggestion never returns. An accepted **Fix** or **Improve** can return after 30 days.

| Kind | When it is suggested | The button |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Fix** | An MCP server failed 3 of its last 5 calls. It shows the last error | **Open server** opens MCP servers |
| **Copy** | A skill or MCP server ran here, and a tool you used in 3 or more sessions here cannot see it | **Add for <tool>** links the skill into a folder that tool reads, or copies the server into its file |
| **New** | You gave a general-purpose subagent the same task in 3 sessions, or typed a `/command` with no skill or command behind it in 3 sessions | **Create it** opens the New form |
| **Improve** | You typed a skill's `/name` 3 times and the AI never picked it, or you stopped it 3 times | **Open it** opens the skill |
| **Remove** | It did not run in 20 or more sessions of the tools that load it, counted from when its file was made | **Remove** takes it out of every folder and file that keeps it. A subagent's or command's row names the file |

A lesson Memory proposes as a skill waits here as **New**; accepting in either place writes it once.

## How counts work

* Same 30 days as run counts, plus one row per session read, so a session that used nothing counts.
* Counted when you open Suggestions, at most hourly per project; at most 3 new suggestions a day. No model runs.
* **Remove** appears only when every tool that loads the item records that kind of use. A server Gemini CLI loads, or a subagent Cursor reads, is never called unused.
* A session that ended before the item's file existed does not count against it.
* **Copy** and **Remove** of a skill are not suggested in a project with `.slate/`, which decides each skill's tools.

## From an agent

The MCP tool `propose_setup_change` adds a fix, copy, create, improve or removal of a skill, command, subagent or MCP server, with a reason. It sits beside Slate's own, without the 3-a-day cap, and writes nothing until you accept. A **New** skill or subagent can carry its whole file.

Refused: a change already accepted or dismissed; a **New** for an existing name; a removal of a subagent or command naming any file but its own. Instructions files such as `CLAUDE.md` are never removed by a suggestion.

---

# Start using .slate

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio/start-using-slate.md

A project without `.slate/` shows **Start using .slate** at the top of its Toolkit tab. Each skill is kept once in `.slate/skills/` and published to the tools you pick. Part of [Toolkit](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio.md).

It says first what it will do:

* create `.slate/config.toml` listing the tools and every skill;
* move each skill from `.claude/skills`, `.agents/skills` and other tools' folders into `.slate/skills/` (you pick which copy stays where two differ); `studio sync` links each folder back;
* make the instructions one file:
  * neither file exists: creates `AGENTS.md`;
  * `AGENTS.md` and a `CLAUDE.md` with its own text: that text is appended to `AGENTS.md` under **From CLAUDE.md**, and `CLAUDE.md` becomes a link;
  * only `CLAUDE.md`: it stays the real file and sync makes `AGENTS.md` the link;
* leave MCP servers in each tool's file (a server listed in `.slate/` is also written to the machine-wide Claude Desktop and Cursor configs on every sync).

## What it protects

* A skill folder that links elsewhere in the project is copied; its target is untouched. A link inside a skill folder is never followed: it is skipped and listed, so a file outside the project (a key in `~/.ssh`, say) is never copied in. A skill whose folder is really outside the project is not moved at all, and a `.slate` that is a link is refused. Same for a tool's whole skills folder linked to a shared folder outside the project.
* An `AGENTS.md` that is a link (often to `CLAUDE.md`) first becomes a real file with the same text.
* Nothing is committed: **Projects → Code → Changes** shows every file; discarding one restores it.
* Before removing an untracked skill folder or `CLAUDE.md`, Slate copies it to `slate-adopt/` in the project's git folder (never committed, kept after you commit). If the list of those copies (`slate-adopt/index.json`) is damaged, adopting and discarding in Changes are refused before anything changes, until the file is restored or removed.

---

# Project environments

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio/cli-profiles.md

Each agent keeps a config directory (auth, settings, history). The one a session uses decides whose account touched the code. Slate sets the account per **workspace**, with an override on a group or on a project that stands on its own.

* A project inside a group uses its group's.
* A project that joins a group drops its own and takes the group's.
* A project that leaves a group keeps a copy of the group's, so it runs under the same account.
* A new group takes the settings of its first project that has its own.

## How it works

In **Connect → Agents** choose, per tool, the account this workspace runs it under. A group or project can override it (most never need to). There is one account per tool per group or project; what runs picks a tool and its place supplies the account. Automations, Home turns and skill steps store no login, and moving a skill re-points it.

The same switch installs Slate into that account, which gets its sessions captured. A config directory exists once per machine, so workspaces naming it share the sign-in.

## Which folders it covers

A group or project covers its own folder and the folder of every project in it. A session is judged by the **deepest** folder containing it.

## What it governs

* **Sessions started from Slate.** A session runs as the workspace its place belongs to, whichever workspace the window shows. A work project started from Personal runs on the work account.
* **Home**, when scoped to the group or project.
* **Automations and skills** that belong to it, including scheduled runs nobody watches.
* **Sessions you start in a terminal.** Slate installs hooks into each account, through the tool's own plugin or config file. They refuse the first prompt of a session running under an account the group or project does not use.

A group or project with no tools of its own (most of them) is judged by its workspace's accounts, in the terminal and in Slate. One limit: only an account that another workspace or project on this computer uses is refused. A Personal login in a work folder is stopped. A third login no workspace names still runs. A tool the workspace does not list is never refused.

A model is a starting point, not a limit. A group or project can set a default model per tool, and any model may still be used.

## What it cannot govern

* **OpenCode.** It has no documented config-directory variable, so it cannot be pinned. `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `GEMINI_CLI_HOME`, `CODEX_HOME` and `CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR` are the four that exist. OpenCode is captured, not governed, and its row says so.
* **A group or project with no folder.** A terminal session is matched by working directory.
* **A broken Slate.** Enforcement fails open: an unreadable setting or a crashed hook lets the prompt through.

## How you know it's working

A group's doc, and the doc of a standalone project, shows one line above its tabs: "3 captured sessions ran under the accounts this project assigns." When some did not: "1 of 3 captured sessions ran under an account this project does not assign." **Review** lists up to five, each with the account it ran under and the one expected. The line appears once the group or project has an environment and one captured session.

## See also

* [Agents & Model Providers](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/brains.md): the tools these environments configure.
* [Connect](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md): the screen this is set on.
* [Toolkit](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio.md): the wider "configure once, use everywhere" story.

---

# Home

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent.md

Home is the doc Slate opens on. It shows what needs you, and it has an agent built in that reads and writes your workspace (nested docs, memory, activity) and reaches any MCP tools you connect. The agent runs on whichever coding agent you point it at.

## Contents

- [What Home shows](#what-home-shows)
- [The Set up Slate card](#the-set-up-slate-card)
- [Resuming a past session](#resuming-a-past-session)
- [Scope, and dropping a file in](#scope-and-dropping-a-file-in)
- [Skills and mentions](#skills-and-mentions)
- [In this section](#in-this-section)

## What Home shows

Home shows **one thing that needs you at a time**. The headline counts the cards on the deck, the same total as the pager under it ("Seven things wait for you."). When finished sessions are among them, the line under it splits the count ("Six to answer, one finished — look when you can."). When only finished sessions wait, it says "One session finished."

Each card has a badge for its kind; the deck is ordered by it, blocking first. The dot before the badge is amber when the card blocks on you now and grey when it can wait.

| Order | Badge | What it is | What the card offers |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Needs permission** (amber) | The agent wants to run a tool call and waits for your yes | The command in a code box, **Open to allow**, **Later** |
| 2 | **Asks you** (amber) | The session's last turn ends on a question | If Slate runs the session: a **Reply** box, **Send**, **Open**, **Later**. For a terminal Slate does not own: **Open session**, **Later**, and a line saying the answer is typed there |
| 3 | **Automation asks** (amber) | A call an automation's rules held ([Automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/loop.md#when-it-asks-first)) | The call, **Yes, do it**, **No** with an optional reason, **Open the thread**, **Later** |
| 4 | **Review asked** or **Task** (grey) | A task in Tasks that needs you | **Open in Tasks**, **Open in {app}** (such as GitHub), **Later** |
| 5 | **Reminder** (amber) | A reminder you set on a task | **Open in Tasks**, **Done**, **Later** |
| 6 | **Finished** (grey) | The session's turn is a report: nothing blocks | **Open session**, **Mark seen**, **Later** |

The card title is one plain line: the question the reply ends on, or its first sentence. Below it the reply shows as markdown, about four lines; **Read the whole reply** opens the session. Only Claude Code's transcripts show a pending tool call today, so other tools are **Asks you** or **Finished**, never **Needs permission**.

- **Send** on an **Asks you** card removes it and you stay on Home. For agents not proved to send on Enter, the answer is typed into the prompt and not sent, and the card says *Typed — press Enter in the session to send it.*
- **Later** sets a card aside until you restart Slate; a session set aside returns when it says something new. **Mark seen** does the same for a finished session.
- Move between cards with the arrows, the dots, ← and →, a sideways swipe or a drag. A line under the dots says where you are ("4 of 7 · Automation asks").
- The deck's card is compact at every window size: a title line, then its buttons. A card behind the front one takes no height.
- Working sessions that need nothing show as pills that open the session, always in one row; more slide sideways, with a fade on the side that hides some. Only the open workspace's sessions are listed; one pill counts other workspaces and links to [Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md).
- Every time on Home, in Sessions and in Tasks says **just now** under a minute. A card that waits on you says how long: *waiting 2 min*, *waiting 3 hours*, *waiting 2 days*.
- **A short window keeps the composer in view.** Home sizes itself to the window's height. Below about 900 px the mark hides, and the headline and the widgets get smaller. Below about 560 px the mark, date and subline hide, the widgets shrink further, the pager keeps only its dots, and the running pill under the deck hides (Sessions still shows it). While a card waits, the composer stays at the foot and only the part above it scrolls. The next card peeks in at the side and fades out, and the window edge never cuts it.
- With nothing waiting, the headline says **All clear.** and the composer moves to the middle. Past sessions are in Sessions, under **All past sessions**.
- If Home could not read what waits (tasks, agent runs or held calls), it says so under the headline, with **Try again**. With no card to show, the headline says *Could not check what waits for you.*, never **All clear.**
- A chat opens over Home. **Home** (top left of the chat) returns to Home and keeps the chat; **Back to the chat** returns. A streaming reply does not pull you back; sending a message does.
- **⌘J** opens the **Ask AI** panel beside a doc; elsewhere it shows *The AI panel opens on a doc. Open a doc first.* **Write with AI** in the slash menu drafts text straight into the doc. Waiting setup changes are in [Toolkit › Suggestions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio.md#suggestions).
- Your [widgets](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/widgets.md) for Home sit in the gaps between Home's parts (under the greeting, above or below the box), each at the size its setup in Widgets chose (a third, a half or the whole width). They read what Home shows (running AI sessions, for the project picked here). A new one appears below the box once built. Home has no control that adds or moves a widget: open it in Widgets and click a line on its preview.

For approvals, autonomy and Stop see [Approvals, Stop and Agent Differences](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/approvals.md).

## The Set up Slate card

In a workspace with no agent set, Home is a doc: *{workspace} is ready for an agent*. One card shows the 16 agents as small tiles, four to a row, and what connecting one unlocks (Ask here, Memory, Activity, Automations, Widgets), with **Open Connect** and what works without AI: Tasks, Projects and Artifacts. See [Connect](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md#agents).

Once a tool is set, Home starts with a **Set up Slate** card of three steps, each with one button:

| Step | Button | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| **Connect an agent** | **Connect an agent** (opens Connect → Agents) | This workspace has an agent set |
| **Start a session** | **New session** (runs your tool in a folder) | A session has been captured |
| **See your first memory** | **Open Memory** | A memory is saved |

Ticks come from what is in the workspace, so a step done elsewhere ticks itself. The first step names no agent until one is connected; then it names only the connected ones. The first open step has the main button; the header counts progress ("1 of 3 done"). The card goes when all three are done or on **Skip setup**, and does not return in that workspace (other workspaces are unaffected). A line under it reads *A workspace holds your projects. A project is a folder you open.* and names your workspace.

## Resuming a past session

1. Open [Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md) and choose **All past sessions**.
2. Press **Resume** on the row (a click on the row opens its record instead).
3. Home opens with that session's transcript loaded, and the agent picks the thread back up.

The chat starts with what you first asked and, under **Summary**, what Slate saved of the session (Slate's record, not a new tool reply).

## Scope, and dropping a file in

The composer's **Scope** control (folder icon) lists your **projects** (not workspaces; the rail's switcher picks those), resting at **All projects**. The tool's searches, the memories Home hands it (**What it knows**), the tool picker and the widgets follow it. Scope is not saved.

**Drag a file onto the composer** to attach it, as a paste does. An image shows as a thumbnail; on send Slate saves it in an `attachments` folder in its app-data folder and gives the tool the path. An image unused for 30 days is removed. A text or code file is inlined under its name, cut at 20,000 characters. The same limits hold for a drop, a paste and the paperclip: an image up to 8 MB, a text file up to 1 MB. A larger file, a binary (a PDF, a zip) or a file that is not UTF-8 text is not attached, and a message names it; the other files still attach. This also works in a session's **Conversation** prompt. Dropping a file elsewhere in the app imports a folder as docs.

## Skills and mentions

**`/`** at the start of the composer lists the **skills the agent will load** here: the project's own skills from the folders that tool reads, its commands, and the personal and plugin skills of the account the project runs it as. It is read from disk, so it is there before your first message.

- Matches name first, then description; an exact name comes first.
- A pick waits as a chip; on send, the tool is told to read that skill's file and follow it.
- After Claude Code has answered, its reported commands are listed after the skills; picking one types `/name ` into the box. Only Claude Code reports commands.

**`@`** anywhere names something in the workspace: a **doc**, **session**, **memory**, **task**, **automation** or **report**. The menu shows up to five of each kind whose name holds what you typed, most recent first. A pick is a chip; on send its content goes before your message as plain text:

| Kind | Sent |
| --- | --- |
| Doc | Its text, cut at 8,000 characters and marked when cut |
| Session | Tool, folder, branch, id |
| Memory | Claim with reasoning and source |
| Task | State and link |
| Automation | Its steps |
| Report | Its text |

If Slate cannot read one, the conversation says so instead of sending without it. `/` and `@` also work in a session's **Conversation** prompt and in **Run with AI**'s *What to type in*.

## In this section

| Doc | What it covers |
| --- | --- |
| [Approvals, Stop and Agent Differences](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/approvals.md) | The approval card, autonomy, plans and questions, Stop, and what differs by agent. |
| [Agents & Model Providers](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/brains.md) | The 16 agents, each a thin driver over a CLI you already have, so no API key. |
| [Features by Agent](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/tool-features.md) | Which tool has which feature, and why a gap is there. |
| [Curated MCP Commands](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/mcp-commands.md) | How Home routes a request on a light model, and the two halves of memory. |
| [Connected MCP Tools](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/connected-tools.md) | Reaching the MCP servers your tool's CLI declares. |

See also: [Slate as an MCP Server](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server.md), [Memory](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory.md), [Toolkit](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio.md).

# Approvals, Stop and Agent Differences

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/approvals.md

Home's agent runs on a real CLI and asks before it edits a file or runs a command. This guide covers the approval card, autonomy, plans, questions, Stop, and what differs by agent.

## Contents

- [The approval card](#the-approval-card)
- [Autonomy](#autonomy)
- [A plan or a question](#a-plan-or-a-question)
- [Stop](#stop)
- [What Home shows about the agent](#what-home-shows-about-the-agent)
- [What differs by agent](#what-differs-by-agent)

## The approval card

The agent can read files, edit files and run shell commands in the project you scoped the turn to. It **asks first**, in the amber card used for workspace writes. The card shows the tool's call and the full argument (the whole shell command), with three answers:

| Answer | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| **Approve** | Runs this one call; nothing is remembered |
| **Always allow** | Runs it and keeps a rule so the next identical call is not asked. Claude Code: saved to the project's `.claude/settings.local.json` (the card prints the exact rule first). Codex: remembered for the session. Cursor, OpenCode: kept in their own allowlist |
| **Skip** | Refuses and tells the agent why, so the reply says the call was declined |

- A box beside **Skip** takes an optional reason, which can become a memory proposal.
- **Always allow** appears only when the CLI offered a rule. A question card has no **Approve**: each answer is a button.
- Several calls at once queue and show one at a time. An answer belongs to its own card, so a double click cannot approve the next one unseen.
- Slate's own tools (reading docs, writing memory) skip the card. Everything else asks, including MCP servers you connected.
- Background work (an automation's run) shows no card while running. Its rules decide, and a call that changes something is held and appears on Home as an **Automation asks** card after the run ([Automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/loop.md#when-it-asks-first)).

## Autonomy

The autonomy pill sets how much skips the card. The ⌘J panel and Home's composer share it.

| Setting | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| **Ask first** | Asks before every file edit and command |
| **Auto-edit** | Applies file edits; asks before a shell command |
| **Full auto** | Asks about nothing |

A click moves one step; entering Full auto needs a second click. **New chat** resets to Ask first. A change applies to the current conversation with no restart, so no tool signs in again. **Create an automation** and **Run an automation** ignore the pill and always ask, because they spend money. Other Slate writes (a new doc) run without asking under Auto-edit and Full auto.

## A plan or a question

- **Plan.** The tool writes the whole plan and shows it before touching anything. Approve starts it; Skip keeps planning.
- **Question.** When the tool needs a decision, each offered answer is a button; picking one answers.

The CLI hides its plan and question tools from hosts that cannot answer them; Slate can.

## Stop

**Stop** ends the turn and keeps the agent running with its connections, so your next message needs no new sign-ins. A message sent right after waits up to 10 seconds for the stopped turn to let go, then starts a fresh one. A tool that runs one process per message has it ended ([fallback](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/brains.md#transport)). Stop also declines every waiting card; an interrupted step reads **Stopped.**

Home has one warm agent. A chat started with **Chat** in Sessions has its own, in its own folder; Stop, mode and model there reach only that tool, and closing its tab ends it ([A chat instead of a terminal](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/start.md#a-chat-instead-of-a-terminal)).

## What Home shows about the agent

- The reply streams as written.
- A **context meter** by the token count shows how full the tool's window is (share and bar), using the CLI's numbers (matches `/context`). It refreshes each turn, darkens from 75%, and shows tokens only if the size is unknown.
- The top bar's **tools** chip shows *connecting agents…* with a spinner during the first turn, then how many MCP servers the tool reported (names on hover, *· 1 failed* in amber for any that did not connect).
- A **hook that blocks a turn** is reported in the chat with its name and reason. Only failing hooks are reported.
- **`/`** lists skills and commands ([Skills and mentions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent.md#skills-and-mentions)).

## What differs by agent

**Claude Code and Codex** speak their own protocols. **Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini, GitHub Copilot and the ten newest** (Antigravity, Cline, Grok Build, Kiro, Qwen Code, Droid, Hermes Agent, Goose, Kilo Code, Auggie) speak the Agent Client Protocol. Approval cards work on Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode. **For the ten newest, Home, Stop, the model picker and the approval card are unverified**: only their ACP handshake was checked. Full table: [Features by Agent](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/tool-features.md).

| | Claude Code | Codex |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Asks before a command, file change or tool | yes | yes |
| Question with options as buttons | yes | yes |
| Plan to approve | yes | — |
| Always allow | saves a project rule | remembers for the session |
| Stop ends the turn, not the tool | yes | yes |
| Context meter, model picker, streaming | yes | yes |
| Own slash commands in `/` after the first reply | yes | — (in its terminal UI, not the protocol) |

Codex also asks before **escalating out of its sandbox** and passes on questions from **its own connected MCP servers**. Claude has neither.

**Cursor and OpenCode** show the card (**Approve**, **Always allow**, **Skip**) but no plan or question card. Always allow goes in the tool's own allowlist. Slate answers by the pill:

| Pill | Cursor (asks for anything outside your Cursor allowlist) | OpenCode (Slate starts it with shell and edits set to ask) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ask first | Card for each call | Card for each call |
| Auto-edit | Allows edits, reads, searches; card for the rest | Same |
| Full auto | Allows all | Same |

If OpenCode does not answer the protocol, Slate runs one process per message with no card, so an ask is a refusal: Ask first refuses shell commands and edits, Auto-edit refuses shell commands, Full auto leaves OpenCode's default.

**Gemini** is *unverified* for asking, because Gemini CLI stops before any turn on a consumer Google account ([Features by Agent](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/tool-features.md)). Its autonomy pill is disabled, with the tooltip *Slate cannot yet ask Gemini for permission, so it runs pre-approved whatever this says*.

The 10-minute limit on a quiet agent gets one more window while an approval waits on you. An unanswered card still ends; Stop always works.

---

# Tasks

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks.md

**Tasks** lists what you owe: issues assigned to you, pull requests to review, messages to answer, and lines you write. Any can carry a reminder. It sits in the rail after Home and belongs to the workspace the switcher picked.

## Today's meetings

If a connected work gateway carries a calendar (Google Calendar or Outlook), a **Today** row sits above the Overview:

- **Next meeting**: "in 25 min", "in 8h 12m" or "now", its name, **Join** if it has a video link.
- **Day line**: 08 to 19 (wider if needed), one mark per meeting. Dashed = unanswered or maybe. Red tick = now.
- **Sums**: meetings, all-day events, free time left (gaps of 45 minutes or more).

Point at a meeting for its card: title, times, length, your answer, **Join**, **Open in** your calendar. Click to keep it open. A title naming a task key ("Sync on PROJ-123") or a pull request number ("Review #412", if only one task has it) lists that task under **About**.

Declined and cancelled meetings are left out; none counts. The calendar is read with each Tasks sync through the Jira/Slack/Gmail gateway, at no token cost. If it needs sign-in the row shows **Sign in** (checks every few seconds, gives up after three minutes). No calendar, no row.

## The four sections

| Section | Holds | Tools |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **To-dos** | Lines you wrote | none |
| **Issues** | Issues and tasks assigned to you; unassigned issues on your projects | Jira, Linear, GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, Asana, ClickUp, monday.com, Notion, Trello, Shortcut, YouTrack, Basecamp, Todoist, Plane |
| **Reviews** | Reviews asked of you, pull requests assigned to you, your open ones, unclaimed ones on your projects | GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, Gitea, Gerrit |
| **Messages** | Chat and email awaiting your answer | Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord, Google Chat, Zoom, Mattermost, Zulip, Rocket.Chat, Gmail, Outlook |

**Reviews** groups by pull request state:

1. **To review**: asked of you or assigned to you. Only a review asked of you counts as needing you.
2. **Changes asked**: yours; a reviewer asked for changes.
3. **Checks failing**: yours.
4. **Ready to merge**: yours; checks pass, no conflicts, no review owed (approved, or none required). If the review state was never read: **No review asked for**, with no merge run.
5. **Checks running**: yours.
6. **Waiting on review**: yours. Also where a pull request of unknown state goes (only GitHub is read for it today).
7. **On your projects**: nobody's, on projects your account owns.

**Issues** groups by each tool's status names; Jira "In Progress" and ClickUp "in progress" share a group. Each task shows its tool's logo (initials tile for Outlook and Azure DevOps).

Sources: GitHub, apps connected in Connect → **Integrations**, and Jira/Slack/Gmail through an agent gateway; others are learned ([Teach Slate](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/learning.md#teach-slate)). Unreadable apps say **Not read yet**. See [Where tasks come from](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/sources.md).

## To-dos

1. Click **+** in the side panel's title row.
2. Type the line ("call the accountant"), press Enter. The box stays open for more lines. Set a reminder first if needed.
3. The list shows To-dos with the new line selected.

Nothing you write lands in Issues, Reviews or Messages, and no tool writes to To-dos. They never sync and never vanish. On the Overview their source is **Slate**.

Groups by **when**: Overdue, Today, Tomorrow, This week, Later, No time. **Done today** sits at the bottom, struck through, until tomorrow.

- **Tick the box** to finish; again to undo.
- **Double-click the title** to rename (a ticket's title belongs to its tool).
- **Run with AI…**: **Feature** (default), **Bug**, **Investigate only**. With no ticket the agent reads the title and your note and ships a pull request with no ticket update.

## Reminders

**Remind me…** (beside **Done** on a to-do; in **⋯** on a tool's task) offers in an hour, this evening, tomorrow morning, next week, or a picked time. When due, a notification rings with the title and the task moves to **Needs you** until done. A new time snoozes; **Clear the reminder** removes it.

- Slate must be running. A reminder due while it was shut rings once on next open and says its time. One due while the computer slept rings within five minutes of waking.
- **Reminders** in [Automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations.md) turns it off; set times stay.

Agents set one with **remind\_me** ([MCP tools](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tools.md)); for repeats use an [automation](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/loop.md).

## The side panel

Opens on **Overview**; the title row has **+**. Under it:

- **Overview**: its number is what needs you now (a review asked of you, a direct message, a reminder that rang).
- **To-dos**, **Issues**, **Reviews**, **Messages**: each with a count (only tools that answered). Dimmed when nothing waits.
- **Agent runs**: runs started from Tasks in the last 14 days with their session's receipt; the number is unreviewed flagged receipts. A session you ran yourself is not here (see **Details** in [Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md)).

Drag the line between list and item to widen the list (320 to 640 px; item keeps 420 px minimum); double-click resets. Above the list: one chip per tool with items, most first, extras fold into **+N**; no row with one tool.

**Sync** reads your tools now. Its label says when the last read finished, which tool failed, or which needs sign-in ("Jira needs sign-in"). Greyed while reading.

Every tool is read to the end, up to 1,000 items from one tool. When a tool holds more, or its rate limit stops the read, the list says so above the rows: "1,000 of 3,400 from GitHub. Narrow by project or label, or open the full list in GitHub." with **Open the full list in {tool}**. A tool that does not say its total reads "The first 1,000 from {tool}". A group draws its first hundred rows, then **Show 100 more of N**. A group with items from more than one tool or project is split under a heading for each ("GitHub · acme/api", with its count), the ones holding something of yours first, then by name, and each heading folds with a click; a fold is remembered on this Mac. In a group of more than a hundred, only the headings holding something of yours, and the first by name, start open. The hundred rows are shared by a group's open headings, and **Show 100 more** keeps its count when you fold. A fold never hides the item you have open. The note stays until a whole read replaces it, through a "nothing changed" sync and through a failed one. When GitHub says to slow down, the last list stays as it was, what that read did take is kept, the next sync goes on from where it stopped, and the sync line does not report an outage. When GitHub needed more than one read a search for your items, the next syncs for 30 minutes ask only for what changed (with one minute of overlap); an item that left the list is noticed by the full read after that, or at the end of a full read that took several syncs, which keeps every item it saw along the way. It is never noticed by a read that stopped early or asked only for changes. Items that only now came into reach (the first 1,000 after an upgrade) are not "arrived": an automation on a new task starts only for items updated after the previous read.

A chip filters to one tool; **⋯** beside the chips:

- **Disconnect** (apps connected from Slate): remove the sign-in.
- **Hide from Tasks** (any app): removes its count and tasks, leaves the tool alone. Hidden integrations are listed on Connect → Integrations, each with **Show**.
- An unreachable tool keeps its old tasks, last, under **Can't reach GitHub**, outside the count.

A tool your agents already reach is offered above the list as **Use from your agents**. On a first day the Overview gives way to the six most used apps, as rows of Connect's own list, and **See all {count} integrations in Connect →**; the panel says nothing more then, and the sync line shows once something is connected or found.

**Sign in** opens the tool's sign-in page. Tasks shows "Waiting for you to sign in…", checks every 4 seconds, then **Signed in to Jira**; after 3 minutes it asks you to retry. For GitHub it says to run `gh auth login`. A sign-in link from Teach Slate opens directly.

## The Overview

Left to right: **your tools** (logo and name, a number for what waits, **Sign in** if needed, **You wrote** feeding To-dos, **Connect an integration** last), **the four kinds of work** (dots with counts or "nothing waiting"), **Slate** (the shared memory, with how much needs you) and **the agents at work** (past two, the second becomes a count). Click any logo, dot or name to open its list.

## A task

Click a row to open it beside the list:

- Origin ("GitHub assigned this to you"), comment count, project.
- **Slate remembers**: up to three memories naming the task by key (`ECL-18747`) or pull request number (`#140`). None for To-dos and Messages.
- **Run with AI…** leads (a to-do also keeps **Done**). **⋯**: **Open in GitHub** (when the tool gave a link), **Remind me…**, **Hide from Tasks** (this list only; **Undo**; the task returns if the tool reports a newer change). Each section has a folded **Hidden (N)** line with **Unhide**.
- **Run button**: shows Slate's mark, the skill (`fix-bug`) and the agent (Claude Code). Its chevron picks the agent for this run only, and the skill, which changes the project's rule for that kind. Once started it says **Running** and opens the run. With nothing to run yet (your pull request waits on review or checks), one line says so.
- It says **Run it** or **Open a session**; a blocked start (a folder that is not a git repository) is explained in the footer. See [the start dialog](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/agent-runs.md#the-start-dialog).

Description and comments are read in the tool; terminal and changes are in the task's session ([Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md)).

## Agent runs (beta)

A run takes a task through Read it, Plan, Build, Check, Draft, Ship with two stops for your approval, in a visible session. On as **agent runs (beta)** in [Automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations.md); off, the card offers only **Just open a session**. Six kinds each run **one skill per project**, changed from the run button's menu, the start dialog or the folded **Workflow** box atop Issues and Reviews. See [Agent runs](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/agent-runs.md) and [Workflow](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/workflow.md).

### Workflow

The kinds (**Bug**, **Feature**, **Someone else's PR**, **My PR**, **My PR, checks failing**, **My PR, ready to merge**) and their skills: [Workflow](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/workflow.md).

## Receipts

A receipt is what an AI session ran, checked against what it said, written from the transcript at turn end. See [Receipts](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/receipts.md).

See also: [Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md), [Connect](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md), [Privacy & Security](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security.md).

# Where tasks come from

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/sources.md

A normal read uses no agent and no tokens. This guide lists the source for each tool, how often it is read, and how Messages is limited to the workspace.

## GitHub

Read through the **GitHub CLI** (`gh`) once you press **Connect** on its card in Connect → Integrations or setup. A signed-in `gh` alone reads nothing.

- Several `gh` accounts: Slate asks `gh` who is signed in, in every `gh` config folder, including several logins in one folder (`gh auth login` twice, `gh auth switch`). Each workspace reads as the account owning its git repositories (for an organisation's, the one that can see them). A workspace no account reaches shows no GitHub; switching accounts drops the old one's tasks.
- A remote cloned through an SSH host alias (`git@github.com-work:acme/app`) counts as GitHub: the alias is resolved with `ssh -G`.
- Every AI session started in a project runs `gh` as the sign-in reaching that project. An agent run shows GitHub connected only when one of your sign-ins reaches the project.
- A write made in your name (an app's card) runs as exactly the login shown, with that login's token for that one call. If `gh` cannot confirm that login, the write is refused and asks you to sign in.
- Read on opening Tasks, and on returning to the window after a minute. Each read first asks GitHub whether anything changed; a full read follows a change, a last read over ten minutes old, or **Sync**.
- Six lists: reviews asked of you, pull requests assigned to you, your open pull requests, issues assigned to you, and on git repositories your account owns, pull requests nobody reviewed or took (**On your projects**) and unassigned issues. A task on several lists shows once.
- One more read gets your open pull requests' state (review decision, checks, can merge). If it fails they show under **Waiting on review**.
- No `gh`: **Unavailable**. Signed out, or no sign-in sees the workspace's git repositories: **Sign in** (`gh auth login`). A workspace whose docs name no GitHub git repository shows no GitHub row.

## When a source is down, or goes away

An outage, a rate limit or a settings file an agent is rewriting never removes tasks: the row says **Unavailable** and the last tasks stay until the next good read. This holds for every source above: GitHub (a rate limit is a skipped read, never "cannot see"; a `gh` sign-in that cannot be told is kept as it was, and a "cannot see" answer is asked again after ten minutes) and the tools read through your agents (an empty, half-written or just-removed settings file is not "no tool").

When a source really goes away (you disconnect GitHub, switch `gh` accounts, or remove an app's token connection), its tasks leave the list. Items you **dismissed** or set a **reminder** on are not forgotten: they stay hidden, with their title and link erased, and come back with the same dismissal or reminder if the source returns. Reconnecting a source is a first import, so it starts no automation for the tasks it brings back.

## Apps connected from Slate

GitLab, Jira, Linear, ClickUp, monday.com, Notion, Trello, Plane, Mattermost, Shortcut, Basecamp, Todoist, or any server added by address are read through the app's official server, signed in as Slate. Once signed in, Slate reads first and an agent's server for that app is left alone; until then that server keeps reading, so a personal Jira never stops a company Jira syncing. Other trackers are [learned](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/learning.md#tools-slate-learns-on-its-own); a chat app such as Mattermost by [Teach Slate](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/learning.md#teach-slate).

**Read card.** Where a server cannot list what is assigned to you (monday.com), the app-list entry has a **read card**: one read-only call and how to keep your unfinished items. monday.com: your 25 most recently used boards, 100 items each. A changed answer shape is flagged on the row.

## Jira, Slack and Gmail through your agents

Read through your agents' MCP servers after you press **Use from your agents** once. Slate scans the settings of Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Codex and OpenCode, only for accounts **this workspace** runs under, and keeps:

- **A tool gateway** carrying many tools (one declared several times, or as local server and web address, counts once).
- **A server for one integration** (`linear`, `atlassian`), skipped if a gateway or Slate already reads that tool.

Either is a **local server** (started and kept running; turning integrations off stops it unless another workspace still has them on) or a **web address** (streamable HTTP or SSE). A web address uses the key in its settings; with none, **Sign in** opens the server's sign-in page and Slate signs in as itself, one per workspace, kept on this machine. Your agent's sign-in is never read.

Only [read-only tools](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/learning.md#teach-slate) are called. If a gateway is unreachable (expired sign-in) its tools say **Unavailable** or **Sign in** and last tasks stay until the next good read. Tasks from a tool no gateway reads any more are removed.

| Tool | Read |
| --- | --- |
| Jira | Issues assigned to you, not done, by Jira status |
| Slack | Direct messages and mentions from the last 7 days you have not answered |
| Gmail | Unread emails from the last 7 days, up to 30, by subject and sender; at most 15 new opened per read, the rest later. A row opens in the Google account the gateway reads; when no email names that account, the row says so and opens your first signed-in account. Outlook is not read this way |

## Apps read with a pasted token

Six apps have no usable sign-in; connect with a token (Connect → **Integrations**). Read-only web API, finished items left out:

| App | Read |
| --- | --- |
| **Bitbucket Cloud** | Open pull requests where you review and have not approved or asked for changes. No such list exists, so each git repository you are a member of is asked, up to 200 |
| **Gitea**, **Forgejo** | Open pull requests whose review was asked of you |
| **Gerrit** | Open changes whose attention set holds you. Someone else's: a review; your own back in your attention: yours to act on |
| **YouTrack** | Unresolved issues assigned to you, with state and priority |
| **Zulip** | Unread direct messages and mentions, one row per conversation |
| **Rocket.Chat** | Rooms with unread direct messages or mentions, one row per room |

A read that worked is not repeated for three minutes unless **Sync**. Two servers of one app are read together; one failing never hides the other's tasks.

## Messages stay in this workspace

A message stays when it names something the workspace works on: a group or project in your tree (`thunderbolt`, `acme/api`), or a project key, name or git remote from your Issues and Reviews tasks.

- **Gmail**: filtered in its own search, on the subject only.
- **Slack**: checked on its text as read (a link or channel name alone does not count; text not kept). Also stays if from someone in your Issues or Reviews tasks.
- **Learned tools, tools Claude reads for you, Zulip and Rocket.Chat via token**: checked on title, channel and sender.

A workspace with no groups, projects, Issues or Reviews shows everything.

---

# How Slate learns an app

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/learning.md

Slate can read some apps it was not built for. This guide covers the automatic try, Teach Slate, the safety check on every call, and what Tasks keeps on disk.

## Tools Slate learns on its own

During a sync, a tracker app with no reader gets one try a day per workspace. No model.

| Step | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Pick | Read-only tools whose names say tasks, issues, items, tickets, cards or stories and that are yours (`get_my_issues`) or take an assignee. Writers and tools needing unknown input are never tried |
| Identify | Your id from the app's "who am I" tool (`atlassianUserInfo`, Todoist `user-info`, Shortcut `users-get-current`). Apps with none (ClickUp) are asked to resolve "me" |
| Call | The best tools, at most 6 calls: your id as assignee, then `me` |
| Keep | The first read returning a list with a title and a status for at least one task (a done flag like `completed: true` counts). A plain list beats one narrowed to a slice, such as by date |

Then the tool is read like Jira, free, with your id as a placeholder. Finished items are left out: ones the app marks finished (`completed: true`, a completion date, a status class like Linear's `completed`), and statuses that say so in English or in the team's language (Done, Erledigt, Terminé, 完了). A negated status ("Nicht erledigt", 未完成) or a "ready for" one ("Listo para QA") stays open, as does any status Slate cannot read. Priority names are read in any case, with Urgent and P0 to P3.

- An app that reads fine but has nothing yours yet (new account): no read is kept; retried next day.
- **Sync**, connecting or disconnecting an app: learns again at once.
- A kept tool renamed or removed by the app: read removed, learned again in the same sync.
- A gateway tool that read fine in the last 3 minutes is not asked again until **Sync**; one awaiting sign-in is always asked.

## Teach Slate

A connected app in Connect → Integrations with no reader shows **Not read yet** and a button to teach it; opening the screen starts nothing. When you press it, its tile says **Learning how to read your tasks in GitLab…** for about a minute; apps go one at a time. Claude (Sonnet) is asked about that app through Slate's `connected_tools` and `read_connected`, with no shell or web. Slate tries the answer and keeps it only if it returned a list; afterwards no agent and no tokens. If nothing is found: **Could not find your tasks in Notion.** with **Try again**, and Slate never retries by itself; each lesson starts only when you press the button. A read kept later clears it.

**Write-word check.** Every tool is checked when picked, when kept and on every read. Refused: any tool with a write word in its name (send, create, update, remove, add, move, post, reply, comment, merge, close, assign, set, mark, upload, write and about fifty more), or belonging to another app. Filter words pass: `get_assigned_issues` yes, `assign_issue` no.

**Tools only your Claude account reaches** (a claude.ai connector such as monday.com): read by Claude (Haiku) only when you press **Sync** (at most every 2 minutes). Opening Tasks never starts a model call, so your Claude usage is spent only when you ask. Never a tool Slate reads itself; no background timer.

## What is stored

- **Per task**: one line with tool, key (`acme/api#412`), title, state, person, link, a few counts, the tracker's type (Bug, Story), reminder time. Never description, comment or message text. A line you wrote is the same row with no tool. In the workspace's local file, never shared, even in a shared workspace.
- **Meetings**: never on disk; in memory until the day ends or Slate quits.
- **Per project**: only the skills you picked (a name per kind), in the file of the workspace holding the project's doc. Skill text never copied.
- **Per learned tool**: name, arguments, your id in that app, where each field sits in the answer; never the answer. For an app Teach Slate found nothing in: when.
- **Receipts**: see [Receipts](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/receipts.md#what-is-stored).

Private files on this machine, readable only by your user:

| File | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `work-gateway-auth.json` | Slate's own sign-in for a web-address gateway or an app connected from Slate; sent only to the server that issued it |
| `work-token-auth.json` | A pasted token with the account name; never logged, sent only to its server; **Disconnect** removes it |
| `oauth-pending.json` | An unfinished sign-in, kept 15 minutes so a restart mid-browser-step loses nothing |

A connected app's address is in the workspace's file; not secret, never shared. Sign-in returns to one fixed address; if another program holds it, to the app's own port.

---

# Agent runs

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/agent-runs.md

An agent run takes a task through a fixed process in a session you can see. On as **agent runs (beta)** in [Automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations.md); off, the card offers only **Just open a session**. Only your click starts one.

## Start a run

1. Open a task, click **Run with AI…**.
2. Check **Where** and **What it is**.
3. Click **Run it** (or **Open a session**).

## The start dialog

- **Where**: project and agent. Default: the task's project, else the last used, else your only project.
- **What it is**: the kind ([Workflow](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/workflow.md)), plus **Investigate only** (to solve), **Draft a reply** or **Find the answer, then draft** (message), **Just open a session** (all).
- **The kind's rule**: the skill, its steps on one line with the two stops for you as an amber hand (*Stops for you after the plan, and before it ships*), and *Saved for every bug in <project>* under the skill picker.
- **What the agent run gets**: **The task**; **What Slate knows** (memories in the brief, each with **×** to leave out; none is valid, and a memory read that fails says so instead of showing none, in the dialog and in the brief the agent gets); **Your note** (closed until added).
- **What it can use**, one line (*GitHub · yarn test · Autopilot off*), opening to each tool and whether the agent reaches it, the check command, Autopilot and the agent run rules, under **Saved for every run in <project>**. **Allow Autopilot** is the project setting; **This run: Step by step / Autopilot** is per run.

**Just open a session** shows **What to type in**: the task's name and link (or a to-do's words), typed but not sent. `/`, `@`, Cmd+Enter work as on Home. A blocked start (folder not a git repository) is explained in the footer.

| Kind | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| **Investigate only** | Reports cause and options; changes no file |
| **Your pull request** | Branch fetched from `origin` into its own folder; it is the only branch the run may push. You approve the plan, then the changes and one comment, word for word. A pull request from someone else's copy of the project is refused (its branch cannot be pushed from your project) |
| **Someone else's PR** | You approve comments as **Post comments**, **Request changes** or **Approve**; the run posts exactly that, never picks. Head fetched from your `origin` (no remote added) into its own folder. Never pushes |
| **A message** | **Draft a reply** in a folder under Slate's data, or **Find the answer, then draft** (reads the project you pick first). The dialog says whether Slate can send it or hands it to you |
| **Check** | Command from the project's files (`package.json` scripts, `Makefile` targets, `pyproject.toml`, `Cargo.toml`, `go.mod`) or **Let the agent run find the tests**. Opens on the detected one; a pick is saved |
| **Tracker and code host** | Whether your agent reaches each (`gh`/`glab`, an MCP server, or a claude.ai connector). Unreachable never blocks: the row says the fallback (a link to open, a ticket update to copy); **Connect** goes to Connect → Integrations. If the agent reported the server needing sign-in in the last day: **Needs sign-in** and **Sign in to Jira in Claude Code** |

## What the run does

**Run it**:

1. Makes a branch named after the task (`fix/proj-12-short-title`) and a folder, then runs the project's setup command there in the background. A failed start removes both; failed setup blocks the run.
2. Starts your agent there with one line naming the run. Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI are told to trust the folder.
3. Closes the dialog; the task shows the run (steps, last report, status). **Open session** shows the terminal. A tool that cannot take a first line at launch opens with it typed in. The run also tops **Agent runs**.

The brief (first step) gives the agent notes on the task, the project's [memory index](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/session-start-brief.md#the-same-index-everywhere-slate-runs-an-ai) and any earlier run for it. Then one step at a time (Read it, Plan, Build, Check, Draft), each reported. After each the run waits for **Next**, shown when the agent finishes its turn.

## Approvals

- **After the plan**: **Approve plan** or **Send back**. **Save as Plan doc** keeps the plan as the branch's Plan doc, in the project, labelled with the branch; unticked, it stays in the run's steps. A Plan doc a person wrote is left as it is, and the run's trail says it was kept. A Plan doc Slate saved from an earlier plan is replaced, but its **Progress** stays.
- **Before anything leaves your machine**: **Approve to ship** shows commits, changed files, and the pull request title and body, ticket update, review comments or reply, word for word, each with **Copy**.
- Approving lets the push through, plus writes to the task's own tracker or chat and the code host. Other servers still ask; merging and removing are always refused.
- After shipping, Slate reads the pull request back and says whether it matches.

A run stopped for you (step done, plan or ship to approve, held call, block) counts in **Needs you** and ⌘⇧J; Claude Code also sends a system notification.

## Autopilot

Runs steps back to back without **Next**. Still stops at both approvals, at a held call, and after a long run of steps. A failed check returns to Build up to twice, then stops.

Off for every project until turned on in the start box or the project's **Settings**; then the panel switches a run between **Step by step** and **Autopilot**. On Autopilot, Claude Code skips asking for calls the rules allow.

| Tool | Autopilot and rules |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code, Cursor (interactive), OpenCode (via Slate's plugin), Codex | Supported; Slate types and sends the next step |
| Gemini CLI | Step by step only: rules can refuse a call but never ask; Slate types the next step and you press Enter |

## Finish a run

After shipping the run waits for its merge. Every two minutes Slate reads the pull request state with `gh` or `glab`; merged, or task done, ends the run. A project on GitHub Enterprise is read the same way, through `gh` signed in to that host.

- **Mark done**: finish by hand.
- Pull request closed unmerged blocks the run, even when its task is done: **Mark done** or **Watch for the merge again**.
- Task done while the pull request is still open or cannot be read: the run ends, and no decision or lesson is marked shipped.
- Reply or review you posted yourself: **I sent it myself**.

A finished run adds one session entry to its project (labelled with the branch), keeps a lesson if the agent reported one, and records session tokens and estimated cost (all but Cursor report usage). It also shows on its pull request's task under Reviews.

In a section, its runs sit at the top under **Agent runs**; **Needs you** shows runs awaiting an answer. **Agent runs** in the side list shows the last 14 days, newest first: status, steps, approvals, the session's [receipt](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/receipts.md); a line above sums runs started, done, pull requests and estimated cost.

**Remove folder** (done runs): the folder goes; the branch too when every commit is on another branch or a remote. A branch holding work stays, as does your own pull request's.

## Pause, reopen, cancel

- Typing in the run's session pauses it until **Resume**.
- **Reopen session**: reopens an ended session in the run's folder (a running background Claude Code job is reattached; else the conversation continues where the tool allows).
- A session that does not pick up the run within five minutes blocks it; **Resume** restarts.
- **Cancel agent run**: stops the session, removes the folder; the branch follows the **Remove folder** rule.

## The agent run rules

The agent keeps your tool's normal reach (shell, web, MCP servers) inside **agent run rules**:

| Area | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| **Git** | Only the run's branch. Push refused until you approve shipping. Force pushes, tags, branch removal always refused |
| **MCP** | A tool that writes elsewhere asks first. Merging and removing refused |
| **Shell** | A command that sends data out asks first |
| **Files** | Writes stay in the run's folder; none while reading and planning |

Rules read every tool call and shell command, including those wrapped in `env`, `$( )`, `sh -c` strings and heredocs. A guard, not a sandbox: an unknown program can still reach the network. The push rule has a second lock, a git hook in the run's folder.

### What the rules do not stop

The rules are a guard, not a sandbox. They read the text of each call. They cannot see what a program does after it starts. These limits are known, accepted and written in ADR 0055 (`docs/internals/decisions/0055-a-task-has-full-capability-inside-task-rules.md`). Plan with them in mind.

- **Scripts and configs in the run's folder.** The rules do not read them. This covers `npm run`, `make`, `rake`, `cargo run` and the scripts in `package.json`. It also covers a script the run writes and then runs (`echo … > x.sh && sh x.sh`). The first step is a write inside the folder, so it is allowed. The second runs a file the rules cannot read in full.
- **Plugins and modules named in a command.** A reporter, plugin or `-r` module comes from the project's installed packages. It is not checked (`pytest -p` still asks).
- **What is inside a `.tar` or `.zip` file or a patch.** `tar`, `unzip` and `patch` are judged by the folder they unpack into, not by the paths inside.
- **Reading your secrets.** Reading is not guarded. `cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa` is allowed.
- **Git changes that stay in the run's own folder.** `git reset --hard`, `git stash drop`, `git reflog expire` and `git gc --prune` are allowed. They can lose work that was never pushed.
- **Paths built while the program runs.** Inline code that builds a path at run time is caught only in some forms (`'/' + 'x'` is caught, most others are not).
- **A pattern that never ends.** A decision that takes longer than one second asks you. The rules cannot interrupt a regular expression that never returns.

What still holds when the text is misread: the git hook in the run's folder holds every push before you approve shipping, and after that any push to another branch. It does not stop a force push to the run's own branch. The shell rule refuses that one. After shipping, Slate reads the pull request back and says whether it matches.

To close one of these for a project, add a **Deny** rule for the command, for example `shell:git reset --hard`.

**A held call** is refused for now and shown in the run. Answer: **Allow for this step**, **Always allow in this project**, **Deny**. An allowance names that one call (MCP tool or exact command) and only passes what a rule would have asked about.

**Your own rules**: **agent run rules** in the start box lists built-in and project rules. Add **Allow**, **Ask first** or **Deny** naming a call as the held-call card does: an MCP tool (`mcp__jira__add_comment`, `mcp__jira__*`), `shell:` plus a command (`shell:npm publish`), or `file:` plus a path. **Allow** covers one exact call; **Ask first** and **Deny** also cover a command's first words and everything under a folder. **Deny** always wins.

---

# Agent runs: Workflow

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/workflow.md

Each kind of [agent run](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/agent-runs.md) runs **one skill per project**. This guide lists the kinds, skill sources and how to change a rule.

## The six kinds

| Kind | How it is known | Steps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Bug** | Ticket type Bug or Defect (Jira), or GitHub issue with a bug label | Read it, Plan, you approve, Build, Check, Draft, you approve, Ship |
| **Feature** | Any other ticket | As bug |
| **Someone else's PR** | You were asked to review it | Read it, Review, you approve, Post |
| **My PR** | Yours; a reviewer asked for changes | Read the comments, Plan, you approve, Build, Check, Draft, you approve, Push and comment. Then done; the next review round is a new run |
| **My PR, checks failing** | Yours; checks fail | Read the checks, then as **My PR** |
| **My PR, ready to merge** | Approved, checks pass, no conflicts | Read it, then as **My PR**: updates the branch and pushes. The merge is yours; a run never merges |

Your pull request awaiting reviewers or running checks has no kind yet; you can pick one. A pull request you opened counts as yours even if assigned to yourself.

## Skills

A skill is one the project keeps (`fix-bug`, `dev-flow`, `code-review`) or **Slate's own steps**. Skills are read from `.claude/skills`, `.agents/skills`, `.cursor/skills`, `.gemini/skills`, `.opencode/skills`, also in sub-packages. A folder with no `SKILL.md` is not a skill.

Slate suggests by skill **name**, best first, never by description. No match: Slate's own steps run until you pick.

| Kind | Names looked for |
| --- | --- |
| Bugs | `fix-bug`, `bugfix`, `fix` |
| Features | `dev-flow`, `development` |
| Reviews | `code-review`, `review` |
| Your pull request | `address-review`, `fix-pr` |
| Failing checks | `fix-checks`, `fix-ci` |
| Ready to merge | `git-merge`, `merge`, `land` |

## Change a rule

1. Open **Workflow**, the folded box atop Issues and Reviews: that section's rules for one project (*Bugs → fix-bug*), with a project picker.
2. Pick a skill. The run button's menu and the start dialog change the same rule.
3. It saves at once for every task of that kind in that project. A changed rule says **Changed** and resets in one click.

If a picked skill leaves the project, the rule says so and Slate's own steps run. **Open** shows the skill in Toolkit; the rule shows its use in the last 30 days (**ran 4× · 1 stopped by you**).

A kind with no skill shows **Slate's own steps** and **New review skill** (or **New bug skill**). It opens [Toolkit](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio.md)'s New skill form on that project with name and description filled. **Create** writes the skill, makes it the rule and returns to Tasks; **Cancel** writes nothing. Offered for a project, not a group.

## Steps and approvals stay

A whole-process skill still runs inside Slate's steps: each step opens the skill's `SKILL.md` and follows it for that step only. The plan still waits for approval; nothing ships before it. The skill lives in the run's folder (a committed one already does; an uncommitted one is copied in with its files), so the agent does not ask permission per step. Skill text is never copied into a prompt. A run keeps its starting skill; a rule change affects the next run.

---

# Receipts

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks/receipts.md
