A receipt is what an AI session ran, checked against what it said. Slate writes one from the transcript when a turn ends, in any captured agent, with no model and nothing leaving this computer.

A session that only talked (no check, no changed file, no commit) gets none. The **Agent runs** count is flagged receipts not yet reviewed.

## What it shows

- **It said**: first paragraph of the last reply.
- **Checked against the transcript**: where said and ran disagree, with evidence; *What it said matches what it ran* otherwise.
- **What it ran**: every test, gate, lint, typecheck and build, in order, with passed and failed counts or exit code.
  A run fails when its summary counts a failure or an error (vitest's `Errors  1 error`, pytest's `2 errors`), or when the command exited with an error even though every test passed. A filter such as `| tail` owns the exit code, so then the counts decide.
- **What changed**: files edited.
- **Outcome**: commits its own `git commit` reported, and whether they are on the default branch or were reverted there within 30 days. Checked when you open agent runs, at most every 10 minutes per receipt.

## Flags

| Flag | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| Red **Flagged** | **A test failed, then passed on a re-run with no change in between.** |
| Red **Flagged** | **The last run failed, and nothing passed after it.** |
| Red **Flagged** | **It said the checks pass, but no test or gate run passed**: the last reply says tests, a gate or a build passed, and no such run did |
| Amber **Worth a look** | **A run ended without a result**: killed or stopped before saying how it went |
| Amber **Worth a look** | **It edited a file outside the project** (temporary and agents' own folders do not count) |
| Amber **Worth a look** | **A test's expected value was changed**: an edit to a test file changed what an assertion expects |

Checks are read from `package.json` scripts, `make` and `just` targets, and the pre-push hook (always a gate). A script running a file in a `gate`, `ci`, `check` or `verify` folder is a gate whatever its name. Cursor records commands but not their output: **not recorded**.

## Actions

- **Mark reviewed**: clears it from the count; new runs, edits or commits in that session ask again.
- **Open session**: opens its tab.
- **Copy as Markdown**: whole receipt, for a pull request.
- **Share as artifact**: publishes the same text as an [artifact](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/artifacts.md).

Both come from the stored receipt. Widgets can read receipts, and a Home widget can show the last day's ([Widget API](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/widgets-api.md)).

## What is stored

Per session that ran a check, changed a file or made a commit, one receipt in the workspace holding the project's folder: session id and tool, title and branch, first paragraph of the last reply, each run's command and result, edited paths, flags, commit ids and subjects, and when you marked it reviewed. Never a run's output beyond counts, nor edit text. Local, never shared.

---

# Docs & the Block Editor

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/docs.md

A doc is Slate's one unit: a note, design doc, project and captured AI session are all rows in one `doc` table, so nesting, reordering, icons and Trash work the same. Each has an id, `parent_id`, title, icon, fractional `position`, block content and metadata (`doc_type`, `status`, `archived`, timestamps).

The line under a title ends with who can read it: **Private** in Personal, **Shared · <workspace>** in a shared one.

**The open screen stays current.** When an agent writes over MCP (appends to the doc you read, renames, files a doc, saves a memory) the screen updates within seconds. If you are typing on that doc, your text is kept and a "changed elsewhere" notice offers **Copy my text**, **Keep my version** (asks once, then overwrites the newer one) and **Reload doc**.

**A save that fails says so.** Typing saves within half a second. If a save does not reach the store (Slate's server is down, or it refused the write), the header shows **Not saved** where it shows **Edited …**. Slate tries again on your next edit, every 5 seconds while the server answers, and at once when it comes back; the word goes when a save lands. A retry never overwrites a newer copy: if the doc changed meanwhile, you get the "changed elsewhere" notice instead. Unsaved edits live in the open window only, so they do not survive quitting Slate.

While the server is down, a red strip at the top reads **Slate isn't responding**. It says your work is safe only while no doc has unsaved edits; otherwise it says some edits are not saved yet. After a minute it says **Still trying. Restart Slate if this stays.** with **Open logs**.

## The block editor

[BlockNote](https://www.blocknotejs.org); content is stored as BlockNote JSON in `content`.

Blocks: paragraph, six heading levels (and toggle headings), bullet, numbered, to-do and toggle lists, quote, code, table, image, video, audio, file, divider; plus **callout** and **doc card** (embeds another doc as a preview). A callout is a plain note; only the ⚠️ emoji draws it in the warning colour, and clicking the emoji cycles the ten offered.

- **`/`** opens the slash menu. First item **Write with AI** asks an agent to draft text; a failed draft keeps the prompt open with the reason and **Retry**. **Callout**, **Link to doc**, **Doc card** are also there.
- **@** links a doc inline; **/Link to doc** opens the same list (loose matching, recent first, arrows and Enter).
- Drag blocks by handle or move by keyboard.
- Pasted Markdown replaces a selection, fills an empty block, or splits a paragraph at the cursor.
- Right-click menus open with their corner at the pointer.

**Right-to-left.** A doc in Hebrew, Arabic or another RTL script lays out right-to-left (body, title, tab, breadcrumb, sidebar row). Direction is read from the text; nothing to set. **Words** are counted by starting script, a tie going to RTL. A doc has one direction; a title declares its own.

## Projects: made in the workspace menu, narrowed to in a feature

Click the workspace mark at the top of the rail, on any tab:

- **New project…**: choose a folder; the name comes from it.
- **Manage projects…**: the workspace's projects by group. Rename, **Open project doc** (where its agent is set), **Move to Trash**.

⌘K and the foot of every project picker's list offer both.

In Projects, Automations, Activity, Artifacts and Memory a **project picker** under the side panel's title narrows the feature to one project. It reads **All projects** at rest; a picked project shows its name with **×** to go back. Each feature keeps its own choice and opens on **All projects** (Memory remembers yours). Home and Toolkit keep their own controls. Sessions covers the whole computer and picks a workspace first ([Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md#narrowing-to-a-workspace-or-a-project)).

## A group's or project's doc

These open on a doc that holds others rather than text: name, one-line description, and tabs with counts. A project's line under its name also has **Code**, opening its files in the side panel ([Files and Changes](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/docs/code.md)).

| Doc | Tabs |
| --- | --- |
| Group | **Projects** · Docs · Sessions · Memory |
| Project | **Docs** · Sessions · Memory · Projects (only when another project was moved under it) |

- **First tab** is what the doc holds and opens first. Empty tabs are omitted except the first. The picked tab is kept per doc kind while the app is open.
- **A project's Docs and Sessions hold everything written in it.** Docs lists the same docs and type folders as the tree, same count (Notes included), filterable by folder, status and title. Sessions lists all its sessions newest first, each with its git branch in grey; with two or more branches a select above shows one branch's. There is no Branches tab: git owns branches, and a branch is only a label on a doc or session.
- **A group's tabs list one level down**: its Docs are those directly in the group, not its projects'. Same for Sessions and Memory. Decisions are not in Docs.
- **Description**: click, write one line, Enter or click away; Escape restores. A group or project has no other doc text (text from an older version is kept in the store, not shown).
- **Memory** lists up to 20 memories saved to that doc, most used first, with a link to all in Memory.
- **Accounts line** (group or standalone project): above the tabs, how many captured sessions ran under the accounts it assigns ([Project environments](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio/cli-profiles.md#how-you-know-its-working)).

Every other doc (plan, design, plain) keeps the editor.

## Markdown in, Markdown out

Pasted Markdown becomes real blocks; blocks render back to Markdown for agents and MCP tools (`blocksToMarkdown`, `markdownToBlocks`, `parseBlocks` in `@slate/shared`).

## More on docs

- [The doc tree](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/docs/tree.md): Overview, Docs, Trash, ordering, nesting, Settings.
- [Files and Changes](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/docs/code.md): Code view of a project.
- [Typed Docs & Hierarchy](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/docs/typed-docs.md): `doc_type` templates and group → project nesting.
- [Legacy work docs](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/docs/missions.md): the legacy work container and branch progress.

Which workspace holds a doc decides whether it is shared. Its ⋯ menu moves it, with everything nested under it, into another workspace (a real move between two SQLite files): [Working in a Shared Workspace](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces/sharing.md).

See also: [Memory](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory.md), [Workspaces](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md).

---

# The doc tree

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/docs/tree.md

The Docs tree nests groups and projects with docs as leaves; any doc can hold children to any depth. With a project picked it starts inside it; on All projects it shows every group and project. For Code see [Files and Changes](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/docs/code.md).

## Overview

Under the project picker, above the Docs and Code tabs, **Overview** shows a card per project, grouped as the tree: **On their own**, then each group by name (empty groups hidden). With no group at all, the cards stand without a heading.

- Card picture: the project's README (first heading and paragraph), else its doc; with neither, the card has no picture.
- Below: name, folder's branch, worktree count if more than one (still one card), last worked time. Green dot = a session is working in it.
- Click a card to pick that project on Docs and Code: Overview keeps its one card, drawn larger; the side panel lists only it. Click that card to open the project's doc. The picker narrows Overview the same way.
- Projects with no doc open lands here. No project: one sentence with a **New project** button; the side panel says nothing more.

## Docs or Code

The tabs under the picker choose what the side panel lists. A project opens on its doc. **Code** on the doc switches the panel to Code → Files with that project's files open. On Code, the doc icon at the end of a project's row returns to Docs. The choice lasts while the app is open; every launch starts on Docs.

## Add a doc or project

The side panel's **+** (title row, Docs and Code):

- **Blank doc** (⌘N, caret in title).
- **Write it with AI…** (⌘⇧G): an agent drafts from your description.
- **New project…**.

A doc goes in the picked project. On All projects **Blank doc** is off and says why (a doc lives in a project; pick one first). The tooltip names the destination: "New doc in slate". With no project, a top line says: *A workspace holds your projects. A project is a folder you open. A group collects related projects.* Each row's icon shows its type, changeable later ([Typed Docs](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/docs/typed-docs.md#doc-types)).

## What the tree shows

- **Breadcrumbs**: `Grandparent / Parent / Title`. **Icon**: a [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) name or an emoji.
- **Captured sessions are not rows**; a project lists them under **Sessions · N**; [Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md) lists all.
- **Notes are counted**: a doc an agent wrote as a note is not a row. A doc holding some shows a **Notes** row with the count; it lists them in the main area, newest change first, with a title filter. They open, link and edit like any doc. A note holding docs stays a row.
- **Decisions are not in Docs**: each is a memory listed in [Memory](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory.md). A decision holding docs stays a row.
- **Same-named projects** show folder ends: `lq  Documents/lq`, `lq  Private/lq`.
- **No branch is a doc**: a branch is a label on docs, sessions and memories made on it; the project holds them. Its worktree is read from git, and Sessions can start a session in it.

## Order, move and group

- **Order**: docs keep your order.
- **Drag to reorder** rewrites one row (fractional `position`); after about 52 drops into one gap, that parent's children are renumbered once. `position` is local, never pushed.
- **Move / nest**: drag under a new parent. A group goes at the top; a project at the top or in a group; other drops are refused with the reason and nothing moves. Other docs go anywhere.
- **Group projects**: shift-click two or more standalone projects, **Group…** on ⋯ or right-click, name it; they move in.

## Trash

**Move to Trash** keeps the doc recoverable: "Moved “Title” to Trash." with **Undo**; the open tab closes.

**Trash** lists each doc with when and from where ("Moved to Trash 2 days ago · from slate"), with a title filter.

- Row: **Restore**, **Delete forever…** icon, shown on hover or focus.
- Tick rows: **Restore (N)**, **Delete forever (N)**. Nothing ticked: **Empty Trash**, or **Delete forever · N shown** while the filter hides some. Delete forever always asks.
- Widgets in Trash have their own **Widgets** heading with **Restore** and **Delete forever…**.
- Click a doc to read it, read-only, with a **Restore** bar. A link to a vanished doc says so and offers **Open Trash**.
- Unreadable Trash: **Try again**.

## Branches and worktrees

- **Removed worktree**: worktrees are made beside the git repository as `<repo>-<branch>` (Slate's tooling: `<repo>.noindex/`). A session captured after its folder is removed files under its project; a folder that still exists keeps its own name.
- **Ended branch**: nothing changes; docs stay in the project's type folders and sessions in **Sessions**, labelled with the branch.

## A project's docs by type

Docs and Code share one skeleton: groups you made holding projects, and standalone projects. In Docs an open project has one folder per doc type it holds, with a count, in order: Plans, Designs, Meetings, Reviews, Test Plans, Bug Reports, **Notes**, General Docs.

- Folders start closed and stay as left; the open doc opens its folder.
- Inside, newest first: the ten most recent, then **Show N older**.
- Every doc written in the project is there, whichever branch, whether or not git still has it. Hover a doc for its branch.
- Code keeps **Files** and **Changes**, with a group's projects under its row.

## Settings

A group doc or standalone project has a **Settings** button in its header (a project in a group uses its group's). One sheet:

- its folder; the agents and accounts it uses;
- worktree commands: **Set up**, **Preview**, **On remove**, **Carry over**;
- the **Check** command that decides a task is done; **Autopilot**; a **Memory** section.

Fields save on leaving; tools save with **Save agents**. Settings stay on this computer (they name local accounts and commands) and never travel with a shared workspace; only the Memory section is saved in the workspace. Accounts and models are set in Connect → Agents. A group's or project's tools override the workspace's; a new project asks for none.

## A refused action

A failed move, rename, duplicate, Move to Trash or restore (doc gone, workspace read-only, someone else's doc) shows a bottom message naming the doc and reason; the tree stays as it was. It closes after 8 seconds (waits while pointed at) or with ✕. The same message reports what you did elsewhere, with **Undo** when possible.

---

# Files and Changes

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/docs/code.md

**Code** lists every project with a git folder on this computer (the picked one, or all) with two views on its left edge: **Files** and **Changes**. A project with no folder here says so. Open it with **Code** on a project's doc ([The doc tree](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/docs/tree.md#docs-or-code)).

## Files

A tree like an editor's explorer.

- One-folder project: one row (name and branch) with files under it. With one project picked the row goes: files start at the top under a bar with the branch and the row's buttons.
- Two or more git worktrees: a group headed like **slate · 2 worktrees**, a row per worktree named by branch (hover for folder). Group starts open, worktrees shut; all stays as left.
- Files changed since the last commit show **M**, **A** or **D**, with a dot on their folders. Find a file by name with ⌘K.
- Hover a checkout's row: **New file**, **New folder**, **Refresh**, **Collapse all**.
- Right-click a file, folder or the space below: **New file**, **New folder**, **Open terminal here**, **Start session here**, **Copy path**, **Reveal in Finder**, **Rename**, **Move to Trash**. Names are typed in place. These wait while an agent works in that project.
- Rename or trash can be undone from its message or from Turns; a trashed file is also in the system Trash (the Recycle Bin on Windows). A file on another disk than the Trash, or on a Windows network share or removable drive, is refused and stays where it was.

## Changes

One section per checkout with files waiting to be committed, named by project and branch (branch named once). Source control as VS Code lays it out: one-line message, full-width **Commit** with **Commit & Push** in its ▾, files waiting (each committed unless unticked), same as a session's Changes ([Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/review.md#source-control)). The icon counts all waiting files. A worktree removed in a terminal leaves the list within about half a minute, or at once on returning to the window.

## A file in a tab

A file opens in a tab; the rail stays on Projects. A file picked in ⌘K comes here with its tree unfolded.

- The line under the cursor shows, after its end, when it last changed and in which commit. **Blame** shows it for every line.
- **Show changes** appears when the file differs from where its branch began; **Back to the file** or Esc leaves.
- Bottom bar: branch, **worktree** when relevant, path from the project folder.

---

# Typed Docs & Hierarchy

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/docs/typed-docs.md

`doc_type` says what kind a doc is; `status` says where it stands. Together they give memory tools a structure to navigate.

## Doc types

A new doc is a plain **Doc**. The chip under the title (**Doc ▾**) changes its type any time, listing the seven types a person writes: Doc, Plan, Design, Review, Meeting, Test Plan, Bug Report. A change appends the new type's template headings after the existing text, once. Group, project and branch are made by Slate from folders and sessions, so they are not in the menu. The `DocType` enum is in `@slate/schema` (`doc-type/types.ts`):

| DocType | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `general` | Plain knowledge doc |
| `design` | Design doc |
| `plan` | Implementation or work plan |
| `review` | Review write-up |
| `meeting` | Meeting notes |
| `test-plan` | Test plan |
| `bug-report` | Bug report |
| `group` | Set of projects you made and named; no folder of its own |
| `project` | One folder, usually a git repository, in a group or alone |
| `mission` | Legacy; work now files under its project ([`mission` docs](missions.md)) |

## Status

From `DOC_STATUSES`: `draft` (started, not active), `active` (in progress), `done`, `canceled` (abandoned).

## The hierarchy

Structural types nest as memory expects (`@slate/schema`, `doc-type/rules.ts`):

```
group
└── project
    └── branch
        └── knowledge docs
            (plan | design | test-plan | bug-report | review | meeting | general)
```

A project may stand at top level with no group. Knowledge docs may sit directly under a `group` or `project`. `ALLOWED_DOC_CHILDREN` says what nests under what; for groups, projects and branches it is enforced on move (a `project` dropped in a `branch` is refused). A knowledge doc in an unusual place shows a tree warning.

Memory tools work without a doc id: on `recall` or `remember` Slate resolves a **target** by walking from the current project and group. A memory belongs to the project it concerns and says which git branch it was learned on (a label, never a doc). A decision's full reasoning is a decision doc under the project, labelled with its branch; the tree counts them in a **Decisions** row.

## Filling one in

Slate never creates a knowledge doc without asking: at a milestone your agent asks whether to save it ([`mission` docs](missions.md#slate-offers-the-doc-at-each-milestone)). To have an agent write into a doc, use **Start session** on the doc's header or its Sessions tab. The launcher hands the CLI the doc, its lineage (group → project → branch), the branch's goal and next open item, and the project's recorded decisions ([Sessions → Starting a session from a doc](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/start.md#from-a-doc)).

See also: [Docs & the Block Editor](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/docs.md), [Recall & Remember](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/recall-remember.md).

---

# Legacy `mission` docs, and progress on a branch

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/docs/missions.md

A `mission` doc was Slate's first container for a piece of work. No new ones are made; old ones still open. Work now files under its **project**: a session, plan or decision made on a git branch carries the branch as a label, and no doc stands for the branch.

An old `mission` doc (`doc_type = mission`) keeps nesting, breadcrumbs and the editor, and:

- the type chip shows its **status**: `draft`, `active`, `done`, `canceled`;
- a new empty one starts from the old outline: Goal, Checklist, Session log, Decisions, Notes;
- a list above the text shows docs filed under it; a project may hold one without a tree warning.

The **Doc ▾** menu does not offer `mission` ([Typed Docs](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/docs/typed-docs.md#doc-types)).

## Progress on a branch

The next session on a branch, yours or an agent's, starts with what the branch is for, derived from the project's records labelled with the branch and from git. No doc holds it.

The MCP tool `log_mission_progress` takes `cwd` (and `branch` when the work was on a branch other than the checked-out one, which git must know):

```
recall  →  work the task  →  log_mission_progress(summary, goal, open_items, decisions)
```

- **Goal and open items** become the branch's goal and open items, shown in the next session's brief. A newer report replaces the older; they fade after a state memory's shelf life, and are retired when the branch lands or is removed.
- **Each decision** is saved as a decision memory labelled with the branch.
- **The summary** is a session entry of the project, labelled with the branch, in its **Sessions** tab.
- No doc is made. On a trunk branch (`main`, `master`, `develop`) the goal is not changed.

`log_mission_progress` is a memory tool exposed to every connected agent ([Recall & Remember](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/recall-remember.md)).

## Slate offers the doc at each milestone

At a milestone (plan, review, test plan, bug report, design) Slate has your agent ask in chat whether to keep it as a doc. It tells the tool to use its own click-to-answer question tool, so where that tool shows choices you click one; the wording is the tool's.

| Tool | Asks with | Reminded when you ask for a milestone | Sent back to ask if a plan was never offered |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `AskUserQuestion` | yes | yes |
| Gemini CLI | `ask_user` | yes | yes |
| Codex | `request_user_input` | yes | yes |
| OpenCode | `question` | yes | yes; its end-of-turn event cannot reply, so Slate's plugin sends the ask as a new prompt when the turn goes idle |
| Cursor | `AskQuestion` | sent from Cursor's prompt event, which does not run in print mode (`cursor-agent -p`) | yes in the interactive app; its stop event does not run in print mode |

Choose save and the tool saves the doc in the project, labelled with the branch; choose not and nothing is saved. If the branch already has that doc, the choice is to add to it, keeping what is there. Every tool also carries a standing instruction to ask before saving a plan, review, test plan, bug report or design.

**A plan from plan mode is kept** as the branch's Plan doc, in the project, labelled with the branch. A later plan on the same branch replaces the one Slate made. A Plan doc you wrote is never changed.

See also: [Typed Docs & Hierarchy](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/docs/typed-docs.md), [Recall & Remember](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/recall-remember.md), [Docs & the Block Editor](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/docs.md).

---

# Automations

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/loop.md

An **automation** works without being driven: a standup at 7:00, a debrief when a coding session ends, a plan per assigned ticket. Automations holds yours and everything they write, plus what Slate runs itself ([Built-in](#the-automations-place)).

## Make an automation

An automation is **a job, a trigger and steps**, held to **rules**.

1. Click **+** in the side panel's title row.
2. Pick **From a template**, **Set it up yourself** (empty editor) or **Describe it to AI…** (an agent writes it).
3. Write the **Job** in your words ("Every weekday morning, tell me where each project stands and what to focus on"). Every step reads it first; with none, steps run as written.
4. Pick what starts it, and a project.

## What starts it

| Starts | When |
| --- | --- |
| **By hand** | **Run now**. You can type a starting text. |
| **On a schedule** | **How often**: *every day*, *every weekday*, *every week* or *every month*, at an hour and minute :00, :15, :30 or :45. Weekday = Monday to Friday (a weekend run moves to Monday, same time). Monthly takes day 1 to 28. Listed as "Weekdays · 7:30 AM". |
| **When a session ends** | After an AI coding session is captured. With **Scheduled automations** off in [Automations › Built-in](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations.md) these do not start, nor later for sessions that ended meanwhile. |
| **When a task arrives** | When Tasks pulls in a new integration item, such as an assigned ticket. One read hands the run up to 5 new items. If already running, new items wait and start one run together afterwards. A just-connected tracker starts nothing (its first read brings everything). Your own to-dos never start one. Tasks reads integrations on opening and on returning to the window after over a minute. |

Starts on its own only while **Runs on its own** (under **Starts**) is on. A line under the schedule says "Next: Mon 7:30 AM" or "Off, so it will not run on its own." Any automation can be run by hand.

- **Asleep at due time**: runs once on wake. For time-bound reports switch on **Skip a run that is more than two hours late** ("· skips late runs").
- **One at a time**; never started twice. **Slate stops mid-run**: marked failed; a scheduled one reruns minutes after return.

An automation belongs to the workspace it was made in and runs **while Slate is open on it**. It needs a project:

- New ones open in the project Automations is narrowed to and cannot be saved without one. With none picked, **Runs in** says **Pick a project**, listing only groups and projects.
- The six seeded ones have no project: **Run now** and **Turn on** ask, save, then go on. **Turn off** never asks.
- No scheduled run without a project. If the project was removed: editable and can be switched off, not on, until you pick one.
- Moving a group or project to another workspace takes its automations along.

## Its steps

Run in order; each reads what came before:

- **`@context`**: what the run started with: text typed at Run now, "A coding session just ended.", or today's date for a scheduled run. After Recent tasks, that step's report.
- **`@prev`**: previous step's answer.

A step can name its own agent (one on Claude, next on Gemini); none named uses the automation's tool, with the account from the group or project. Each run writes **one report**: last step's answer first, earlier steps after under their labels.

The first step can be **Recent tasks**: [Recent tasks](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/loop/recent-tasks.md).

## What it follows

**Follows**, in the editor under **Runs in**:

- **Slate's own steps**: as written (default).
- **A skill of its project** (**Skills in** *project*): the skills [Toolkit](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio.md) shows.
- **A subagent of its project** (**Subagents**).
- **+ New skill in Toolkit…**: opens Toolkit's New skill form on the project with name and purpose filled. **Create** writes it, sets the automation to follow it, returns you. Only for a saved automation with no unsaved changes.

Every step opens the skill's or subagent's file first and follows it, so runs count as that skill's use. The file is found in the project's folder at run start. If the skill left the project, the editor says so and runs follow Slate's own steps until you pick another. Moving the automation to another project clears the choice.

## The thread

Opens on its **Thread**: every run, oldest first; typed words above the answer they started; under each run a line of what it used ("Used jira ×2, github · 1 call waiting for you"). A report over 1,600 characters shows its opening; **Read the whole report** opens it.

To answer the last run, type in the box under the thread and press **Send**: one more short run (not the steps) on the same agent and folder, reading the last four turns and your words, each earlier report cut to its first 3,000 characters. The box is off while the automation runs or cannot run (for example, no project). Before the first run it is the run's starting text and the button says **Start**; **Run now** runs with nothing typed.

## What it may do

An automation uses the tools its agent reaches: your MCP servers (Jira, GitHub, Slack…). **Setup → May do**:

- **Reading goes on without asking**: searching, listing, opening a ticket or pull request.
- **A call that changes something asks first**: posting, commenting, creating an issue.
- **Merging, removing and writing files are refused.**

It also reads apps connected in [Connect → Integrations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md#integrations) with no MCP server needed (`connected_tools`, `read_connected`, using Slate's sign-in). Setup shows each at the head of the **Allowed** row with its logo; click opens Connect. Excluded: token-connected apps, and an app the automation's Deny covers whole (`mcp__linear__*`). The report names the app (*linear · list_issues*) and the lists below treat that read as a call to it.

Three lists adjust this per automation, the same as an agent run: **Allow**, **Ask first**, **Deny**. One call per line as the agent names it; trailing `*` covers a server (`mcp__jira__*`). Slate's rules hook enforces them when the agent is connected in [Connect](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md) with hooks on; without hooks the tool is not held and Setup says so.

### When it asks first

A held call lets the run carry on, saying what it wanted. When the run ends it waits as an **Ask first** card ("Standup's rules held a call: …") in the thread under that run and on [Home](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent.md). **Yes, do it** starts one short run allowed exactly that call; the card then says "Done: Posted to #acme-dev." or "Not made: …". **No** closes it. Each is answered once. **Later** (Home) sets it aside.

## What it knows

**What it knows** lists memories the automation wrote (replaced or retired ones stay, crossed out) and previews those it is given before a run, each with a pin and a keep-out. Each run reads: its job, sessions and memories of its project or group, its last three reports, your replies.

## Where an automation works

It runs **in its group's or project's directory** (the watched checkout, else the folder), loading project-scoped MCP servers for every step; fixed once per run. Without a group or project it does not run by itself and **Run now** asks you to choose.

Background runs have limits:

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Spend per run | $5 shared; each turn gets what is left; none starts at zero |
| Turns, tool not reporting spend | 12 |
| Claude Code agent turns inside each turn | 30 (other tools have no such flag) |
| Silence before a step gives up | 4 minutes (any word, tool call or result restarts the clock) |

## The ceremonies

Six seeded automations, each one Recent tasks step, organised **by project**. All start **switched off** with no project; **Run now** or **Turn on** asks which project, saves, goes on.

| Automation | Starts | Looks back | Produces |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Standup** | daily, 07:00 | 3 days | Where each project stands, today's focus |
| **Shutdown** | daily, 18:00 | 1 day | What moved, loose ends, tomorrow's first move |
| **Planning** | Monday 08:00 | 7 days | What to commit to this week, per project |
| **Weekly review** | Friday 17:00 | 7 days | Shipped, in flight, blocked |
| **Retro** | Friday 17:00 | 7 days | What went well, what dragged, one change |
| **Monthly review** | day 1, 09:00 | 30 days | Trajectory, decisions that mattered, one change |

Standup, Shutdown, Weekly review and Retro also write decisions to memory (up to five per run); Planning and Monthly review do not. None skips a late run. Each is ordinary: change the time, scope it, or add a step after Recent tasks ("turn this into three Slack-ready bullets").

**Memory pass** template: daily 08:30; reads yesterday's sessions and the group's or project's memories; adds at most five (a correction, a confirmed approach, a decision and why); proposes merges and retirements for review. Does nothing until saved, scoped to a group or project, and switched on. Runs on its agent and account.

**Memory care**: turning on **AI memory care** in Memory adds it (daily 03:00, skips a missed night). See [AI memory care](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations.md#ai-memory-care).

## The Automations place

Opens on **Overview**:

- **Latest**: newest report per automation, plus a live card for a run in progress.
- **History**: every report by automation, newest first. The find box matches automation name, a word in a report's title or opening, or a date ("Oct 8", "2026-10-08"); every word must match. A renamed automation keeps its history. A report opens only when picked. Unreadable reports: **Try again**; **No reports yet** only when none exist.

Under Overview is **Built-in**: what Slate runs itself, each with a switch (`/loop?view=built-in`); see [Built-in automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations.md). Below are yours, grouped by trigger: **Running**, **On a schedule**, **When a session ends**, **When a task arrives**, **By hand**. Pick one for tabs **Thread**, **Setup** (job, start, where it works, what it may do, steps) and **What it knows**; **Run now**, **Edit** and the on/off switch sit above. **Edit** opens the editor; **Overview** returns.

Reports **go for good, not to Trash**: **Delete forever…** asks once ("Delete forever?"); the automation can run again. Deleting an automation forever keeps its reports. **⌘K** searches reports (title and body), under **Reports** (at most four) then **Artifacts**.

**When a run finishes**: an OS notification with the report's opening line (cut at 180 characters) and a **Report ready** toast. A failure shows an **Automation failed** toast, and the error stays under **Last run**. If your agent's own sign-in lapses you get one notification, on the first run failing that way. A report opens **in Automations**, beside earlier runs, from anywhere.

See also: [Home](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent.md), [Built-in automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations.md), [Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md).

---

# Recent tasks

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/loop/recent-tasks.md

**Recent tasks** is a first step for an [automation](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/loop.md). Before writing it gathers what happened and checks it against your live tools. Only the first step can be one, since later steps read its report.

## Context it sees

| Source | Brings in |
| --- | --- |
| Sessions | Up to 80 newest captured AI sessions in the look-back window, tagged with group or project; one-line summary cut at 280 characters |
| Memories | Up to 30 memories picked by pin, recent use and kind (not date), each with kind (`decision` / `preference` / `state` / `fact` / `lesson`), ref and reasoning; list stops at about 5,600 characters; memories whose cited code changed are left out. Scoped to a group or project: that doc's own memory (a group's includes its projects'), plus global |
| Docs | Titles of up to 100 docs, newest change first, in the automation's group or project |
| Prior runs | Its own three latest reports, each's opening 600 characters |

**Look back**: days of sessions read, 1 to 365, starting at 7.

**Write decisions back to memory**: the report may end with a `memories` block, saved as memory (at most five per run) and removed from the report you read. The same switch lets a `memory-proposals` block propose merges and retirements of the memories shown, by ref; each waits in Memory under **Needs review** until accepted. Only an automation scoped to a group or project can file one.

It can also search the workspace and your connected tools; what it may change follows the automation's rules ([What it may do](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/loop.md#what-it-may-do)).

## Grounding on live tools

Stored records show what was true when written, so Recent tasks checks live tools first. It takes the distinct **working contexts** (directory and CLI config) of the period's sessions, drops folders under `/tmp` and similar, ranks the rest (git checkouts first, then work done), keeps the top three, and names the others as skipped. For each, one short pass runs the agent *in that directory under that config* (so project-scoped MCP servers load), checking:

1. Jira or Linear: your issues, not Done (defines your work).
2. GitHub: your pull requests for those tickets: state, CI, who the review waits on.
3. Calendar: today's meetings (skipped if the calendar was already read).
4. Slack: who waits on what for those tickets and pull requests, last three days.

Passes ask only for identifiers, states, names and times. Ticket bodies, comments and message text are never requested or stored.

## The report

Opens with three columns: **Assigned to me**, **Pull requests**, **Today's meetings**. A pull request shows its full GitHub name (`acme/api#12`), so two projects' `#12` are two rows.

- A source needing sign-in shows a sign-in button (same account and directory as the pass), then reruns the automation.
- An unreachable source says so, never "Nothing assigned".

The text then lists what was **verified this run** and which sources **could not be reached** (the agent said so, or its CLI reported the server failed, pending, unknown or needing sign-in). If no project had sessions in the window nothing is checked, and the report says so. A ticket or PR status may be stated as current only if a tool returned it this run. Seeded Standup and Shutdown end with **Not verified**; a gallery template adds none unless its prompt does.

## Prompt variables

Filled just before it runs; only Recent tasks reads them (the editor warns if a later step uses one and points to `@context`):

| Variable | Expands to |
| --- | --- |
| `@sessions` | Recent captured sessions |
| `@memory` | Memories the run is given: up to 30, each with kind, ref and reason. Never a hidden memory or a stale `state`. If Slate's server is not running, the line says no memory |
| `@docs` | The doc titles above |
| `@date` | Today's date |
| `@prior_outputs` | Recent reports of this automation |

---

# Built-in automations

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations.md

Slate runs thirteen things on its own; **Automations › Built-in** (the row under **Overview** in [Automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/loop.md)) says what each does and what turning it off costs. Eleven have a switch. Two always run: clearing the queue a finished session leaves, and the [startup repairs](#the-repairs-at-startup).

## Switch scope

Ten switches are app-wide: off stops it in every workspace. They pause things you already choose one by one (each automation's switch, each reminder, each workspace's sharing) all at once.

**AI memory care** is per workspace: it spends your agent's tokens on that workspace's account. Its card is last in **Built-in** and says it holds for this workspace only. **Auto-capture** appears twice (top card and a list row): one switch.

## What runs

| Automation | Does | Off means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Scheduled automations** | Starts your automations at their times and those that run when a session ends; files each report under its group or project. Open workspace only, while Slate is open and the computer awake | Nothing runs on a schedule; automations stay listed and run by hand |
| **Shared workspace sync** | At startup, then every two minutes: pushes your docs in a shared workspace, pulls others'. Needs sign-in. After repeated failures waits longer, up to an hour | Shared workspaces stop updating both ways; **Sync now** still works |
| **agent runs (beta)** | Adds **Run with AI…** to a task (branch, folder, guided run). Every two minutes checks if a shipped run's pull request merged; for 30 days after shipping, hourly checks for a revert | Task card offers only **Just open a session**; started runs keep their rules; no merge or revert checks |
| **Reminders** | Rings when a task with a time comes due, in every workspace on this computer | Nothing rings; times stay |
| **AI memory care** (per workspace) | [Below](#ai-memory-care) | Free rules only: memories whose code is gone or whose state expired are hidden, badly shaped new ones refused; nothing spent |
| **Automatic updates** | Checks for a version, downloads in background, installs on next quit | Keep your version until you check in Settings → About |
| **Tell me when a session needs me** | One notification when a session waits on a permission or question and Slate is not in front; none for a finished turn | Sessions carry on; the amber dot and ⌘⇧J show the waiting one |
| **Show Slate in the menu bar** | Menu bar icon opens a panel of working or waiting sessions, with a count while one needs you | Icon leaves; Sessions and ⌘⇧J still show all |
| **Start Slate at login** | Opens Slate in the background at login. Off until turned on | Starts when you open it |
| **Auto-capture** | Watches agents' transcripts and your projects, files what happens into the workspace owning the folder. While Slate is open; sessions run after quitting are caught at next launch | Nothing captured on its own, at once; agents can still write through Slate's MCP server |
| **Keep the computer awake** | **Off until turned on.** While a session or automation works, stops the computer sleeping | Computer sleeps on schedule; running work pauses until wake |

**Per-agent capture.** Auto-capture is the master switch. Each agent whose transcripts Slate reads has a **Capture** switch on its row in Connect → **Agents**: off, its sessions are not recorded; it stays connected; other tools unaffected. Cursor has none: its capture is the hook on that row.

A switch applies on the next tick, not next launch: within a minute for the automation tick, two for sync and the merge check. Auto-capture applies at once.

### AI memory care

**Off until turned on.** Each night at 03:00, with the computer awake and Slate open, it reads up to 50 memories the free rules cannot judge.

- Each is read twice, separately, against the code it cites.
- Skipped: pinned or protected memories, lessons with a trigger, preferences, memories with a proposal waiting, any read in the last 90 days.
- One group or project per night: the one with the most memories, on its own agent and account.
- A memory both readings call wrong is retired (**Bring back** under the **retired** chip in Memory undoes it for 30 days). A disagreement waits in Memory → **Needs review**, at most 10 at once.
- Turning it on shows the cost and asks a monthly token cap: 1 million, 4 million or none. It stops for the month when the next night would pass it.
- Runs as an automation named **Memory care**, so **Scheduled automations** must be on.

## What reaches the network

- **Slate's own account** ([Privacy & Security](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security.md)): the update check (release manifest) and shared-workspace sync.
- **Through your agent's CLI, under its auth**: scheduled automations, session-end automations, agent runs, AI memory care.
- **Your own `gh` or `glab`**: agent run merge check and revert search (revert search is GitHub only).
- Everything else is local.

Turning something off removes nothing: capture off keeps captured sessions; sync off does not withdraw shared docs ([leaving a workspace](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces/sharing.md)).

## Keeping the computer awake

Stops the computer sleeping before a 7:00 automation, only while there is work: a session whose status is *working*, a running automation, or a turn of Slate's own agent (a session only waiting on you does not count). Afterwards it may sleep on schedule. No effect in safe mode.

One switch, two places: the **coffee-cup button** in the top bar (green with a live dot while holding; click for the switch and what holds it, such as "Holding now — 1 session working, 1 automation running"), and the **Keep the computer awake** row in Built-in.

It never keeps the screen on, never stops you sleeping from the menu, and a Mac on battery still sleeps on lid close. It ends when Slate quits or crashes. On macOS it is `caffeinate -i`.

## The repairs at startup

Each start, Slate fixes rows earlier versions wrote wrongly (a doc indexed with empty search text, one under a vanished parent); some every start, some once. The same pass removes log entries older than 400 days. No switch.

See also: [Privacy & Security](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security.md), [Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md), [Automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/loop.md), [Licensing & Updates](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/licensing.md).

---

# Artifacts

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/artifacts.md

An **artifact** is a web page an agent made for you: an HTML page, dashboard, chart, report or Markdown note. Any connected tool publishes one with the `publish_artifact` MCP tool; it is stored in your workspace on this computer and listed in **Artifacts** in the rail.

A [widget](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/widgets.md) is different (`get_widget`, `publish_widget`); given a widget, the artifact tools refuse and name those.

## Make or change one

You ask; you never edit by hand.

1. **Ask for one**: "make me a dashboard of this data as an artifact". Every connected tool is also told to show a chart, table or report this way unprompted.
2. **Ask for a change**: "make the bars blue", in **Ask for a change** under the title or to any tool.
3. **Open it**: click the `slate://artifacts` link the tool gives; it names the workspace, so Slate switches first.

Details:

- The tool sends the HTML with a title, or writes a file and sends its path. Files are read only from the working folder or a temp folder, never a file or folder whose name starts with a dot below your home or the working folder (`.env`, `.ssh`). A working folder that is your home folder or wider is not trusted.
- **Ask for a change** opens a session in the artifact's project, on that project's tool. It reads the HTML with `get_artifact` and sends only the changed parts. That adds a **version**; older stay. Republishing the same HTML adds none.
- On an older version the box says so ("This change starts from v1, not the newest (v3)") and the tool sends the whole HTML as a new version (edits apply only to the newest).

## The Artifacts screen

- **Side panel**: **Overview**, then every artifact in the workspace, newest first, with an HTML or Markdown icon and last-change time. Artifacts belong to the workspace, so no project picker. **Filter artifacts** matches title and description.
- **Overview**: a card per artifact, newest first, the same cards Widgets draws. An HTML picture is the HTML in a script-free frame in Slate's look and the current theme; script-drawn charts show only what the markup holds. Markdown uses the viewer's renderer. Drawn only while on screen, at most nine at a time.
- **Open artifact**: name, who made it and when, what it is.
- **Preview | Code**: the HTML or its read-only source (HTML laid out one block per line, indented; only spacing changes). **Copy HTML** copies the HTML as published.
- **‹ v2 of 3 ›**: steps versions. An older one says "You are looking at v2. The newest is v3." with **Restore this version** (republishes it as a new version; nothing in between is lost).
- **Ask for a change** shows only on an artifact you published under a project folder (a teammate's has one writer; a folderless one has nowhere to start a session).
- **⋯**: **Copy HTML** or **Copy Markdown**, **Open in browser** (HTML only), **Rename**, **Delete forever** (asks "Delete every version forever?"). A failed rename or removal keeps the menu open with the reason.

## Finding one

- **⌘K**: title or description, and Markdown by text, under **ARTIFACTS** after reports. HTML code is not searched.
- **The doc it was made on**: **Artifacts made here**. A branch shows its own; a project every one made inside it.
- **`recall`**: returns up to 2 artifacts after memories when every word of the question matches one, so a session can find last week's dashboard and change it.

## How HTML artifacts look

Slate's look (app font, colours, plain buttons, inputs, tables, code, headings; your theme, Mint or Forest, live) comes before the artifact's own styles, which win. In your own browser: default colours and the system light or dark. Tools are told to use `var(--text)`, `var(--muted)`, `var(--surface)`, `var(--border)`, `var(--accent)`, chart colours `var(--c1)` to `var(--c5)`, and classes `card`, `badge`, `grid`, `row`, `stack`.

## Live artifacts

Published with `live: true`, an artifact reads your workspace while shown, so a dashboard stays current without republishing. Header: **Reads your workspace · no internet**. Toggling live adds a version (ADR 0070).

| Aspect | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Reads | Docs, one doc's text, memories and AI sessions of its project (whole workspace if made under none); newest first, up to 5,000 rows each; read-only |
| Network | No fetch, WebRTC, resource hint (preconnect, prefetch), internet image or font, form, new window, frame or `document.write`. Scripts may load from cdnjs, jsDelivr, unpkg (chart libraries work). An attempt to leave for another address closes it |
| Isolation | No origin of its own; shares nothing with other artifacts, not even localStorage; talks to Slate only over a private channel opened at start |
| Yours only | In a shared workspace a teammate's live artifact is a plain HTML page and never reads your store; restored on another computer it is also plain |

## Where it runs

HTML runs its own scripts, served from your workspace on a private local address apart from Slate and your data; it cannot steer the Slate window and nothing is copied to disk. It may load internet scripts and fonts. Markdown is formatted text. A teammate's artifact has no storage of its own (scripts, forms, downloads, popups kept) and cannot read the browser storage of your own artifacts, which keep theirs.

In a shared workspace every member sees artifacts. One writer, the publisher: a teammate's shows "Written by" and their name, with no Rename or Delete forever. Their new versions reach you on next sync, newest only; you keep versions received; later joiners start at the newest. Moving a group or project to another workspace takes its artifacts along.

## Limits

One web page per artifact, up to 5,000,000 characters. HTML or Markdown only.

---

# Widgets

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/widgets.md

A widget is a small card that Slate runs for you: tokens per project, a review queue, a form that files tasks. You describe it, your agent writes it, and it shows on a tab: today [Activity](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/activity.md), [Home](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent.md), or the side panel of a session open in [Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md). Change it by asking again, or by editing its files.

A widget is a small folder of React files, built on `@slate/sdk` and `@slate/ui`. It is an [artifact](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/artifacts.md) with its own **Widgets** item on the rail. Every version is kept. The starter Slate makes a new widget from ("Your agent is building this widget…") is not one: your agent's first build is version 1, and a new version comes only when you ask for a change. There is one kind of widget. Decisions: ADR 0077, ADR 0089 and, for GitHub, ADR 0080.

## Contents
