# Connect

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md

**Connect** (base of the rail, beside Trash and Settings) has three tabs, **Agents**, **Integrations** and **Import**. It is **per workspace**. What Slate runs on its own is in **Automations › Built-in** ([Automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations.md)).

## Contents

- [Agents](#agents)
- [Integrations](#integrations)
- [Import](#import)
- [What is not here](#what-is-not-here)

## Agents

**Connect an agent** heads the tab. Under it: filters **All 16**, **On this Mac**, **Connected**, and **Find an agent** (by name). Each tool is a row: logo, name, and on the right one mark or button. A second line shows only when something differs from normal: a warning, a tool not on this Mac, or a profile or model you chose. Click the logo or name for the tool's dialog, which shows the profile it runs under (one login of the tool: its config folder) and its model. Your **account** is your Slate sign-in, in Settings.

Order, always: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Antigravity, OpenCode, Gemini, Cline, Grok Build, Kiro, Qwen Code, Droid, Hermes Agent, Goose, Kilo Code, Auggie. The first six are measured end to end. The ten newest show *unverified* in [Features by Agent](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/tool-features.md) where no feature has run.

**A row never moves.** Turning a tool on or off changes only its mark and button; under **Connected** it keeps its row until you pick another filter.

| The tool is… | Mark or line | Button |
|---|---|---|
| Connected (Slate installed, workspace runs on it) | a small green dot at the right edge | **Disconnect**, on hover |
| On this Mac, not connected | none | **Connect** |
| Not on this Mac | none (greyed out) | **Install** |
| Slate installed, nothing runs on it | a grey line, *Not turned on · sessions not recorded* | **Remove Slate**, **Connect** on hover |
| Running here, Slate not installed, or last session used another Slate install | a grey line with an amber dot in front | **Connect** or **Disconnect** |
| Config could not be read | a grey line with an amber dot in front | **Connect** |

A state that needs you is said once: a small amber dot in front of a grey line. No pill repeats it, and every row is one height, so the dots line up.

### A tool that is not installed

The row reads *Not on this Mac* and has no **Connect**. **Install** shows the command with a copy button, a second way where there is one, how to sign in, what the account needs, and the vendor's guide link. Paste the command into Terminal, then press **Check again**; once Slate finds the CLI the row gets **Connect**. Slate never runs the command.

| Tool | Install | Sign in |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh \| bash` | run `claude` (needs a Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise or Console account) |
| Codex | `brew install --cask codex` | run `codex`, then **Sign in with ChatGPT** |
| Gemini | `brew install gemini-cli` | `GEMINI_API_KEY`, or a Gemini Code Assist licence. Personal Google accounts moved to Antigravity CLI |
| Cursor | `curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS \| bash` | `agent login` |
| OpenCode | `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install \| bash` | run `opencode`, then `/connect` |
| GitHub Copilot | `brew install --cask copilot-cli` | `copilot login` (needs a GitHub Copilot plan) |
| Antigravity | `curl -fsSL https://antigravity.google/cli/install.sh \| bash` | run `agy` (personal Google accounts sign in here) |
| Cline | `npm install -g cline` | `cline auth` |
| Grok Build | `curl -fsSL https://x.ai/cli/install.sh \| bash` | `grok login` |
| Kiro | `curl -fsSL https://cli.kiro.dev/install \| bash` | `kiro-cli login` |
| Qwen Code | `npm install -g @qwen-code/qwen-code` | run `qwen`, then `/auth` (needs a model provider) |
| Droid | `curl -fsSL https://app.factory.ai/cli \| sh` | run `droid` (needs a Factory account or `FACTORY_API_KEY`) |
| Hermes Agent | `curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh \| bash` | `hermes setup` |
| Goose | `curl -fsSL https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/releases/download/stable/download_cli.sh \| CONFIGURE=false bash` | `goose configure` |
| Kilo Code | `npm install -g @kilocode/cli` | `kilo auth login` |
| Auggie | `npm install -g @augmentcode/auggie` | `auggie login` (needs Node.js 20 or later and an Augment account) |

A turn that cannot find a tool's CLI names the same command.

### What Connect does

**Connect** installs Slate into the tool's config directory (sessions captured, workspace readable and writable) and records that this workspace runs on the tool (Home, automations and skills use it). **Disconnect** undoes both ([how](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect/how-slate-installs.md)).

* If only one half is true the row says so, behind an amber dot, and **Connect** repairs it: *Not turned on · sessions not recorded* (in grey: Slate records only the agents a workspace turns on, so this one is a leftover), or *Runs here, but Slate is not installed — sessions are not captured*.
* **Remove Slate** removes Slate from a tool this workspace does not run, leaving the workspace as is. The dialog names the config file Slate writes. Nothing is written until you connect, on first launch too.
* **Capture** switch (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini; the ten newest have none yet): off stops recording that tool's sessions, and it stays connected. Cursor has **Capture sessions** / **Stop capturing**; OpenCode has none. **Auto-capture** in Automations › [Built-in](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations.md) stops all.
* **A profile exists once per computer.** If another workspace runs the same tool on the same profile, the row says *Slate is installed here for Work* and offers no **Remove Slate** (it would break that workspace); disconnecting only stops this workspace, and says so first.
* **Claude Desktop** is connected with Claude Code, if installed; turning Claude Code off leaves it (one machine-wide setting). The **Codex** desktop app follows the Codex CLI's config.

**With no tool, a workspace cannot chat on Home, run automations, build widgets, learn memories or record activity.** The Automations, Memory, Activity, Widgets and Toolkit icons stay dimmed (hover says why; a click does nothing); Memory, Activity and Widgets open once they hold something. Home opens as a doc: the agents, what connecting one unlocks, **Open Connect**, and what works without AI (Tasks, Projects, Artifacts). Set a tool and all works with no reload.

**One place decides which tool runs.** Connect sets the workspace's tool; a group or project can override it. Home, the ⌘J panel, New session and automations show the tool that will run, linking here. With several tools in a project, Home and New session let you pick per turn. Sessions lists every AI session on the computer.

More: [MCP servers, profiles and models](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect/dialog.md); [checking it works](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect/how-slate-installs.md#checking-it-actually-works).

## Integrations

The **Integrations** tab holds this workspace's connected apps. Press **Connect**, approve on the app's sign-in page, and what you owe there shows in Tasks. List, states and per-app notes: [Integrations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect/integrations.md).

## Import

The **Import** tab brings in the projects your editors already know: one tile per editor, with one button for the tile picked. **Preview** lists the folders before anything is added. See [Import](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/import.md).

## What is not here

Settings holds **Account**, **Workspaces**, **Appearance**, **Terminal**, **Keyboard** and **About**. Moving, exporting and restoring a workspace file: **Settings → Workspaces**.

## See also

- [Connecting Your Agents](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/connecting.md): connecting by hand, and the MCP contract
- [Project environments](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio/cli-profiles.md): profiles and how a session is judged
- [Workspaces](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md): the boundary all of this turns on

---

# Import

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/import.md

Slate can bring in the projects you already work in, so Projects does not start empty.

Your agents' memory needs no import: Slate reads Claude Code's and Gemini CLI's own memory files on its own for every project you add, and keeps them up to date (see [Memory](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/map.md)). Importing notes, docs and past chats from other apps is not offered yet.

## The Import tab

**Connect › Import** shows one tile per editor, with its logo. A tile shows one short line: what was found, or how it stands. The button under the tiles is for the tile picked. Import picks the first editor found; click another tile to pick it.

| A tile says | Meaning | The button |
|---|---|---|
| A count, such as *4 projects* | Found on this Mac | **Preview** the editor's folders |
| *Already in Slate* | Every folder it lists is a project already | None |
| *Not on this Mac* | Slate can read it, and it is not here. The tile is drawn quieter | None |
| *Soon* | Slate cannot read it yet. The tile is drawn quieter | None |

## The editors

| Editor | Where Slate reads it |
|---|---|
| **VS Code**, **Cursor**, **Windsurf** | Each editor's list of folders you opened lately |
| **WebStorm**, **IntelliJ IDEA**, **PyCharm**, **GoLand**, **Rider**, **CLion**, **PhpStorm**, **RubyMine**, **RustRover**, **DataGrip** | Each IDE's `recentProjects.xml`, one tile per JetBrains IDE found. With none here, one **JetBrains IDEs** tile |
| **Zed** | Soon |

A project's own rules, skills and MCP servers are not imported here: open the project's [Toolkit](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio.md) and use its offer to bring them into `.slate/`.

## Projects from an editor

An editor's **Preview** lists the folders that editor opened, with a box to tick. Slate lists the folders it opened lately that are still on your Mac, are git projects, and are not a project in Slate yet, in any workspace. Folders you removed from Slate are not listed. Nothing becomes a project until you pick it. Adding one works the same as adding a folder anywhere else in Slate.

**Setup**'s **Project** step lists the same folders in its own folder list.

## Nothing is read until you choose

Slate first looks only for whether each editor is on your Mac and how many folders it lists. It reads the list only after you pick the editor, and shows it before anything is added. Slate never writes into an editor's files.

---

# A tool's dialog: MCP servers, profiles and models

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect/dialog.md

Click a tool in [Connect](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md) to open its dialog.

## MCP servers

The dialog lists the servers the tool declares, read from the profile this workspace runs it under. A tool this workspace does not run lists nothing and says to turn it on. With none, it says *Nothing besides Slate itself.* and **Add an MCP server** opens Toolkit's New dialog.

* A **gateway** (one server, many integrations) is one row. Its chevron opens what it carries. It has one **Sign in** and says when they stopped together.
* **Your Claude account**'s connectors are one row under Claude Code, the only tool that can use them.
* A server declared for every directory says **every workspace**.

| Server | States | Buttons |
|---|---|---|
| Read by Slate | **Live**, **Needs sign-in**, **Not turned on**, **Unavailable**, **Not read yet** (a failure says when it last worked) | **Turn on**; **Let an agent read it**, or **Read with Claude Code** when only your Claude account reaches it |
| Not read by Slate | What the tool last reported: **Connected in Claude Code**, **Needs sign-in in Claude Code**, **Claude Code could not connect**. Neither spoke: **Set up, not checked** | none |

**Sign in** uses the sign-in Tasks uses for a tool Slate reads. For a server only an agent reaches, it runs that tool's own login. **Refresh** and any waiting sign-in sit above the list.

## Profiles

A tool's servers, sign-in and history live in a **config directory**, set by `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `GEMINI_CLI_HOME`, `CODEX_HOME`, `CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR`, `COPILOT_HOME` or the variable in each newer tool's record. Antigravity, Auggie, Kilo Code and OpenCode have none, so no profile to choose.

Pick the **Profile** this workspace uses, or **Add** one by naming it and its config folder.

* For Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, the add form offers config folders already in your home folder (such as `~/.claude-work`) as buttons under **Found here**. Gemini offers none: its variable names a replacement home folder.
* **Choose folder…** picks any other. A missing path is fine: the tool creates it on sign-in.
* Pick before connecting: the profile decides where Slate is installed.
* **Its own default** is the tool's built-in folder (`~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, …). A `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `CODEX_HOME` set in your shell is not followed for it: name that folder as a profile instead. Slate does follow `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_DATA_HOME` and `OPENCODE_CONFIG`.
* A tool kept only under a profile or its own variable's folder counts as installed. Gemini CLI and Antigravity share `~/.gemini`; each is told apart by the files only it writes.
* **Cursor:** `CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR` moves only its sign-in. `cursor-agent` reads servers, hooks and plugins from `~/.cursor` and writes history there (or where `CURSOR_DATA_DIR` says) for every profile. Slate writes them once for all Cursor profiles. Turning one profile off leaves them while another connected Cursor profile uses them.

Why two workspaces on one profile share its sign-in: [Project environments](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio/cli-profiles.md).

## Models

The model list shows once this workspace runs the tool. On **Its own default**, Slate passes no model and the CLI picks. **Make default** marks the tool used when nothing more specific is named, with a **default** badge. A group or standalone project can override any of it.

---

# How Slate installs into a tool

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect/how-slate-installs.md

Connecting installs Slate once, by plugin or config hooks, plus one MCP entry. See [Connect](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md).

## Contents

- [Two ways in, one at a time](#two-ways-in-one-at-a-time)
- [What Slate writes into a config](#what-slate-writes-into-a-config)
- [What you see in a Claude Code session](#what-you-see-in-a-claude-code-session)
- [Four commands in every session](#four-commands-in-every-session)
- [What turning a tool off puts back](#what-turning-a-tool-off-puts-back)
- [Checking it actually works](#checking-it-actually-works)

## Two ways in, one at a time

A **plugin** is a directory the tool owns, with five hooks (six for Claude Code) and four slash commands. The tool's own uninstall removes it all. The MCP server is separate: every tool reaches it through one `slate` entry in its config.

* OpenCode and GitHub Copilot have no plugin route, so hooks go into their config. So for Claude Code, Gemini and Cursor when the plugin cannot be installed or run.
* Codex takes no config hooks. Without its plugin it keeps only the MCP entry.

**The MCP entry** is a URL on the running app (`http://127.0.0.1:47366/mcp`; the port follows the Mac user, 47366 for the first account) with Slate's private key in a header (ADR 0106). No session starts its own process. Slate writes the entry itself, readable by you only. Claude Desktop and VS Code keep a stdio entry running `slate-mcp`. VS Code's entry goes into each of VS Code, VS Code Insiders and VSCodium that is installed, and into the own `mcp.json` of every VS Code profile; on Linux their folders follow `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`. A profile made after you connect gets the entry when VS Code is next turned on in Connect. With Slate closed the tool lists the server as failed and the session-start hook says why: open Slate, start a new session.

| Tool | Turning it on |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | installs the plugin |
| Codex | installs the plugin |
| Gemini | installs the plugin, as a Gemini extension |
| Cursor | installs the plugin, as a link in Cursor's local plugins folder |
| OpenCode | writes one plugin module and names it in OpenCode's config (OpenCode loads a module, not a directory) |
| GitHub Copilot | writes the `slate` entry into `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` and hooks into `~/.copilot/hooks/slate.json`, a file of its own |
| The ten newest tools | write the `slate` entry into the tool's own MCP config (the file is in the tool's record in `agentsAndHosts.json`). Grok Build, Droid, Hermes Agent and Auggie also get hooks; Antigravity, Kiro, Cline and Goose get none yet |

* **Node 24 or newer** is needed for the plugin. Without it, tools with a config route use that. If Node disappears, Slate removes the plugin rather than leave a server that cannot start. Slate asks your shell once per launch where `node` is (an app opened from Finder has no shell PATH), which finds fnm, nvm, volta and asdf.
* **Only from where Slate lives.** Opened straight from the disk image, or from the temporary copy macOS runs a downloaded app from, Slate installs no plugin: that path is gone once the app moves, and the tool would keep a dead link. The config route carries capture until Slate runs from Applications (or any folder or drive it was copied to); a registration left from such a copy is recognised as Slate's and replaced then.
* **Exactly one way.** Each launch checks every tool and profile: with the plugin installed, old hooks are removed; a connected tool with neither gets back what it can have (else everything runs twice). Slate decides from its record of what it installed per profile: a matching profile gets no writes, an unrecorded one is left alone unless you connected it, and a connected profile that lost Slate is connected again. Only turning it off in Connect keeps it off. If Slate's record, or its list of connected or turned-off profiles, cannot be read (cut short, or written by a newer Slate), that launch changes nothing from it: no profile is connected again, no kept original is removed, the file stays as it is with a copy beside it (`.corrupt`), and Disconnect of a profile that shares its files with another (Cursor) is refused until the file is fixed or removed.
* **Asking the tool first.** Whether the plugin is installed, and where from, is asked of the tool's own list command when it has one: `claude plugin list --json`, `codex plugin list --json` and `gemini extensions list -o json`. Slate reads the tool's files only when the command is missing, fails, or does not name the plugin, and writes a warning to `slate.log` when one of those files is not in a form it reads. Connect re-registers a `slate` MCP entry that is already there when the tool's config file holds one; the tool's error text is not read.
* **What actually ran.** The MCP server records tool, account and Slate when a tool starts it. The tool's dialog shows what its last session ran: this Slate and when; one started before this Slate was built (the next session runs this one); or another Slate install, named (also on the row, behind an amber dot). A dev checkout's server run from its source counts as this Slate. The HTTP entry always reaches the running Slate; a host's stdio entry keeps the server it started with.

## What Slate writes into a config

On the config route, connecting writes hooks into `~/.claude/settings.json`, `~/.gemini/settings.json`, `~/.cursor/hooks.json`, `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` and `~/.copilot/hooks/slate.json` (under a profile, that profile's folder). These files are **global**: they apply to every project on the machine.

* One entry per event: five for Gemini and GitHub Copilot, six for Claude Code and Cursor.
* Claude Code's sixth runs after a RemoteTrigger or Bash call and records a cloud session it started (see [Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/cloud.md#cloud-sessions)).
* Cursor's sixth is a prompt hook applying the account rule of the folder you are in.
* OpenCode gets one plugin module with two events.

Every entry names one script Slate rewrites on each launch in its data directory. If it cannot find what to run it exits 0 silently. Removing it is safe.

## What you see in a Claude Code session

Claude Code prints one line when Slate loads or captures memory. Each prints at most once per session. A session with nothing to load says nothing. The lines are Claude Code only; the interruption goes to Cursor, Gemini and others in the form each reads.

| When | What prints |
|---|---|
| Session starts | `Slate · <branch> · 5 memories, 1 parked branch, 3 sessions` (a count of 0 is left out) |
| Session saves memory | `Slate · saved 3 memories from this session · <page>`, and a desktop notification |
| Stop interrupted | `Stop hook feedback: Slate · this session did real work but saved nothing yet.` Or, after a likely correction, `Slate · this looked like a correction (“no, …”). If it was, save the lesson…`. Two lines at most, no doc id; the model then ends with one short line |
| Plan made, not saved | `Stop hook feedback: Slate · you made a plan. Ask the user whether to save it as a Plan doc in Slate…`, then the model asks you with a click |

## Four commands in every session

The plugin adds these to the `/` menu (type `/slate` in Claude Code):

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/slate:brief` | What Slate knows about this project, in a few lines |
| `/slate:recall <what>` | Search your memory, and check any code it cites |
| `/slate:remember <fact>` | Save one memory, in your words |
| `/slate:open` | Open this branch's doc in the Slate app |

## What turning a tool off puts back

Slate records what each file held before its first write. On disconnect, a file only Slate changed goes back to those bytes, and a file Slate created is removed. If you or the tool edited it after Slate, only Slate's parts are removed.

If disconnect fails it says so, naming whichever of the plugin and the old hooks did not come out (hooks first, since they keep running). For a stuck plugin it gives the terminal command, such as `codex plugin remove slate@slate`. Slate still remembers you turned the tool off, so the next launch does not put it back.

## Checking it actually works

Plugin hooks and the MCP server run the Slate the app is running (a plugin's own copy is used only without the app), so a tool that caches plugins by version (Codex) still gets today's Slate. Every release is a new plugin version, refreshed next launch. A broken tool looks like one nobody used, so run:

```
"$HOME/Library/Application Support/app.slate.workspace/hooks/slate-hook" doctor
```

One line per tool. A tool with no hooks says `not connected`. Otherwise:

| Line | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n hook(s) OK · last session <when>` | Working. |
| `n BROKEN of m` | A hook cannot run; the lines under it say why and name the file. Slate's fault. Exits with an error code. |
| `n hook(s) OK · no session recorded yet` | Wiring is sound; something outside Slate stops it: tool unused since connecting, hooks need approving once, or the account cannot sign in. |

Two silent causes:

* **Codex runs no plugin hook until you trust it.** Until you clear the hook-trust step, `codex plugin list` says `installed, enabled` while nothing runs.
* **Gemini CLI cannot sign in on a personal Google account** (`IneligibleTierError`). Use an API key or a Code Assist licence.

For the first kind, the Activity card **Do sessions save memory?** (off by default) compares sessions the tool wrote here in the last 7 days with those Slate's hooks recorded. When the tool wrote at least 3 and fewer than half were recorded, it says so, e.g. "Codex ran 9 sessions in the last 7 days and Slate saw 1. Its sessions got no memory from Slate and saved none.", with the fix.

---

# Integrations

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect/integrations.md

The **Integrations** tab in [Connect](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md) holds this workspace's apps. Press **Connect**, approve Slate on the app's own sign-in page, and what you owe there shows in Tasks. No agent is involved.

## The list

One row per integration: its logo and name. A connected app in its normal state is that one line and one small green dot. **Disconnect** shows when you point at the row, and the hover text says what Slate reads and when it last synced. A second line shows only when something differs: **Sign in again so Slate can keep reading it.**, **Slate could not reach it.**, or a note that your admin may have to allow Slate first. A tool's own error text stays out of the row. Connectable apps come first, then **Coming soon**.

* **Official-server sign-in:** **GitHub** (through your `gh`), **Jira**, **GitLab.com**, **Notion**, **Trello**, **ClickUp**, **Linear**, **Mattermost** (your own server), **monday.com**, **Basecamp**, **Plane** (Plane Cloud), **Shortcut**, **Todoist**.
* **Pasted token:** **Bitbucket Cloud**, **Gitea** (and Forgejo), **Gerrit**, **YouTrack**, **Zulip**, **Rocket.Chat**.
* Order: most used first by the Stack Overflow Developer Survey's share, then apps it omits, A to Z.
* **Coming soon**, each with its reason: Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord, Google Chat, Gmail, Outlook and Asana say *Needs Slate's own* app of that vendor (not registered). Azure DevOps and Zoom say *No server Slate can sign in to yet*.
* **Issues**, **Reviews** and **Messages** narrow the grid to apps shown in that group of Tasks (mail is under Messages), with counts. **Find an integration** searches.
* An app hidden from Tasks sits under the grid as **Hidden from Tasks**, with **Show**.
* **Another app**, the last tile, connects any MCP server: name, https address, sign in.

## States and behaviour

| Case | What happens |
|---|---|
| GitHub | **Connect** turns on reading through `gh`. A signed-in `gh` alone reads nothing. |
| Sign-in ended (new password, admin removed access) | **Needs sign-in**, **Sign in again**. The sign-in is Slate's own, stays on this computer, and survives restart and update. An agent's server reading the same app never makes it look signed in. |
| App refuses reads by a setting | **Unavailable** with the change needed or the app's words. GitLab: "GitLab blocks Slate until you turn on “Allow connection to GitLab” in a GitLab group you own." |
| Slate cannot read it yet | **Not read yet**; a logo under **Not reading yet** in Tasks, not a 0. Slate teaches itself once: **Learning how to read your tasks in Notion…** while your agent works it out through Slate's connection; the answer is kept. If nothing is found: **Could not find your tasks in Notion.** with **Try again**. This is how Notion is read: each workspace keeps tasks in its own database. |
| **Disconnect** | Forgets the sign-in or token. Tasks leave at the next sync, unless an agent's declared server still reads the app. |
| Same app via an agent's server | Read here only, so a task never comes from two places. |

## Per-app notes

* **Jira**, **Trello:** their admin may have to allow Slate before it connects (Atlassian controls which apps connect; Trello follows).
* **Mattermost:** **Connect** asks for the server address (`https://chat.example.com`) and signs in at the Agents plugin's MCP server, `/plugins/mattermost-ai/mcp-server/mcp`. The admin must first enable that server and OAuth dynamic client registration (Enterprise plan up). The tile then shows the address and replaces the plain tile.
* **Pasted-token apps:** **Connect** opens a form with the server address (not Bitbucket), the account name the app wants (Zulip email, Gerrit username, Rocket.Chat user ID) and the token, with where to make it and which read-only permissions to tick. Slate asks the app who owns the token before keeping it; a refused token is not kept and the form says why. The token stays on this computer in a file only your user can read. If refused later: **Needs sign-in**, **Paste a new token**. Zulip and Rocket.Chat show only messages naming something this workspace works on.

## Agents read what you connect

An app connected through its own server (not a pasted token) is readable from any AI session in this workspace, with no setup: `connected_tools` and `read_connected` use Slate's sign-in while Slate is open. Only reading tools are offered. See [Connected MCP tools](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/connected-tools.md).

---

# Connected MCP Tools

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/connected-tools.md

Home reaches whatever MCP servers your agent's CLI can reach. This guide covers that direction, with Slate as the client; for the other, see [Slate as an MCP Server](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server.md).

## Where servers come from

Home keeps no server list. The CLI loads the servers in its own config (the account's and the project directory's) and reports which connected. [Connect → Agents](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md) sets the account a tool runs under (a group or project may override it); edit its servers where the CLI keeps its config. The top bar's **tools** chip shows the count the CLI reported, names on hover, *· 1 failed* in amber, and keeps it after the turn ([details](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/approvals.md#what-home-shows-about-the-agent)).

## Apps you connected in Slate

An app connected in [Connect → Integrations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md#integrations) (Linear, Notion, Jira…) is readable from every session, even when the tool's config has no server for it, while Slate is open. `connected_tools` lists the apps and their read-only tools; `read_connected` reads through one with Slate's own sign-in. Tools that write are never offered. See [Slate's MCP tools](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tools.md#apps-you-connected-in-slate).

See also: [Curated MCP Commands](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/mcp-commands.md), [Home](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent.md).

---

# Workspaces

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md

A workspace is one SQLite file on your machine holding its own docs, memory, activity, artifacts and search. Switch into one and the whole app is in it. Every workspace starts private; share one and everything in it belongs to its members (nothing is marked per doc).

## Personal, and the ones you share

**Personal** is the starting workspace and the only one that fills by itself: captured sessions, git repositories with no project doc, cross-project notes. It cannot be left or removed.

Any workspace, Personal included, can be shared:

1. Click its row in **Settings → Workspaces**.
2. Use its **Sharing** switch.
3. Agree to the count shown: docs, memories, activity rows and artifacts to publish.

Switching off withdraws them (they were readable in between).

**Sharing needs the Team plan** (coming soon); all else is free, including any number of private workspaces. On Free the switch is refused with a message saying so. Accounts that already shared keep sharing free until Team ships. Turning sharing off is always allowed.

**The switcher** is at the top of the rail: Slate's mark, grey on the rail; in the open switcher each workspace's mark wears its own colour, beside its name. Shared = small people mark, failed sync = warning, read-only = padlock. Open rows say **Shared** or **Private**.

**⌘\`** next workspace, **⌘~** previous; with only Personal, nothing. Switching back restores the same doc, tab strip and rail section. A workspace not yet opened in this window opens on Home. Nothing carries over.

## What follows a switch

Per workspace: open tabs, favourites, recents, expanded sections, what Home is scoped to, automations (they belong to a group or project doc). What you were still typing when you switched, a title or a doc's text, is saved in the workspace you left. The same everywhere, kept in `machine.db`: theme, sidebar and rail widths, running AI sessions, the CLI accounts your tools use.

## Using it

- **Sign in**: **Settings → Account**, GitHub. **Make, share, rename, recolour, leave, remove**: **Settings → Workspaces** (a private one renames at once; inviting needs it shared; Personal keeps its name; a workspace you belong to but have not set up here shows **Add here**). **Switch**: the switcher, whose last row **Manage workspaces…** opens Settings → Workspaces.
- **Move a doc in**: right-click or ⋯, **Move to <workspace>** ([sharing](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces/sharing.md)). Others' docs sit in your tree with their avatar, read-only.
- **Ask your AI**: [`recall_workspaces` and `workspace_doc`](../mcp-server/tools.md) search every workspace you belong to, including ones not set up here; `recall` stays in the working directory's workspace.

## How a shared workspace stays in step

Sync runs every 2 minutes and at startup. **Sync now** (Settings → Workspaces) runs it at once and reports what moved. After a failure the retry waits 2, 4, 8… minutes up to 1 hour; a success resets. With no shared workspace it does nothing.

- Only changed rows are sent (hash of exactly the published fields); nothing new costs one query.
- The same comparison **withdraws**: a row the cloud holds that your replica lacks (in Trash, removed for good, moved to another workspace) is tombstoned upstream and every member's copy goes on their next pull. A store's first pass (new Mac, reinstall) withdraws nothing and pulls your rows down first. After that, a Mac withdraws only a row it once held: something you wrote on your other Mac since this one last synced is not in its replica yet, and arrives instead of being withdrawn. A doc you moved to Trash on one Mac is not published again by your other Mac. The withdrawal records which Mac wrote it, and your other Mac moves just that doc to its own Trash on its next sync (a doc inside it that you moved elsewhere stays). It does this once per withdrawal: if you then restore the doc from the Trash on that Mac, it stays restored and is published again. Memories and artifacts follow the same rule. A withdrawal that names no Mac (from Stop sharing, or older than this rule) is sent again after you turn sharing on again, or when you restore a doc that this Mac had already seen gone; a doc restored before that Mac's first sync after the update is not sent until then. A sync pass checks again, right before each write, that the workspace is still shared, so pressing Stop sharing while a pass runs cannot put the work back.
- Offline works: you are the only writer of your rows, so queue order does not matter.

## What actually leaves your machine

Everything in a shared workspace is for its members, except what is specific to your machine:

| Sent | Not sent |
| --- | --- |
| Doc title, block content and plain text for the cloud index, as written. A captured AI session's doc is never sent | The rest of `properties` (typed and captured metadata, including a project's folder path) |
| `doc_type`, parent link, your timestamps, the doc's branch label (a branch name, from `properties`) | `position`, the sibling order |
| Memories anchored to a doc in the workspace: sentence, kind, subject, confidence, a lesson's trigger, the doc learned on | A memory's reasoning body and source reference. Also never: a memory hidden from sessions, a global memory (no doc), one Slate no longer believes, one an app saved |
| Git activity: commits and branch events with branch, commit subject (never the rest of the message) and normalised git remote (so a teammate's checkout at another path matches) | A commit message body, the activity payload (file paths, diff stats, counts) and `activity.repo`, the absolute path |
| Artifacts: title, kind, description, agent, the doc made under, newest version | Older versions |
| That a session happened, with branch and time | Everything else: transcript, tool, session id, summary |
| Your display name, email, avatar from the sign-in provider | Anything in a workspace you have not shared |

Postgres enforces the activity kind list with a `CHECK` constraint, not the client.

> **Warning:** The right column withholds fields, not words. A doc body and a memory's sentence go up as written; a path typed in a doc or recorded by an agent in a decision goes up with the row. Withheld are the structured places a path is held: `properties` and the absolute git repository path on a commit.

Every workspace, Personal included, keeps an append-only log in its own store: docs created, renamed, moved, trashed, removed; joins; syncs that moved something; withdrawals. Two SQLite triggers block change or removal for 400 days; startup then removes it and activity rows that old.

## Leaving, erasing, and being removed

| Action | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| **Stop sharing** | Publishing stops; everything you authored is withdrawn from the cloud and every member's copy on their next sync. Slate first counts docs, memories, activity rows and artifacts; the button reads **Stop sharing and erase my work**. The store stays here and keeps working. Your other Macs stop sharing it too, on their next sync, and withdraw anything they had sent meanwhile; on those Macs it stays off until you share it there. Share again and the next sync publishes it as it then stands. The cloud keeps a blank row per item saying it existed; as sole member, Slate removes those too |
| **Leave** | Shared: **Leave “…” and end my access** removes your seat in the cloud workspace first, then this Mac's copy (a copy is kept in `backups/`, named `left-…`). You can no longer read what the workspace holds, and what you published stays for its members; **Erase my work** takes it back. If you are the only owner, Leave is refused: make someone else an owner first. If you are offline or signed out, Leave is refused and nothing changes. **Remove from this Mac** keeps your seat and only removes the copy here. Never shared (no other copy): **Delete workspace forever**, confirm **Delete “…” forever, with everything in it**; export from **Storage** first. If the copy fails or a connected agent still has it open, nothing is removed. Personal cannot be left |
| **Erase my work** | Every row you authored is tombstoned upstream and every member's replica drops it on next pull. Final: sharing again does not restore it (the Article 17 request). Editors and the owner only; a viewer or former member is refused with the reason |
| **Someone removes you, or the owner removes the workspace for good** | Row Level Security stops answering; your replica becomes read-only. What you read stays readable and exportable; removing it is your decision |

Personal is never marked read-only (every window falls back to it). If it is shared and its cloud side goes away, sync fails; **Stop sharing** is the way out.

See also: [Working in a Shared Workspace](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces/sharing.md), [Workspaces & Invites](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces/workspaces-and-invites.md), [Privacy & Security](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security.md).

---

# Working in a Shared Workspace

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces/sharing.md

Everything in a shared workspace is the team's; there is no "publish this doc" button. Keep work private in a workspace you have not shared.

A doc you create there is shared at once, as is a decision your AI records, and a commit in a git repository the workspace owns lands in its activity feed. A captured AI session's doc is never published, and neither is a plan captured from a session in plan mode: it stays on this Mac. Sharing needs **Team** (coming soon); accounts that already shared keep it free until Team ships.

## Getting existing work in

Groups and projects are moved, not copied. Right-click in the sidebar or use ⋯ in the header, **Move to <workspace>**; Slate first says how many docs move and who can read them. Moving out works the same.

- **Whole subtree**: a group takes its projects; a project takes its branches and their plans and designs.
- **Ids kept**: a published doc keeps its cloud rows.
- **Properties come**: the folder path routes the git repository to the workspace.
- **Memory comes**: memories anchored to the moved docs. A move refuses to carry one anchored to no doc.
- **Lands at top level**; its old parent stays behind.
- **Refuses what is not yours**: a subtree with anyone else's docs, memory or activity, or a move where either workspace is read-only for you. Nothing is copied or removed.

Order is read, write, remove. No transaction spans two SQLite files, so a failure between write and remove leaves the docs in both workspaces; re-run.

**One folder, one workspace.** A folder decides where the work done in it goes, so it belongs to one workspace on your Mac. Adding a folder that another workspace already holds is refused, and the message names that workspace: move the project instead. If two workspaces still both have a project on the same folder, the one holding it keeps it, and Personal always wins, so the work stays private.

## Read-only, and why there is no merge

Each doc has one writer, its author. A teammate's doc opens with a read-only editor and a line giving the reason:

| Reason | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Another author** | A teammate wrote it (named). Their edits reach you; yours would not reach them |
| **Workspace is read-only** | Removed upstream, or you were removed. Everything stays readable and exportable |

With one writer per row there are no version columns, 409 handling or conflict resolution. Your manual sibling order is not published; on a teammate's machine your docs arrive in pull order.

**You on two Macs.** Each Mac remembers the version of your doc it last saw in the workspace. When your other Mac published a newer version, this one takes it, and never sends its older copy over it. If you edited the same doc on both Macs before either synced, the later edit wins (by when you made it, not when it reached the cloud) and the other is kept beside it as "<title> (copy from this Mac)". Docs, memories and artifacts all work this way. One exception: a doc or memory whose published copy has words of a hidden memory blanked out is not taken, so the words this Mac holds are never replaced; it stays as it is until you edit it here.

**Who wrote what** (shared workspaces only):

- Sidebar: a teammate's doc shows their picture at the row end; yours show none.
- Under the title: "Written by you" or "Written by Sam".
- Memory: a teammate's shows their name where yours shows "you".

Names come from member profiles, kept locally and refreshed at app start and when you open Members in Settings, so docs stay signed offline. An unlooked-up member shows as "A teammate".

## Removals travel as tombstones

A removal is a **tombstone**: a row saying "gone", and when. When a teammate's doc is removed, the pull re-parents your surviving children to the workspace root first; **Sync now** reports that count as `reparented`. A tombstone removes only its author's row: Trashing your doc leaves a teammate's doc under it; deleting yours forever moves theirs, with everything under it, up to your doc's parent.

## Memory

A memory (decision, `fact`, preference or state saved by `remember` or `record_decision`) is anchored to a doc; if that doc is in a shared workspace, the memory is the workspace's. What travels: [What actually leaves your machine](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md#what-actually-leaves-your-machine). Superseding a decision withdraws the old one on the next pass.

## Artifacts

An artifact published in a shared workspace belongs to it and every member sees it in **Artifacts**. Only you can publish a new version, rename or delete it forever; a teammate's shows who wrote it and its menu offers only Copy and Open in browser. Only the newest version travels; members keep versions they received. Removal withdraws it from everyone on the next sync.

## Finding a teammate's memory from your checkout

You and a colleague clone one git repository to different folders, and their memories hang on docs recording a path missing on your machine. So Slate identifies a git repository by its **git remote**, normalised to `host/owner/repo`; when recall finds no stored path for your checkout it finds the doc recording the same remote.

- Only the remote counts; a checkout with no fetchable remote gets nothing.
- Never by name: two unrelated git repositories called `site` share nothing.
- Any clone form: `git@github.com:Acme/Site.git` and `https://github.com/acme/site` are one git repository (key lower-cased, credentials stripped).

See also: [Workspaces](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md), [Workspaces & Invites](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces/workspaces-and-invites.md), [Privacy & Security](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security.md).

---

# Workspaces & Invites

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces/workspaces-and-invites.md

Sign-in, plans, roles, invitations, creating a workspace, deleting it forever, and removing people.

## Signing in

1. **Settings → Account**.
2. Sign in with **GitHub** (the only provider). Your system browser opens.
3. After approval the provider returns to a loopback address on Slate's local server, which does the code exchange: no code, token or password passes through the UI.

The session is in `cloud-session.json`, a `0600` file in the app-data folder, never in a database, so exporting a workspace cannot hand over a refresh token. First sign-in creates a **personal account** (everyone signs in on first launch, ADR 0103). After that Personal works offline and never syncs until shared.

**Settings → Account** shows who you are and **Sign out**, then **Plan**:

- **Free**: everything Slate does on this Mac; your plan unless you have early access.
- **Team**: sharing a workspace with your team; coming soon, no price. **Tell me when it's ready** records interest; the button then reads **We'll email you**. With early access: **Early access**.

Work stays on this Mac on every plan; the account holds only who you are and your plan.

**Another account on the same Mac.** Each shared workspace belongs to the account that joined it on this Mac. Signed in with a different account, Slate does not list or sync it, and does not mark it read-only. Sign in with its account again and it is back as you left it. Personal belongs to the Mac, whoever is signed in.

**Sharing is Team.** On Free a new workspace is local only: the switch is off and disabled with **Team · coming soon** and the same button. An already-shared workspace can still be turned off. With early access sharing works.

## Two tiers

| Tier | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Account** | Billing and organisation: a company or one person. Roles: `owner`, `admin`, `member` |
| **Workspace** | One store, one audience, inside an account. Roles: `owner`, `editor`, `viewer` |

Workspace membership is independent of account membership (a contractor gets one workspace, not the company). An account owner reaches a workspace in the account without being added. Settings → Workspaces lists every workspace you belong to, across accounts.

## What a role controls

| Role | Read | Write docs | Invite, remove, rename | Grant owner, delete workspace forever |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `owner` | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| `editor` | yes | yes | no | no |
| `viewer` | yes | **no** | no | no |

The account's owner can do all a workspace owner can; account admins can invite, remove and rename only. Only a workspace owner or the account's owner can make, change or remove an owner, or delete the workspace forever; an account admin cannot make themselves owner (database-enforced). A role does not decide whose docs you may edit: author-only for everyone.

> **Note:** **A viewer's replica is read-only on their machine too.** The role is stored locally and writes (including a memory you or an agent saves) are refused where made, with a line saying an editor or owner can change it; a viewer's machine does not push. Accepting an invitation fetches the role at once. Until fetched (offline, signed out, a machine that joined earlier) the workspace counts as writable, so offline use works; the cloud has the last word. **A role change reaches the machine on the next sync pass, not the next launch.** A demoted editor stops pushing at once. The workspace shows "You can only read this workspace now." It is not a failure, so syncing does not slow down and teammates' work still arrives.

## Inviting someone

1. **Settings → Workspaces**, click the workspace's row.
2. **Members**: type an email, **Create invitation** (editor role).
3. Tell them (below); Slate sends no email.

An invitation is a membership addressed by email (a user id exists only after someone signs in). The address is stored lower-cased and trimmed, database-enforced, so it matches a login. It matches only an address the sign-in provider confirmed; Google and GitHub confirm it when the account is made. Pending invitations are listed with members and can be revoked before claimed.

**Accepting is explicit.** A banner at the top of the app, on any screen, names the workspace, inviter and role with **Accept** and **Decline**. Accepting sets up the replica and the workspace appears in the switcher. A declined invitation stays declined until re-invited. The only way into a workspace is an invitation the person accepts; the database refuses an admin who tries to add someone directly, to a workspace or to its account.

**Telling them.** Each pending row has:

| Action | Does |
| --- | --- |
| **Email** | Opens your mail app with the invitation addressed and written; you send it |
| **Copy** | Copies the same message for Slack, Teams or elsewhere |

The message names the workspace and inviter, links to where Slate installs from, and states the exact address the invitation is tied to (membership is claimed by email, so another account would find nothing).

## Creating a workspace, and deleting one forever

**New workspace** (Settings → Workspaces): name, colour, whether to share. **Create workspace**. Sharing starts on and needs sign-in; off, it is a local file, shareable later. A shared one belongs to your account, you are first member, its replica is set up on creation. **Sync now** sits beside it and reports what moved; results show as a status note under the buttons.

**Colour** is used for its mark in the switcher's list and in its settings, always beside its name. Nine, in the order new workspaces get them: Cobalt, Lagoon, Iris, Silver, Orchid, Fjord, Heather, Wisteria, Graphite. The rail's tabs and the Sessions screen wear Slate's own green, not a workspace's colour. Stored on your machine, not the shared row: everyone keeps their own and anyone can recolour whatever their role.

**Delete workspace forever** (**General** in the workspace dialog) removes every doc everyone put there, for every member, without notice; authors keep what they moved back out. Only a workspace owner or the account's owner; asks twice; nothing for anyone else. Every member's Mac learns of it on its next sync and removes what teammates published there; what a person wrote themselves stays on their Mac, and the store is marked read-only and stops sharing, so you can copy your own work out. A person who was removed before it was deleted forever keeps the read-only copy described below: only people who were members when it was deleted forever are told.

## Removing someone

Read access ends on their next request (Row Level Security decides every query). Their machine checks membership on every sync pass, about every two minutes. It marks the replica read-only on the next pass: they can read and export what is on disk; nothing goes up or arrives. Docs they authored stay. If the workspace is deleted forever later, their Mac is not told, because they were no longer a member: the copy stays read-only. **Erase my work** no longer works for them: the cloud refuses a former member, and Slate says so instead of reporting the work erased. The workspace owner removes it for them.

See also: [Workspaces](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md), [Working in a Shared Workspace](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces/sharing.md), [Privacy & Security](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security.md).

---

# Search & Command Palette

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/search.md

Press **⌘K** anywhere. One input runs a command, jumps to a doc, or searches your workspace: doc titles and bodies, tasks, memories, reports, artifacts and captured AI sessions ([Session Capture](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/session-capture.md)).

Search uses **SQLite FTS5**, an index in the same local file as your content; it never leaves the machine.

⌘K searches **your** workspace only. What others shared is searched by opening [Workspaces](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md), or by an agent calling `recall_workspaces`. The palette never blends private and shared results.

### What ⌘K lists

With nothing typed: **Open tabs**, **Live sessions**, **Recent**, **Favorites**, then five places under **Quick navigation**.

Typed, the order is: **Actions** (commands whose name holds the text), open tabs, **Go to** (places and a few Settings sections), sessions, files, **Docs**, **Tasks** (to-dos and tickets; open in Tasks), **Memories** (open in Memory), **Reports**, **Artifacts**. Loose command matches come last, under **More actions**.

Files come from the open workspace's projects only. When git does not answer for a checkout (a large checkout read cold, past the 5 s limit), the palette names that checkout under the results instead of showing **No matches**; the other checkouts still answer, and a checkout read before keeps its last file list. A doc row shows its parent path. A doc in Trash is marked **In Trash** and opens read-only, with **Restore**.

### Text inside files — ⌘⇧F

**⌘⇧F** (*Search docs and files*) searches doc bodies, then the text inside files of every project and worktree in the open workspace. A file hit is the matching line with file and line number, grouped by checkout and branch; Enter opens the file read-only at that line.

The query starts at three characters. It is plain text, not a pattern, and ignores case. Ignored and binary files are skipped; uncommitted files an agent wrote are included. At most 200 lines are found, and the palette shows the first 30. A checkout git could not search is named under the results, as in ⌘K.

### Sessions in ⌘K

Every live AI session on the machine is a row. With nothing typed, up to five show under **Live sessions**, those waiting on you first. Typed, up to four match by title, project, branch or tool (`fix/` finds the agent on that branch). Enter opens it as a chip in the Sessions tab strip: the live terminal where Slate can attach or branch, the transcript where it cannot. On a doc that stands for a folder, **Start a session here** launches on the project's default tool. **Second session here**, **Continue in a copy**, Stop and the resume command are on the session's own header.

### Web pages in ⌘K

Type a web address and the first row is **Open in Slate**, which opens it in Slate's own browser as a tab. It accepts a full address (`https://example.com/docs`), a local server with port (`localhost:3000`), a bare domain (`example.com`, opened over https) and the full path to an HTML file (`/srv/site/index.html`). Ordinary words, file names such as `index.html` and versions such as `v1.2` go to normal search.

The tab is read-only: back, forward, reload, an address bar, a button to open the web page outside Slate. Back and forward follow addresses typed in the bar, not clicked links. Sites that refuse to show inside another app get a note and your browser. Your browser's sign-ins do not carry over.

A local HTML file is served from its folder on a private local port, so scripts, styles and images load; dot-names (`.env`, `.git`) below it are never served, and the HTML page may connect nowhere but that folder. Slate keeps the 16 most recently used folders served; an older one is closed and served again when you open it again. A local server address in a session's messages or terminal opens here too, beside the session.

## The cheatsheet

Press **`?`** for the shortcuts of the current context. The palette opens it too, as **Keyboard shortcuts**. Tooltips read the same list, so they follow a key you rebind. Every key is in [Keyboard shortcuts](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/shortcuts.md).

## Rebindable shortcuts

**Settings → Keyboard** lists every command the palette knows; click a key to record a new one. See [Rebind a shortcut](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/shortcuts.md#rebind-a-shortcut).

## The sidebar

The icons down the left edge are always there; beside them is the sidebar, the list for the current section, pinned or hidden (remembered). With it hidden, resting the pointer on an icon floats that section's list over the doc without moving it; another icon changes the list; moving away, Escape or a click elsewhere slides it back. With it pinned, an icon shows only its name.

Choosing a section never pins or hides the sidebar. Three things do: clicking the icon of the section you are already in, **⌘\\**, and the sidebar button at the top of the list. While a list floats, **⌘\\** and that button pin it and take you to its section.

Every icon with a list works this way, Activity's panel (project picker, range, saved views) included. Picking a conversation from the floating Home list opens it in Home. Trash has no list, so it shows only its name.

### The rail

Top to bottom: **Sessions** first, on its own tile: every AI session on this computer as an orbit, one dot per session: lime while it works, amber while it waits on you. When a session starts, stops, or starts or stops waiting on you, the dots go once round. A working dot breathes; a waiting one grows and stays larger; otherwise they hold still.

A short line separates Sessions from **the workspace**: its tile (the workspace's mark in grey with a small dot in its colour, name on hover), then Home, Projects, Tasks and the rest, with **Connect** and **Trash** as round buttons at the foot. A second short line sets **Settings** last. Outside the lines, items are the same in every workspace; between them, all belong to the open one. Account, sign-in and docs are in Settings.

Where you are sits on a filled tile and is the only icon in colour: Slate's green, in a few tones. Every other icon is grey. The workspace tile is grey too, with one small dot in the workspace's colour. In a short window, overflow folds into **More**.

## Tabs

The main area is one strip of tabs in every world: docs, sessions, terminals, files, a branch's changes and previews.

**A click opens a temporary tab** (italic title) that the next thing you open replaces: a doc in the sidebar, or a row, file or branch in the Sessions list. A tab is kept when you:

* edit the doc (body, title, icon, cover or status)
* double-click the tab, or the doc in the sidebar
* choose **Keep open** or **Pin** from its right-click menu
* open it beside the current tab (⌘-click)

A doc you create or duplicate opens kept, and so does a session you launch.

Tab keys (⌃⇥ by recency, ⌘1‥⌘9, ⌘W, ⌘⇧T, ⌘⇧J, ⌥⌘←/→, ⌘⇧D, ⇧⌘\\) and mouse gestures (double-click, drag, middle-click, right-click, ⌘-click) are in [Keyboard shortcuts](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/shortcuts.md#tabs-and-the-mouse). Every close spares **pinned** tabs, and **⌘W** on a pinned tab refuses until you unpin it.

Two open tabs with one title (two projects each with a doc called **README**) each also show their parent doc's name in grey. ⌘K lists open tabs first, most recently shown first, without duplicates.

Closing a hosted session's tab asks whether to end it or keep it running ([Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md)). The neighbouring tab of the same kind takes over, so closing a session never leaves the Sessions world. A session that ends takes its tab with it.

Open tabs return after a restart, in order, with pinned and kept state, **per workspace** (each keeps its own strip). Up to twenty come back. A session tab returns only while its session still runs. A strip too wide for its box gets a chevron at the end listing everything open; the tab you switch to scrolls into view.

## See also

* [Docs & the Block Editor](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/docs.md): the docs that search jumps to and indexes.
* [Sessions — the Live Tracker](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md)

---

# Trash

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/trash.md

**Trash** holds the docs and widgets you moved there until you restore them or delete them forever. Open it from **Trash** in the left rail, above Settings.

## What lands here

- **A doc**, with every doc inside it. Use **⋯ → Move to Trash** in the Projects tree, or **Move to Trash** in the doc.
- **A widget.** **⋯ → Move to Trash** keeps every version. Nothing moves here by itself ([Widgets](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/widgets.md)).

Each row says when it was moved and where it came from: "Moved to Trash 5 minutes ago ·
from Acme". A doc that held others shows "**N inside**"; expand it to see them. Click a
title to read it first.

## Restore, or delete forever

A row shows **Restore** and **Delete forever…** when the pointer is on it or focus is in it, so Tab still reaches them.

- **Restore** puts the doc back where it was, with everything that went to the Trash with it. A doc inside it that you had moved to the Trash on its own, earlier, stays in the Trash. If its parent is in the Trash too, it stays there with it until the parent comes back.
- **Delete forever…** asks first and cannot be undone. A doc's nested docs go with it. A widget loses every version and the data it kept. If another Mac restored the same doc or widget and has not synced since, delete forever still wins: your next sync makes that Mac move its copy to its Trash. A restore made on that Mac after it has seen that stays restored.

Tick rows to act on several: **Restore (N)** and **Delete forever (N)**. **Select all**
ticks every row shown. With nothing ticked, **Empty Trash**, beside the title, deletes forever
everything in the Trash, widgets and docs, after one question.

**Filter by title** narrows the list. With a filter on, the button reads **Delete forever ·
N shown** and removes only the rows you can see forever.

## In a shared workspace

Trash belongs to the open workspace. Moving a doc you wrote to Trash removes it from every
member's copy on their next sync. A teammate's doc under it stays; when you move
yours forever, theirs moves up to your doc's parent ([Working in a Shared
Workspace](workspaces/sharing.md)).

---

# Themes

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/theming.md

Slate has two themes: **Mint** (dark) and **Forest** (light). Choose one in **Settings → Appearance**; it sets the light/dark mode and the whole palette at once.

| Theme | Mode | Look |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Mint** | Dark | The default. A near-black, neutral ground; the brand in mint |
| **Forest** | Light | An off-white, neutral ground; the brand in forest green |

Surfaces, borders, text and icons at rest are neutral grey. Green is kept for a few things: Slate's mark, the main button, what is selected, and the rail tab you are on.

* **Charts** draw one series in sage. The bar you point at turns mint or forest.
* **State keeps its own colours.** Amber means something needs you, red means it failed or the next step cannot be undone, and green means done or connected. A state is always shown with a word or an icon too.
* **The running light is lime,** the brand's fourth colour, and nothing else is: a bright lime on Mint, a deep one on Forest.
* **Terminal output stays in colour.** A CLI's red means a failure. The terminal takes its surface from the theme and keeps its sixteen ANSI colours.

## Workspace colours

A workspace can wear one of nine colours: **Cobalt, Lagoon, Iris, Silver, Orchid, Fjord, Heather, Wisteria** and **Graphite**. They are cool colours and two neutrals, so none competes with the brand green or reads as a state. A few are close for some colour-vision types (Iris and Silver under tritanopia), so a workspace's mark is always shown beside its name. Choose one in **Settings → Workspaces**. The colour marks the workspace in the switcher's list, in Settings, in the Sessions workspace picker and as a small dot on the workspace tile. Doc icons, the rail tabs and the Sessions map wear the brand, not the workspace.

## Light and dark with ⌘⇧L

**⌘⇧L**, or **Toggle light / dark theme** in the palette, switches between Mint and Forest. The **Active** card in Settings → Appearance moves with it. All keys: [Keyboard shortcuts](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/shortcuts.md).

## Brand colour

Buttons, links and focus rings use mint on Mint and forest on Forest. It is not a setting. On Mint the main button is mint with forest words; on Forest it is forest with paper-white words.

> **Note:** There is no per-element colour picker and no custom theme file. A theme chosen in an older version (Strata, Chalk, Onyx or Graphite) opens as Mint or Forest, whichever has the same mode.

## Size

**⌘+ and ⌘−** zoom the whole app (text, icons, spacing, memory graph) in ten-percent steps from 80% to 140%, starting at 110%. The zoom is saved on this computer, not in your workspace. In a terminal the same keys resize only that terminal's font; click outside it to zoom the app again.

## See also

* [Memory Graph and Map](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/map.md)
* [Typed Docs & Hierarchy](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/docs/typed-docs.md)
* [Sessions — the Live Tracker](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md): where the running light appears

# Slate as an MCP Server

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server.md

Slate runs an MCP server that gives every agent one workspace and one long-term memory: what one tool saves, the next recalls. All 16 agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Antigravity, OpenCode, Gemini, Cline, Grok Build, Kiro, Qwen Code, Droid, Hermes Agent, Goose, Kilo Code and Auggie) can connect. Connect is measured on 15 and unverified on Kiro ([Features by Agent](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/tool-features.md)).

## What it is

Agents reach it over streamable HTTP on the running app, `http://127.0.0.1:47366/mcp` (the port follows the Mac user: 47366 for the first account, then 47367 and up), with the app's private key in a header; sessions start no processes. The `slate-mcp` binary serves the same tools over stdio, for Claude Desktop and other stdio-only clients.

## The recall / remember contract

Every connected model gets a standing instruction (within Claude Code's 2,048-character limit); tool descriptions hold the detail.

* **Start.** If no brief opened the session and no direct tool answers, call `recall({ query: "current branch goal and context", cwd })` for decisions, conventions, memories and the branch brief.
* **During.** `record_decision` keeps a decision and its reason. At a milestone the agent asks whether to save a plan, review, test plan, bug report or design, and calls `create_doc` only after a yes. It lists the refs of memories that shaped its work in `used`, never in its reply. If a memory's `citation` says `changed`, it reads the code first, and calls `remember` with `replaces` if the memory is wrong.
* **End.** The agent must call `log_mission_progress` once before its final reply, and saves at most two memories, only what will change how a future agent acts.

How the two verbs rank, stay silent and dedupe is in [Recall & Remember](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/recall-remember.md).

A client never calls a mutating tool to test the connection: `slate_capabilities` is the read-only check. A write to an existing doc takes its id from a prior Slate result or from you.

## The shared half

`recall` searches the workspace owning the working folder, on this machine only (in a shared workspace, that includes teammates' work your copy holds). `recall_workspaces` and `workspace_doc` search the cloud across every shared [workspace](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md) you belong to, even ones this machine has not added. Both are read-only; Row Level Security decides what they see. They are separate verbs so private and shared knowledge stay distinguishable.

## Capability discovery

The contract id is `slate-mcp-contract/2026-11-10`; `slate_capabilities` returns version, tools, access levels, approval policies and schema hash.

## See also

* [Tool Reference](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tools.md) — all 27 tools and their arguments.
* [Connecting Your Agents](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/connecting.md) — wire a tool to Slate.
* [Workspaces](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md) — what `recall_workspaces` reads.
* [Connected MCP Tools](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/connected-tools.md) — the reverse direction, where Home is the client.

---

# Connecting Your Agents

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/connecting.md

Any MCP-capable tool can connect and share Slate's memory. What it can then do: [Tool Reference](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tools.md).

## From the app: Connect → Agents

In **[Connect → Agents](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md)**, pick the tool and account and switch Slate on. It registers for that config directory, so it holds for every project here. [Toolkit](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio.md) can also project MCP configs to every tool.

Every session talks over HTTP to the running Slate app (`http://127.0.0.1:47366/mcp` for the first account on the Mac; each other Mac user gets the next port, 47367 and up). The entry carries a private key in a header, so Slate writes it into the tool's config file and makes the file readable by you only. Existing setups switch over on the next launch of Slate. The key opens Slate's MCP server and nothing else. Slate does not write it into a config file that is a link (for example into a dotfiles folder): connecting that tool shows an error, and you replace the link with a plain file.

**Another program on Slate's port.** If something else holds the port when Slate starts, Slate shows a red line at the top of the window with the port number: agents cannot reach Slate. Run `lsof -i :<port>` to see which program it is, quit it, then restart Slate. Two Mac users whose ids are 64 apart share a port, which shows the same line for the second one.

**Slate must be running.** With it closed, the tool lists `slate` as failed and the session-start hook says so. Open Slate and start a new session (Claude Code: `/mcp` also reconnects).

## By hand

The app's entry is the supported way. To write it yourself, read the key from `slate-mcp-token` beside your workspace database and `chmod 600` the config. Claude Code, `~/.claude.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "slate": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "http://127.0.0.1:47366/mcp",   // your port: 47366 for the first account, one more for each next user
      "headers": { "x-slate-token": "<the key>" }
    }
  }
}
```

Other tools spell it their own way: Cursor `{url, headers}`, Gemini `{httpUrl, headers}`, OpenCode `{type: "remote", url, headers}`, Codex `url` and `http_headers` under `[mcp_servers.slate]`.

### Claude Desktop and other stdio-only clients

Run the binary inside the app bundle, with no args:

```
command: /Applications/Slate.app/Contents/MacOS/slate-mcp
args:    []
```

That is one process per client, so the agents use the HTTP entry.

## Verify it works

Ask your agent:

> "Use the slate_capabilities tool to check the Slate contract, then use recall with query 'test' to check if Slate is connected."

An answer mentioning your workspace means it works; empty results are fine.

## The contract

Generated from the MCP tool registry and checked by `packages/mcp/test/tools/contract.test.ts`.

<!-- slate-contract:start -->
| Tool | Access | Write target |
|---|---|---|
| `slate_capabilities` | read | — |
| `create_doc` | write | — |
| `get_doc` | read | — |
| `append_to_doc` | write | id, target.kind:branch, target.kind:knowledge_doc; ambiguity=refuse |
| `remember` | write | — |
| `recall` | read | — |
| `get_memory` | read | — |
| `log_mission_progress` | write | — |
| `list_memories` | read | — |
| `propose_memory_change` | write | — |
| `record_decision` | write | — |
| `get_artifact` | read | — |
| `publish_artifact` | write | — |
| `get_widget` | read | — |
| `publish_widget` | write | — |
| `activity` | read | — |
| `handoff` | write | — |
| `live_sessions` | read | — |
| `propose_setup_change` | write | — |
| `get_agent_run` | read | — |
| `report_agent_run_step` | write | — |
| `my_tasks` | read | — |
| `update_my_task` | write | — |
| `connected_tools` | read | — |
| `read_connected` | read | — |
| `recall_workspaces` | read | — |
| `workspace_doc` | read | — |
<!-- slate-contract:end -->

A tool can save a typed document and add to a doc, and nothing else. Saving a document of a type the project already has on that branch rewrites that doc. Every tool carries the standard MCP labels, so a client can skip asking before a read. See [Tool Rules](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tool-rules.md).

A failed call answers JSON with `error.code` and `error.message`:

* `invalid_arguments` — an argument the tool's schema rejects (a missing `id`, a wrong type).
* `unknown_tool` — a tool name this server does not have.
* `approval_required` — `create_doc` without `user_approved:true`.
* `content_required` — `create_doc` for a typed doc with no `markdown`.
* `target_not_found`, `target_archived`, `ambiguous_target` — a doc, or a project and branch label, that does not resolve to exactly one live doc.
* `invalid_request`, `not_found` — a bad `update_my_task` call (such as both `in_minutes` and `at`, or a time with `clear_reminder`), or an item that is not there.
* `proposal_refused` — a `propose_memory_change` the project's memories cannot take.
* `not_a_project`, `invalid_proposal`, `already_offered` — a `propose_setup_change` for a folder that is not there, a change that could never apply, or one the project already had.
* `artifact_not_found`, `invalid_artifact`, `is_a_widget` — the artifact tools.
* `widget_not_found`, `invalid_widget`, `build_failed`, `not_a_widget`, `version_conflict` — the widget tools (`version_conflict`: someone published a newer version while this one built; publish again).
* `wrong_workspace` — the `cwd` belongs to another workspace than the session's ([Tool Rules](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tool-rules.md#which-workspace-a-call-reaches)).
* `no_task` (`get_agent_run` outside an agent run); `stale`, `closed`, `invalid` — a refused `report_agent_run_step`.
* `slate_not_running` — `connected_tools` or `read_connected` while Slate is closed.
* `store_unavailable` — the workspace file is behind this build, so this process cannot change it.
* `internal_error` — anything else, with its message.

A refused `remember` or `record_decision` is not an error. The answer says `saved: false` with the reason.

Memory lands in the workspace the call's `cwd` belongs to (Personal unless the folder belongs to a shared one). Read, edit or retire entries under **Memory**.

## Troubleshooting

- **"command not found" / "no such file".** Slate is not in `/Applications`: install per [Getting Started](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/overview/getting-started.md#1-install), or from source `bash scripts/install.sh`.
- **Tools appear but calls fail.** The workspace database may not exist yet: open the app once; it creates `~/Library/Application Support/app.slate.workspace/workspace.db`. If you moved Personal, the server opens the moved file.
- **From a git clone.** Run `node packages/mcp/dist/index.js`, built by `yarn workspace @slate/mcp build`.

## See also

* [Slate as an MCP Server](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server.md)
* [Tool Reference](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tools.md)
* [Connect](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md) — the screen that installs Slate, and what it writes.
* [Toolkit](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio.md)
