# Tool Reference

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tools.md

Slate's MCP server exposes 27 tools. Rules for workspace resolution and what an agent may not do: [Tool Rules](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tool-rules.md).

Almost every tool takes an optional **`cwd`** (your working directory), resolved to the workspace that owns the folder; `slate_capabilities`, `recall_workspaces` and `workspace_doc` read no local workspace. Every tool carries the standard MCP labels (title, read-only, whether a write can replace). Claude Code loads `recall` and `remember` at session start, the rest on demand.

## Docs

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `create_doc` | Create a typed doc: `title`, `doc_type`, `user_approved:true`, `markdown`, optional `parent_id`, `source_ref`. Without `parent_id` it files under the project holding `cwd`, labelled with the checked-out git branch. Refused without `markdown` or unless the user said yes first. A second call for the same type on the same branch rewrites that doc. |
| `get_doc` | Read one doc by `id` or `target`: title, icon, breadcrumb path, Markdown body. A colleague's shared doc: `workspace_doc`. |
| `append_to_doc` | Append Markdown to a doc, by `id` or `target`. Replies with id, title and path. |

Find docs with `recall` and `kind: "docs"`. Plain docs, rename, move and trash are app-only ([why](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tool-rules.md#what-an-agent-cannot-do-over-mcp)).

## Memory

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `remember` | Save one typed memory (`kind`: `decision`, `preference`, `state`, `fact`, `lesson`), filed by `cwd`. A near-duplicate strengthens an existing memory; a new claim on the same slot replaces the old. `replaces`: refs this corrects and retires. `when` makes a lesson fire on a matching tool call: `{tool: "shell", match}` or `{tool: "read" \| "edit", path}` (a match-everything pattern is refused). `index: true` pins it into the project index; `unindex` removes refs. Reply: `saved`, `memory`, up to 3 `neighbours`. Refused, with reason, when: the text is passing status, a git snapshot or a tool call's markup; a `decision` has no reason; an agent memory holds 3+ numbers (put them in `reason`); a `state` has no `subject`; the project's [memory settings](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/decisions-and-facts.md#what-a-project-keeps) turn off that writer, kind or word; AI memory care is on and `reason` is under 4 words; or the workspace is read-only for you. A title-like line is kept with a `warning`. A claim contradicting a firmer memory waits for review in Memory. |
| `recall` | The one search. When the query is about the branch (names it, or asks what is open or in progress) the first result is the branch brief, with the `target_doc_id` writes file under. Then memories (BM25 over sentence, tags, citation, reason, plus small recency and confidence lifts), then docs whose text matches (not title-only matches or captured session docs). A memory under 0.7 of the best memory's score is left out. Each memory is a line with `ref` (`m:7f3a2b1c`) and citation, marked `weak` for a thin match and `citation: changed` or `gone` when its code moved. Default 8 results, max 25, at most half memories. `scope: "all"` searches every project. `also`: up to 3 other phrasings, merged by rank. Then up to 2 artifacts matching every word (`artifact_id`, title, snippet, `link`). `kind: "docs"`: docs only, up to 20 hits with snippets. `as_of` (`2026-08-01`): memories only, as believed at the end of that day, later-replaced ones marked `until`. |
| `get_memory` | Read memories in full by `refs` (max 20): claim, reason, `citation` (`same`, `changed`, `gone`, `unchecked`), `evidence` (tools that confirmed it), `history` (what it replaced and was replaced by). Unknown refs return under `unknown`. |
| `list_memories` | For a tidy the person agreed to: the project's memories, oldest first, max 100 per call from `offset`, each with ref, kind, text, whether resting. Memories hidden from sessions are left out. |
| `propose_memory_change` | Propose a `merge` (2–50 `refs` into one `text`), a `retire`, a `lesson` (`refs` into one lesson `text` with its `when`), or a `skill` (a lesson as a skill file in the project folder; Slate offers these itself). Nothing changes until the person accepts it in Memory → Needs review. `proposal_refused`: ref outside the project (unplaced refs under `unknown`), merge or lesson with no text, lesson with no `when`, or text the save rules refuse. |
| `log_mission_progress` | Report a session's work on its branch: `cwd`, `summary`, optional `branch` (if the work was on another git branch), `goal`, `open_items`, `decisions`. The summary becomes a session entry, goal and open items feed the branch's next brief, each decision becomes a memory, all labelled with the branch. Each item passes the memory policy and admission rules; refusals come back in `refused`. Makes no doc. |

## Workspaces

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `recall_workspaces` | Search what others published across your workspaces: `memory` (one sentence each, with author) and `pages` (title, doc type, author, excerpt). Default 8 each, max 25. |
| `workspace_doc` | Read one shared doc in full as plain text, by the `id` `recall_workspaces` returned. |

Both read the [cloud](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md), need a cloud sign-in and are read-only. For a workspace you are not in, Row Level Security returns an empty result. Signed out, they say so.

## Activity

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `activity` | What you did across tools and projects. `view: "recent"` (default): sessions newest first over `days` (default 1, max 90); one session is one conversation the tool gave an id; each row has a `docId` (its session doc, else its project's). `view: "parked"`: branches left with UNCOMMITTED changes and not revisited; `stale_after_hours` default 48. `limit` default 10, max 50. |

## Your Tasks list

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `my_tasks` | Your [Tasks](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks.md) list. `view: "today"` (default): your overdue or due-today to-dos, grouped as the Tasks tab does, plus the first 10 open items from your tools, each with its key (`PROJ-12`, `acme/api#412`). `view: "all"`: every open to-do and up to 100 items. Omitted counts: `more_tasks`, `more_items`. No meetings. Old name `my_work` still answers for one release. |
| `update_my_task` | Add a line to your list (no `id`, with `title`) or change one (`id`): tick (`done: true`), reopen (`done: false`), rename, or set/clear a reminder (`in_minutes` or `at` ISO instant; `clear_reminder: true`). Pass one of the three: two at once is refused, not resolved. A reminder notifies when due. Jira, Linear and GitHub items are refused, naming where to change them. Old name `update_my_work` still answers for one release. |

## Apps you connected in Slate

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `connected_tools` | Apps this workspace connected in [Connect → Integrations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md#integrations) (Linear, Notion, Jira…) and each one's read-only tools. `app` lists one. An app whose tools cannot be listed says why (for example, sign in again). |
| `read_connected` | Read through an app: `tool` is `<app>__<tool>` as `connected_tools` lists it, `args` are its own. Slate calls with its own sign-in, so your agent needs no MCP server for the app. Reads only; writing tools are refused. The answer is the app's text, marked `trust: "outside"`, cut at 20,000 characters; the same read within a minute answers from the last call. |

Both need Slate open (else `slate_not_running`) and read only the apps of the folder's workspace. Your rules treat a read through Slate as a call to the app: a Deny of `mcp__linear__*` holds here too.

## Other agents

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `handoff` | Leave one note for the other agents in the project, or for one with `to`. Each sees it once at the start of its next turn. Notes that only narrate work in progress are refused, with the reason. |
| `live_sessions` | Every AI session running now: tool, status (working / needs_you / idle), project, git repository, branch, title, last thing said, last active, goal and next unchecked item, doc id (`targetDocId`), folder (`cwd`). Read a session's doc by passing that doc id and `cwd` to `get_doc`. `cwd` limits to your project; your own `sessionId` leaves you out. |

When another agent works in the same project, Slate says so once at the start of a turn, with that session's own words and a doc id. Agents talk by notes: `handoff` with a `to` is a message, and a reply is another `handoff` addressed back. A note with no `to` is for everyone working here. There is no channel, inbox or queue.

## Decisions and artifacts

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `record_decision` | Record a decision: `title`, `reasoning`, `confidence` (`high`, `medium`, `low`; all required), optional `alternatives`, `outcome`, `source_ref`. Writes a decision memory (confidence 0.95, 0.8 or 0.6) and a decision doc with the full reasoning. Returns the doc `id` and the memory `id` under `memory`. |
| `publish_artifact` | Publish a doc in the **Artifacts** tab. Send `content` (whole doc), `file_path` (a file the tool wrote, inside its `cwd` or the system temp folder) or `edits` (`{old, new}` changes to the newest version; each `old` must appear exactly once). Dot files, files in dot folders below home (such as `.ssh`) and a `cwd` of home or `/` are refused. A new artifact needs `title` and `kind` (`html` or `markdown`); a new version passes the earlier `artifact_id` and keeps both unless given. Optional `description` and `live: true` (the artifact reads this workspace with `slate.query`: docs, a doc, memories, sessions of its project, read-only, up to 5,000 rows each; served with no network, scripts only from cdnjs, jsDelivr, unpkg). Changing `live` adds a version; identical content adds none. Returns `artifact_id`, `version`, `link` (a `slate://` address). `invalid_artifact`: empty title or content, over 5,000,000 characters, file outside the two folders, dot file, too-wide `cwd`, or an edit whose old text is missing or repeated. |
| `get_artifact` | Read before changing: `artifact_id`, optional older `version`. Returns title, kind, description, version read, newest version number and full `content`. Without `artifact_id`: every artifact, newest first. Unknown id: `artifact_not_found`. |
| `publish_widget` | Build and publish a [widget](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/widgets.md) (React files Slate builds and runs in **Widgets**). New: `files` (`[{path, content}]`) and `title`. New version: `widget_id`, only changed files (the rest kept), `delete_paths` to remove. A build error answers `build_failed` with each error's file, line, text and saves nothing. Optional `description`. Returns `widget_id`, `version`, `built_ms`, `published` (false if no file changed), `link`, and `render`: whether the window ran the new version without error (`status` `ok`, `failed`, `pending`; on failure `problems` and a one-line `next`). |
| `get_widget` | Read before changing: `widget_id`, optional older `version`. Returns title, description, version read, newest version, `files`, `render`, `playbook` (build steps and rules), `sdk` (TypeScript declarations every build is checked against) and `examples`: `curated` (Slate's) and `yours` (other widgets in the workspace as `{ widget_id, title, description }`, quoted as data). Without `widget_id`: every widget. Unknown id: `widget_not_found`. |

A widget's id given to `get_artifact` or `publish_artifact` answers `is_a_widget` ("This is a widget. Use get_widget / publish_widget."); a doc's id given to the widget tools answers `not_a_widget`, naming the artifact tools. `get_app` and `publish_app` still answer for one release as deprecated aliases; they take `app_id`.

## Project setup

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `propose_setup_change` | Suggest a change to the project's AI setup: `kind` (`fix`, `copy`, `create`, `improve`, `remove`), `item_kind` (`skill`, `command`, `subagent`, `mcp`), item name, `evidence` (the sentence the person reads). Optional `tool` (for `copy`), `file`, `draft` (whole file, for a skill or subagent `create`). Waits in Toolkit › Suggestions; writes nothing until accepted. Refused: `not_a_project` (`cwd` not a folder here); `invalid_proposal` (a `copy` without `tool`, a `draft` on anything but a skill or subagent `create`, a name not lower-case letters, digits, `-`, `_`); `already_offered` (same suggestion waiting or answered). |

## Agent runs

Only for a session a Slate agent run started (first prompt "Slate task … (token)"). Listed in every session; outside a run `get_agent_run` answers `no_task`.

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `get_agent_run` | The run's current step, attempt and instructions. Takes `cwd` and the `token` from the first prompt, or a `task_id`. A blocked run returns why and tells the agent to wait. |
| `report_agent_run_step` | Report the step `get_agent_run` gave: `task_id`, `step`, `attempt`, an `outcome` (done, blocked, needs_input, failed), a short `summary`, optional `body` as JSON text. A report for an old step is refused and names the current one. |

## Contract

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `slate_capabilities` | Contract version, tools, access levels, approval policies, schema hash. Read-only, no arguments. A tool's access level is its `readOnlyHint`, so they cannot disagree. |

## See also

* [Tool Rules](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tool-rules.md): workspace resolution, secrets, targets
* [Slate as an MCP Server](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server.md)
* [Connecting Your Agents](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/connecting.md)
* [Recall & Remember](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/memory/recall-remember.md) — the memory tools in depth.

# Tool Rules

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tool-rules.md

Rules for every call in the [Tool Reference](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/mcp-server/tools.md). Read them when a call is refused or reaches the wrong workspace.

## Which workspace a call reaches

**One session, one workspace.** The first call with a `cwd` ties the session to that folder's workspace; later calls without `cwd` run there. If that folder is later added to a project in another workspace, or taken out of one, the session follows it to the folder's new workspace. A `cwd` that names a different folder in another workspace is refused with `wrong_workspace` and the session's workspace name: start a session in that workspace's folder instead. A folder matches its project however it is spelled: through a symlink, with `..`, or by its real path. Before the first `cwd`, a call without one gets Personal. Only `live_sessions`, `recall_workspaces` and `workspace_doc` cross workspaces. An agent run's agent reaches its task by the task's token, or from inside the task's folder, wherever the task lives. No tool is marked as reaching outside Slate.

## Secrets

Slate replaces recognised keys, tokens and passwords with `[secret]` in what an agent writes through `remember`, `record_decision`, `create_doc`, `append_to_doc`, `log_mission_progress`, `update_my_task` and the summary of `report_agent_run_step`. It does not do this for `publish_artifact` and `publish_widget` (they carry code) or the `body` of `report_agent_run_step`.

## What an agent cannot do over MCP

A tool can save a typed doc and append to a doc. It cannot create a plain doc, rename, move, duplicate, trash or find-and-replace, because those are undoable gestures in Slate and MCP has no undo. An agent's MCP writes can be undone when the inverse is exact: a new doc goes to Trash, a new memory is retired.

## Resolving a target

`get_doc` and `append_to_doc` take a **`target`** instead of an id:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `kind` | `branch` for the branch overview, `knowledge_doc` for a typed child under it. |
| `cwd` | Your working directory. It anchors to the project, and to its active branch when `branch` is omitted. |
| `branch` | The branch to scope to. |
| `doc_type` | The knowledge doc's type, such as `plan`, `design`, `bug-report`. |
| `title` | The doc title, when `doc_type` is not enough. |

Slate writes only when the target resolves to exactly one doc. An ambiguous target is refused.

## Two tool surfaces

Operations are exposed over MCP (your agents) and in-process (Home's commands). The lists differ on purpose: `slate_capabilities` means nothing in-process, and Home keeps a few finer tools (`recent_activity`, `search_content`, …). `packages/shared/src/tools/operations.ts` declares each concept once with its surfaces.

---

# Curated MCP Commands

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/mcp-commands.md

A curated command routes a request straight to one of Slate's **own** workspace tools (create a doc, search notes, ask a shared workspace) without the model choosing, so a small model works.

## The pipeline

```
request → keyword routing → resolve the tool → prefill known args → model fills the rest (structured output) → one tool call
```

"Create a plan about retries" resolves to `create_doc` with `doc_type` set; the model supplies only the title. The model returns JSON for the missing fields only, and the app merges it with the arguments it injected.

A read tool runs at once. A write asks first, except under Auto-edit and Full auto, where only **Create an automation** and **Run an automation** still ask ([Approvals](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/approvals.md#autonomy)).

## What matches

- A command that writes (doc, project, agent, memory) matches only when your message opens like it ("new project for…", "draft a plan…", "remember that…", after an optional "please" or "can you"). "What's new in this project" is never a command.
- Anything unmatched goes to the agent's own CLI, which loops over its own MCP tools. A turn is one Slate tool call or a CLI handoff.

## Both halves of memory

Home reads this workspace's memory (`recall_memory`) and what colleagues wrote in every [workspace](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md) you belong to, even ones this machine has not materialised (`recall_workspaces`, then `workspace_doc`). Questions like "what does the team know about retries" or "has anyone solved this before" reach the shared half; "what do I know about…" stays local. A shared answer names its author.

Naming a workspace routes to the shared tools, scoped to it, with no MCP connection needed ("what data do I have in my Apollo workspace"). The name counts only beside a team word (*workspace*, *team*, *shared*), so "fix the Apollo timeout bug" stays ordinary.

See also: [Home](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent.md), [Connected MCP Tools](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/connected-tools.md), [Agents & Model Providers](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/brains.md).

---

# Agents & Model Providers

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/brains.md

Slate calls its model providers **agents**: thin drivers over AI CLIs you already installed and signed in to. There is **no API key to paste into Slate**; the CLI makes the model calls with its own auth.

| Agent | Label | Env | Models |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `claude-cli` | Claude Code | `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` | `claude-sonnet-4-6` (default), `claude-opus-4-8`, `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` |
| `codex-cli` | Codex | `CODEX_HOME` | `gpt-5.3-codex` (default), `gpt-5.2`. A fallback only: Slate asks the CLI and lists what the account can reach |
| `gemini-cli` | Gemini | `GEMINI_CLI_HOME` | `gemini-2.5-flash` (default), `gemini-2.5-pro`, `gemini-2.0-flash`. **Needs an API key or a Code Assist licence**, see below |
| `cursor-cli` | Cursor | `CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR` | What your Cursor account offers (`cursor-agent --list-models`). If the CLI cannot be asked: `auto`, `gpt-5.3-codex`, `composer-2.5` |
| `opencode-cli` | OpenCode | — | The providers you are logged into (`opencode models`) |
| `copilot-cli` | GitHub Copilot | `COPILOT_HOME` | What your Copilot plan offers, listed when a session starts. If the CLI cannot be asked: `gpt-4.1`, `claude-haiku-4.5`. Sign in with `copilot login` in a terminal |
| `antigravity-cli` | Antigravity | — | `auto` |
| `cline-cli` | Cline | `CLINE_DIR` | If the CLI cannot be asked: `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`, `anthropic/claude-opus-5.5`, `google/gemini-4-argon` |
| `grok-cli` | Grok Build | `GROK_HOME` | `grok-4.6`, `grok-4.5` |
| `kiro-cli` | Kiro | `KIRO_HOME` | `auto` |
| `qwen-cli` | Qwen Code | `QWEN_HOME` | `coder-model`, `qwen3-coder-plus`, `qwen3-coder-flash` |
| `droid-cli` | Droid | `FACTORY_HOME_OVERRIDE` | `gpt-6.1-sol` |
| `hermes-cli` | Hermes Agent | `HERMES_HOME` | `anthropic/claude-opus-4.6` |
| `goose-cli` | Goose | `GOOSE_PATH_ROOT` | `gpt-4o` |
| `kilo-cli` | Kilo Code | — | `kilo/kilo-auto/balanced`, `kilo/kilo-auto/free`, `kilo/kilo-auto/frontier` |
| `auggie-cli` | Auggie | — | `claude-sonnet-4-6` |

The table follows the order Connect lists the tools. [Features by Agent](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/tool-features.md) shows which tool has which feature.

**The first six tools are measured end to end; the ten newest are not.** Antigravity, Cline, Grok Build, Kiro, Qwen Code, Droid, Hermes Agent, Goose, Kilo Code and Auggie were checked on 2026-11-06 for version, help, MCP setup and the Agent Client Protocol handshake. Unrun features (Home turn, interrupt, asking, token use) are *unverified* or *not yet* in [Features by Agent](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/tool-features.md). They read **Beta** beside their name in setup and in Connect → Agents until their Agent driver cell is "yes". A short model list is a fallback; Slate asks the CLI first.

[Connect → Agents](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md) sets each tool's account and default model; a group or project may override. OpenCode has no config-directory variable, so one account and no profile picker (`OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` only adds agents, commands, modes and plugins).

**Gemini needs paid access since 2026-06-18.** Google stopped serving Gemini CLI for Code Assist for individuals, Google AI Pro and Google AI Ultra. It still works on an API key or a Code Assist Standard or Enterprise licence. On a consumer account `gemini` exits with `IneligibleTierError` before reaching Slate, so the Gemini tool cannot answer. Other tools are unaffected.

## Transport

Rust runs the model calls (`packages/desktop/src-tauri/src/ai/`; `driver.rs` picks the driver from the tool's record in `agentsAndHosts.json`), which keeps auth out of the renderer.

- **Warm process.** Each tool keeps one across Home turns and is sent only your new message. A fresh process (first turn, after restart, after resuming) gets the history first. Resuming always starts fresh, so connected tools may sign in once more.
- **Protocols.** Claude Code and Codex speak their own. Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini, GitHub Copilot and the ten newest speak the Agent Client Protocol (`cursor-agent acp`, `opencode acp`, `gemini --acp`, `copilot --acp`, `grok agent stdio`, `droid exec --output-format acp`, …) in `ai/acp/`. Through it Stop keeps the process, the model can change mid-conversation, and approval cards appear ([Approvals](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/approvals.md#what-differs-by-agent)).
- **Fallback.** A tool silent on the protocol for 20 seconds runs one process per message for the rest of that app session (an automation's unattended Gemini turn too). No card can be answered, so an ask is a refusal (OpenCode's rule: [Approvals](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/approvals.md#what-differs-by-agent)). Cursor runs pre-approved. GitHub Copilot (`copilot -p`) runs every tool only on Full auto, otherwise only what your Copilot settings allow.
- **Automations** run unattended, one process per run. Claude and Codex reach your connected MCP tools and the automation's rules decide each call: reads go on, a call that changes something is held for your answer, and merging, removing, file changes, commands and anything needing more access are refused ([Automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/loop.md#what-it-may-do)).
- **Timeout.** A turn ends when its agent is quiet for 10 minutes; each line it prints starts the 10 minutes again, so a long turn that keeps working is never cut off. A CLI that connects then goes quiet (say, waiting on an auth callback) ends with a readable timeout.
- **Stop.** Stop, New chat and quit also end a message still waiting for a free agent (three run at once, shared with automations and session lanes), so it never runs later where you cannot see it. They never wait on an agent that is not reading what Slate sends it.

## Who runs the tool loop

The agent does. A request that is not a [curated command](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/mcp-commands.md) goes whole to the tool's CLI, which loops over its own MCP tools. A Home turn has **no step cap in Slate**. An automation makes a fixed set of turns: a pass per place its brief checks, one to write the report, one per prompt step.

A run with nobody watching has **one $5 spend ceiling for the whole run**: Slate adds up the cost the tool reports and gives each new turn only what is left; at zero the run stops with a message. Only Claude Code gets it as a flag, with a cap of 30 tool turns per process and the rest of the Claude catalog as **fallback models** for when the primary is overloaded. A tool that reports no cost is limited to 12 turns per run. These limits apply to automations, skill steps and grounding passes, not Home.

A step is bounded by silence: each token, tool call, tool result or usage report restarts a 240-second clock.

Generating a skill also passes a **JSON schema**. Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode enforce it (`--json-schema`, `turn/start`'s `outputSchema`, `opencode serve`'s `session.prompt`); Gemini and Cursor get the shape in prose and their reply is parsed from text.

## Which account an agent runs under

A CLI keeps its config and login in a directory, and you may have several (work and personal Claude). **The workspace decides which one a tool uses**: set it in Connect → Agents; a group or project may override. It also governs terminal sessions you start and what Slate captures ([Project environments](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio/cli-profiles.md)).

See also: [Home](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent.md), [Project environments](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/studio/cli-profiles.md), [Privacy & Security](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security.md).

---

# Features by Agent

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/tool-features.md

Slate works with sixteen agents, and they do not offer the same things. Slate keeps one table of which tool has which feature. Every control that depends on a tool reads it. If a tool cannot do something, the control is hidden or disabled with a reason, never shown doing nothing.

Each cell is one of four answers:

- **yes** — Slate does it on this tool today.
- **not yet** — the tool can do it and Slate does not use it yet.
- **unverified** — it may already work. Nobody has run it to check.
- **no** — the tool has no way to do it. Slate records what was measured and when.

Measured on 2026-09-19 against Claude Code 2.1.278, Codex 0.142.3, Gemini 0.58.0, Cursor's `cursor-agent` 2026.09.15 and OpenCode 1.18.31, on 2026-11-01 against GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.28, and on 2026-11-06 against Antigravity's `agy` 1.5.1, Grok Build 1.0.77, Kiro CLI 3.1.0, Droid 1.4.1, Auggie 0.37.0, Cline CLI 3.0.74, Qwen Code 0.26.8, Kilo CLI 7.8.27, Hermes Agent 0.23.0 and Goose 1.57.0. The CLIs change often, so a "no" is a dated measurement, not a permanent limit.

## Beta agents

An agent whose **Agent driver** cell is "unverified" reads **Beta** beside its name, in setup's Agents step and in Connect → Agents. Today that is ten: Antigravity, Grok Build, Kiro, Droid, Auggie, Cline, Qwen Code, Kilo Code, Hermes Agent and Goose. Slate works with them, but nobody has run a real session on them yet to check every part. The label reads this table, so an agent loses it on the day its Agent driver cell turns "yes". The other six read no label.

Gemini is not Beta, but its row says *Needs a Gemini Code Assist licence or an API key*. Since June 2026, Gemini CLI refuses personal Google sign-ins with `IneligibleTierError` and sends them to Antigravity. Checked again on 2026-11-07 with Gemini CLI 0.58.0.

## Why some cells are "no"

Every "no" was checked against the tool's official documentation or the tool itself, and the code records the day. A cell stays "no" only when those sources offer no way to do it.

- **Budget caps and fallback models** exist only in Claude Code. Gemini has a turn cap and switches from Pro to Flash on its own when rate-limited, but none of the others has a spend cap. Qwen Code has a fallback-model flag, which Slate does not use yet. Slate still bounds an unwatched run on every tool by counting turns for a tool that reports no cost: at most 12 per run (see [Agents & Model Providers](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/brains.md#who-runs-the-tool-loop)).
- **Background sessions** that keep running after you close them: Codex, Gemini and OpenCode have no local way to detach a session. Codex's `cloud exec` runs on OpenAI's servers, so it is a cloud session.
- **Cloud sessions** (work on the vendor's computer, see [Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/cloud.md#cloud-sessions)): Claude Code and Codex have them. Gemini, OpenCode, Cline, Qwen Code, Hermes and Goose have none. Kilo has `kilo cloud`, which Slate does not use yet. Cursor's CLI has a cloud command behind a flag that is off for ordinary accounts, so it is "unverified". Checked 2026-10-07.
- **Structured output**: Gemini, Cursor, Cline and Hermes print a fixed JSON shape only.
- **Choosing a session's id before it starts**: Codex and OpenCode always create the id themselves.
- **Listing running sessions**: Codex, Gemini and OpenCode list saved sessions or history, not running ones.
- **Naming a session**: Gemini keeps no session name, so Slate keeps the one you give.
- **Several accounts**: OpenCode and Kilo have no config-folder variable, so each has one account. Only `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `XDG_DATA_HOME` together move them.
- **Native memory**: Cursor's Memories live only in the editor's settings. OpenCode has no memory feature.
- **OpenCode's end-of-turn save check**: its plugin events all fire after the turn ends, so nothing can hold the turn open.
- **Goose has no hooks**, so Slate cannot check the save at the end of a turn or answer a tool call with an agent run's rules. Its sessions are still captured, from its own database.

Hermes and Goose were measured without a model account: each was installed with its own installer, answered an ACP `initialize`, and ran one turn against a local stand-in for a model, which wrote a real session to its database. Their "unverified" cells need a real model turn. Hermes checks the save only at its `pre_verify` event, which fires on a turn that edited code, so its save check stays "unverified". Hermes runs a hook only once it is approved, so Slate writes its approval into `shell-hooks-allowlist.json` beside the config.

Antigravity, Grok Build, Kiro, Droid and Auggie were measured signed out. Each one answered the ACP handshake Slate starts a session with, and each but Kiro added Slate's MCP server through its own `mcp add`. Kiro's `mcp add` refuses to run signed out, so Slate writes its entry to `~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json` itself. Everything that needs a model turn is "unverified" for these five, because none of them runs a turn without an account.

- **Hooks on Antigravity and Kiro** are "not yet": each keeps its hooks in a file shape of its own, which Slate does not write yet.
- **Kiro's end-of-turn save check** is "no": Kiro's hook docs name only the before-tool hook as able to block in the CLI.
- **Auggie's sessions** are one JSON file each, `~/.augment/sessions/<id>.json`. Slate reads them, and finds the session's folder where Auggie itself does: the workspace folder a turn's IDE state names. Capture stays "unverified" until a signed-in session is seen.
- **Grok Build also runs Claude Code's hooks** from `~/.claude/settings.json` unless `[compat.claude] hooks = false` is set in `~/.grok/config.toml`. With both connected, Slate's hooks can run twice in one Grok session.

Cline, Qwen Code and Kilo were added on 2026-11-06 from their CLIs alone: each answered the ACP handshake, and its `mcp add` wrote the file Slate reads. Cline and Qwen Code ask for sign-in before a session starts, so every cell that needs a real turn is "unverified". Kilo is built on OpenCode and keeps its plugin model and its session database, which Slate reads like OpenCode's. Cline's hooks are one script per event in `~/.cline/hooks`, which Slate does not write yet, and its sessions are JSON files the watcher does not read yet.

Every one of the ten tools added on 2026-11-06 runs a turn in Home through the same ACP driver as Cursor, Gemini and GitHub Copilot, read from its record. Its "agent driver" cell stays "unverified" until one real turn has run on it.

Gemini cells marked "unverified" may already work. On a consumer account Gemini stops before any turn with `IneligibleTierError` (see [agents](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/brains.md)), so they cannot be checked there.

The table lives in `packages/shared/src/agents/features.ts`, with the evidence for every "no". A test fails if this doc and the code disagree.

---

# Settings

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/settings.md

**Settings** is the last item in the left rail. Every tab is about this computer. Which agent a workspace runs, under which account, and what it can reach are in [Connect](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md).

| Tab | What it holds |
|---|---|
| **Account** | Who you are signed in as, your plan, sign-out, and **Delete my account forever**, which removes your Slate account from the cloud and keeps everything on this Mac. See [Licensing & Updates](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/licensing.md). |
| **Workspaces** | Every workspace on this computer: who can see it, where its file lives, how big it is. Open one to share, rename or manage it. See [Workspaces](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md). |
| **Appearance** | Light or dark. See [Themes](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/theming.md). |
| **Terminal** | Font size, line height, cursor shape and blink, scrollback, copy on select. See [Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md). |
| **Keyboard** | Every shortcut in one list. The one place to change or remove one. See [Keyboard shortcuts](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/shortcuts.md). |
| **About** | Version, updates, logs, links, and what Slate may send. See [Licensing & Updates](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/licensing.md) and [Privacy & Security](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security.md). |

What Slate runs on its own is the **Built-in** section of the [Automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/loop.md) place, not a Settings tab. See [Automations](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations.md).

# Keyboard shortcuts

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/shortcuts.md

This guide lists every keyboard shortcut Slate has. Press **?** anywhere for the shortcuts of the current context, or open **Settings → Keyboard** to change one.

Keys are written for a Mac. On Windows and Linux, ⌘ is Ctrl. Shortcuts with ⌘ or ⌃ work while you type. A shortcut on a bare key, or on ⌥ alone, waits until you stop typing, because ⌥ plus a key types a character.

## Rebind a shortcut

**Settings → Keyboard** lists every command in the palette. Click a command's key to record a new one. A key another command held moves over, and a note ("⌘X moved from A to B.") offers **Undo**. Unbind takes a key away; Reset restores the default. **Reset all** restores every key and offers **Undo**. One key per command, no multi-key sequences. The palette, the cheatsheet and tooltips read the same list, so they follow a key you rebind. The shortcuts in the tables below marked "fixed" are not in that list.

## Anywhere

These are the commands in Settings → Keyboard, grouped as the cheatsheet groups them.

### Navigate

| Keys | Command |
| --- | --- |
| ⌘K | **Command palette** |
| ⌘P | **Go to file or doc** |
| ⌘⇧F | **Search docs and files** |
| ⌘⇧K | **Go to Home** |
| ⌘J | **Ask AI** |
| ⌘⇧O | **Steps Ask AI ran** |
| ⌘⇧J | The session that has waited on you longest; again for the next. After the sessions come tasks waiting on you, then back to the first session |
| ⌘[ and ⌘] | **Back** and **Forward** |
| ⌘\` and ⌘⇧\` | **Switch to next workspace** and **Switch to previous workspace** |
| ⌃⇥ and ⌃⇧⇥ | **Next tab** and **Previous tab**, by recency while ⌃ is held: once is the tab you were just on, twice the one before |
| ⌘1 to ⌘9 | **Go to tab 1‥9**; with fewer than n tabs open, the last one |
| ⌘W | **Close tab**. A pinned tab refuses: unpin it first. Every close spares pinned tabs |
| ⌘⇧T | **Reopen closed tab** |
| ⌥⌘← and ⌥⌘→ | **Move tab left** and **Move tab right** |
| ⌘⇧D | **Open tab beside**, such as a session beside its plan doc (⌘-click does the same; also on a doc in the tree, Favorites and Recents, a link in a doc, and **Open beside** in a doc's right-click menu) |
| ⇧⌘\\ | **Close split view** |

### Create

| Keys | Command |
| --- | --- |
| ⌘N | **New doc** |
| ⌘⇧G | **Generate a doc** |
| ⌘⇧N | **Quick capture** |
| ⌃\` | **Open a terminal here** |

### Doc, view and help

| Keys | Command |
| --- | --- |
| ⌘F | **Find in doc** |
| ⌘\\ | **Toggle sidebar** |
| ⌘⇧M | **Focus mode** (the same keys leave it) |
| ⌘⇧L | **Toggle light / dark theme** ([Themes](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/theming.md#light-and-dark-with-l)) |
| ⌘+ and ⌘− | **Increase app size** and **Decrease app size**, 80% to 140% in ten-percent steps ([Themes](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/theming.md#size)) |
| ? | **Keyboard shortcuts** |

## Tabs and the mouse

These gestures are fixed. See [Tabs](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/search.md#tabs) for the rules.

| Gesture | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| ⌘-click a tab, a doc or a link | Open it beside the current tab |
| Double-click a tab | Keep a temporary tab open |
| Middle-click a tab | Close it |
| Drag a tab | Reorder it; pinned tabs stay at the front |
| Right-click a tab | Keep open, pin, open beside, close, close others, close to the right, close all |
| Drag the line between two columns | Widen one column; double-click equalises all |
| Arrow keys on that line | Resize it in steps of 16 px; Shift makes the step 64 px |

## Command palette and lists

| Keys | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| ↑ and ↓ | Move through results |
| Enter | Open the selected row |
| Escape | Close the palette or cheatsheet |
| ⌘Enter | Add a line comment in a file or review, or commit from the Changes message box |
| ⌫ or Backspace | Move the selected docs in the Projects tree to Trash |

## Sessions

| Keys | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| ⌘⇧J | Go to the session that has waited longest ([Sessions](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md#what-you-see)) |
| ⌥⌘B | Show or hide the side panel (Details, Changes, Turns) |
| ⌥⌘I | Open the side panel on Details |
| ⌘K → **Focus the sessions list** | Move focus to the first row; listed only while a row is on screen |
| ⌃\` | Open a plain shell |
| ⌘⇧M | Focus mode |
| ⌘-click a row | **Open beside** |
| ⇧⌘\\ | **Unsplit** the columns |

⌥⌘B and ⌥⌘I are in Settings → Keyboard and work while the Sessions panel is on screen.

On a focused row of the rail ([The keyboard](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions.md#the-keyboard)), with focus inside the rail and no text field active. The cheatsheet lists these under **Session list**; they are fixed:

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab, then Enter | Reach the rows and open one |
| ↑ / ↓ or **k** / **j** | Move between rows |
| Home and End | Jump to the first and last row |
| **f** | Start a second agent in the row's folder |
| **s** | Stop the session; press again within four seconds |
| Escape | Hand focus back to the terminal |

## Terminal

Over a focused terminal, every ⌘ chord belongs to the app except these. On Windows and Linux the app's chord is Ctrl+Shift, and plain Ctrl keys go to the CLI. See [The terminal](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/terminal.md#what-the-terminal-does).

| Keys | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| ⌘F | Search the session, scrollback included |
| ⌘C | Copy the selection; without one, the app's own meaning |
| ⌘V | Paste |
| ⌘+ / ⌘− / ⌘0 | Zoom the terminal font in, out, and reset it (remembered) |
| ⌥⌘K | Clear |
| Shift+Enter | New line in the prompt, without sending |
| ⌥← / ⌥→ / ⌥⌫ | Jump a word left, right; remove a word |
| Ctrl-C | Interrupt, sent to the CLI |

## Files and the editor

In a file ([Reading a file](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/files.md#reading-a-file)). ⌥H and ⌥1‥⌥4 are in Settings → Keyboard and act on the file that has focus; like every ⌥ shortcut, they wait while you type in the editor:

| Keys | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| ⌘S | Save |
| ⌘F | Search the file |
| ⌥H | Open the file's history |
| [ and ] | Step through changes (not while typing) |
| ⌥1 and ⌥2 | Switch between Preview and Read, on a Markdown or SVG file (the code holds up to four forms; today only these two exist) |
| Escape | Leave Diff or a past commit |

The editor uses VS Code's keys ([Editing](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/files.md#editing)):

| Keys | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| ⌘Z / ⌘⇧Z | Undo and redo (Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y on Windows and Linux) |
| ⌥-click | Add a cursor |
| ⌘D | Select the next match |
| ⌘⇧L | Select every match |
| ⌥⇧-drag | Column selection |
| ⌘F | Find and replace |
| Ctrl+G | Go to line |
| ⌘/ | Comment |
| ⌥↑ / ⌥↓ | Move a line |
| ⇧⌥↑ / ⇧⌥↓ | Copy a line |
| ⇧⌘K | Remove a line |
| Enter or Tab | Take an offered word |

## Home

Arrow keys turn the deck of cards on Home; left and right step back and forward.

# Privacy & Security

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security.md

**Sign in once. Your work never leaves your Mac.** Nothing of your work leaves the machine without an action you take.

Your workspace lives in SQLite files on your machine: `workspace.db` (Personal), one file per shared workspace, and `machine.db` (what describes this computer). You sign in once at first launch, with Google or GitHub; the account holds who you are and your plan, not your work. After that Slate works offline; when online it checks your sign-in at each launch.

## Contents

- [Your account](#your-account)
- [What leaves your Mac](#what-leaves-your-mac)
- [How long the cloud keeps it](#how-long-the-cloud-keeps-it)
- [Reporting a problem](#reporting-a-problem)
- [Reporting a vulnerability](#reporting-a-vulnerability)
- More: [Workspace sharing](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security/sharing.md), [Where data lives](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security/where-data-lives.md), [Security details](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security/security-details.md)

## Your account

Sign-in sends your name, email and picture link from Google or GitHub to Supabase Auth in Slate's own Supabase project, which also records which of the two you used. Slate's cloud keeps that profile and an account row with your plan. **Tell me when it's ready** (Team) adds one row: that you asked, and from which screen. The session lands in a `0600` file on your Mac, so later launches need no network. When you are online, Slate contacts its Supabase project at each launch and whenever the sign-in token renews: it renews the token, makes sure your account exists and reads which workspaces you belong to. Those requests carry your account id and your IP address, and no workspace content. Supabase Auth also keeps sign-in logs with your IP address.

Slate's cloud holds only: accounts and plans, opt-in telemetry, problem reports you send, Team interest, invitations (the invitee's email and role, until accepted or declined; Slate sends no email, the invite opens in your own mail app), the update service, and the rows of a workspace you chose to share.

**Removing your account.** Settings → Account → **Delete my account forever** removes your Slate account from the cloud: your identity, name, email, plan and Team interest, your memberships, what you authored in shared workspaces (each row is blanked and marked as removed, so every teammate's Mac removes its copy on the next sync), and any account only you were in. Type your email to confirm. You are signed out, and everything on this Mac stays. If other people are in your account or its workspaces, remove them first; Slate says so and keeps everything. See the [Privacy Policy](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/legal/privacy-policy.md#your-control-export-and-deletion) for what lives outside the database.

## What leaves your Mac

Four exceptions run without a click each time: the agent CLIs, sharing, the update check and opt-in telemetry. A problem report, the requests you start and the connections you set up come after them.

| Exception | What leaves | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agent CLIs | Your prompt and context, sent by the CLI to its model. For a [cloud session](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/cloud.md#cloud-sessions), also the project's code | An [agent](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/brains.md) (any of the 16) runs a CLI you installed, under its own sign-in, for Home, Sessions, agent runs and automations: when you ask it to, or on a schedule you set |
| [Workspace sharing](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md) | Everything in a shared or joined workspace, except what [Workspaces](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md#what-actually-leaves-your-machine) lists as never sent | Only after you switch a workspace (Personal too) to shared, or join one |
| Update check | App version, system, CPU, prerelease flag and an **install id**. Reveals your IP and that you run Slate | 8 seconds after the window opens, then every 4 hours, and on **Check now** in Settings → About. Turn off with Automatic updates in [Automations › Built-in](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/automations.md); the manual check still works |
| Telemetry | Opt-in counts, three events: Slate launched, a session saved, a memory recalled. A saved session and a recalled memory carry the tool's name (one of the 16, or `other`). Crash reports are a separate opt-in: error type and call stack (function, file names, line numbers) | Off until you turn it on in **Settings → About**. Never doc, session or file content, never the error's own text |

- **Agents.** Slate brokers no tokens and runs no web-search proxy. Rust starts the CLI as a child process, so credentials never reach the webview.
- **Install id.** 16 random bytes made once, kept in the `install-id` file in Slate's data folder. It holds nothing about you or your machine and is not the telemetry id. It places your copy in a stable group when a release goes out in steps. Before an update installs, Slate sends only the version to ask whether it was stopped. A newer version (on a Mac, a small patch) downloads from GitHub Releases. The update service keeps no table of ids, but the id is part of the request, so it appears in the request logs its host (Supabase) and the release host (GitHub Releases) keep for a short time. Remove `install-id` and Slate makes a new one. With Automatic updates on, updates download in the background and install when you next quit.
- **Telemetry id and consent** are per machine, in `machine.db`; removing a workspace does not touch them. "New id" replaces the id; turning both switches off withdraws consent.
- **Cloud session.** **Start in cloud**: Claude Code clones your project's GitHub remote (or uploads the code if there is none) to Anthropic's computer. Codex runs in the environment you set up at chatgpt.com. Each uses your sign-in; Slate holds no vendor key and sends nothing. It records the task in `machine.db`: what you asked, your messages, where the task came from.
- **On my phone.** [On my phone](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/sessions/cloud.md#on-my-phone) makes Claude Code connect the session to claude.ai, and Anthropic keeps that conversation. The session still runs here; Slate only types `/remote-control` into its terminal.
- **No model is shipped or downloaded.** Recall is keyword matching on your device.
- **Your shell's environment.** Opened from the Dock, an app gets almost no environment, so Slate asks your login shell once for `PATH` and a fixed list of variables (proxy and certificate settings, `XDG_*`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, node-manager folders, each agent's account variable) and gives them to the programs it starts. API keys and other variables are not copied. The answer is kept in `shell-env.json` in Slate's data folder (readable only by you), so the next launch starts with it at once; the first launch ever waits at most 3 seconds for the shell.
- **Proxies and company certificates.** Every connection Slate makes trusts the certificates in your system's store (a company root certificate included) and goes through your proxy: the macOS system proxy, or `HTTPS_PROXY` / `HTTP_PROXY` from your shell when no system proxy is set. Connections to this computer (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`) never go through a proxy.

**Connections you set up yourself** start when you connect and stop on **Disconnect**. None sends a doc, session or memory.

- Pasted-token apps (Bitbucket, Gitea, Forgejo, Gerrit, YouTrack, Zulip, Rocket.Chat): read requests with that token to the address you gave, and no link that leaves it.
- A web-address tool gateway, or an app connected from Slate: the token that server issued to Slate, sent only to that server.
- GitHub: read through your own `gh` sign-in, after you press Connect on its card.
- MCP servers your agents already have: a toolkit entry already in an agent's config is asked for its tool list at its own address, with the key its config holds, when Tasks syncs and when you let a widget use one of its tools.

**Requests you start.** Git and `gh` fetch, pull, push and open pull requests against your own remote when you press the button. A widget's GitHub action (approve, comment, label) runs only after you confirm its card. A [live artifact](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/artifacts.md#live-artifacts) can load a script from cdnjs, jsDelivr or unpkg, and that host sees the address it asks for.

When an agent calls `read_connected`, Slate reads an app you connected from Slate with its own sign-in, in the workspace of the session's folder, and returns the answer. The sign-in never leaves Slate; nothing is written.

## Reporting a problem

A report leaves only when you press **Send report**. Open it from **Report this** on an error notice, **Help → Report a Problem…** in the Mac menu bar, ⌘K (**Report a problem**), or **Report…** in Settings → About, under Logs. The dialog lists everything that leaves:

- what you wrote under **What happened?**;
- **Where** you were (such as `Tasks` or `Projects › slate · main`, so it can name a project and a branch) and, from an error, its words;
- one line: Slate version, macOS version, chip (`Slate 0.1.54 · macOS 26.6 · Apple Silicon`);
- the last 40 lines of the app log, if ticked (default). **Show** reveals them. File paths become `~/…` before they are shown, so what you read is what leaves. That is the only change: the log lines and the error's words are not otherwise cleaned, so read them, and untick the log if it holds something you would not send.

A report carries no doc, conversation, file, account or install id. It goes to Slate's Supabase project, where anyone can write and only the Slate team can read, whether or not usage counts and crash reports are on. What you wrote, the screen, the error and the version are then copied to a private GitHub issue so the team can track it; the log lines stay in Supabase. A crash's type and stack may be copied to a private GitHub issue the same way. The About row then shows the time and a reference such as `R-7F3A`.

## How long the cloud keeps it

| What | Kept |
| --- | --- |
| Usage counts and crash reports | 180 days, then removed by a daily job |
| Problem reports | 12 months, then removed by a daily job. The GitHub issue copy is removed on request |
| Your account, its profile and sign-in logs | Until you remove it with **Delete my account forever** |
| Invitations | Until accepted or declined |
| Request logs of the update service and the release host | A short time, set by Supabase and GitHub, not by Slate |

To remove usage counts already sent, email your telemetry id (Settings → About) to the contact below before you press **New id**; otherwise they are removed after 180 days.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Email **slate.ai.app@gmail.com** (privacy, security and support) with a description, steps to reproduce and the attacker's gain. Expect a reply within 72 hours and a fix inside 7 days for anything critical. Good-faith research under the safe-harbour terms is authorised: stay within what shows the issue, do not degrade the app for others, allow a reasonable window before disclosure.

Highest severity: a cross-account read through the cloud layer (Row Level Security is its whole access boundary). Out of scope: social engineering, upstream dependency issues, vulnerabilities in the agent CLIs, and theoretical issues with no realistic attack path. Full policy: `.github/SECURITY.md` in the source.

See also: [Your Data & Export](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/data-and-export.md), [Agents & Model Providers](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/agent/brains.md), [Workspaces](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md).

---

# Where Each Piece of Data Lives

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security/where-data-lives.md

No server holds your workspace, only the docs you hand it. A model sees only what you send it in a turn.

| What | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Personal workspace | Local `workspace.db`; syncs only if you switch sharing on ([Your Data & Export](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/data-and-export.md)) |
| Each shared workspace | Its own local SQLite file, same schema, mirrored to and from Postgres |
| Docs, sessions, memories, decisions | Inside that file |
| Which workspaces this machine has | A local registry (names, colours, your role) so the switcher reads offline |
| [Tasks](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks.md) from other tools | One line per task in the workspace file. Never description, comment or message text; never shared. For a tool learned by Teach Slate: how to read it (tool name, arguments, field paths), never its answer |
| [Agent run](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks.md#agent-runs-beta) drafts | PR text, ticket update, review comments or reply, so Approve to ship shows them word for word. In the owning store, removed 30 days after the run closes, never shared. The task description is never stored |
| [Receipts](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/tasks.md#receipts) | One per session, in the file of the workspace holding its folder: last reply's first paragraph, each run's command and result counts, edited paths, commit ids and subjects. Read from the transcript with no model. Never a run's full output; never shared |
| Agent run rules file | Small JSON in the run worktree's own git folder (never committed), or in the run's folder under app data for a reply |
| [Activity](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/activity.md#where-the-numbers-come-from) | Per session and model response: times, token counts, model, the tool's own cost. Never prompt or reply text. In `machine.db`, so never shared |
| Slate's own cost | One line every 15 minutes in `slate.log` (`~/Library/Logs/app.slate.workspace/` on a Mac): CPU, memory and wake counts for server, app and web view. Numbers only, never sent; telemetry switches do not reach it |
| Export | A one-click copy of the SQLite file |
| Agent credentials | None stored; the CLIs hold their own |

Credential files, all `0600`:

| File | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| Cloud session (app-data root) | The cloud sign-in; never in a database, so an export cannot contain a live token |
| `slate-server-token` (in the app-data folder, also when you move Personal) | The credential every local caller presents to the server, capture port included ([how](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security/security-details.md#the-local-server)). Persists across launches. No agent's config holds it |
| `slate-mcp-token` (in the app-data folder too) | A copy sits in each connected agent's MCP entry, in a config made owner-only and never passed on a command line (ADR 0106). It opens Slate's MCP server only, not the rest of the server. Slate will not write it through a config file that is a link |
| `work-gateway-auth.json` | The token a web-address work gateway, or an app connected from Slate, issued to Slate; sent only to that server |
| `work-token-auth.json` | The token you pasted for Bitbucket, Gitea, Gerrit, YouTrack, Zulip or Rocket.Chat, with the account name, keyed by workspace and server. Sent only to that server, never logged, removed on **Disconnect** |
| `oauth-pending.json` | A sign-in in progress; dropped when used and after 15 minutes |

Back to [Privacy & Security](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security.md).

---

# Workspace Sharing, Precisely

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security/sharing.md

Sharing does nothing until you switch a workspace to shared. This guide says what then leaves, what never does, and how to take it back. Other exceptions: [Privacy & Security](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security.md).

## Rules

- While no workspace is shared, sync costs one local query, no network calls, and does not renew your sign-in.
- A shared workspace is a separate SQLite file. A store you never shared has no cloud counterpart, so nothing in it can leak.
- Personal starts unshared. It holds your projects and the sessions and memories captured in them; a session in a folder no project holds is not recorded. Personal can be shared on the Team plan. The switch counts what it would publish before you agree. The rail always shows the workspace you are in.

## What a shared workspace sends

Assume everything is shared: docs, memories, git activity, a record that a session happened (branch and time), and artifacts.

| Withheld | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Machine-specific | The `properties` bag with a project's folder path (only a doc's branch label, a branch name, goes); the absolute path on a commit (the normalised git remote goes instead); per-file path lists from a filesystem watch or `.git/index`; your local sibling ordering |
| Content | Transcript content; the reasoning body behind a memory |
| Never sent | The doc of a captured AI session; a memory that belongs to no doc (global); a memory you hid from sessions; a memory a widget saved |

Full list: [Workspaces](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md#what-actually-leaves-your-machine). Postgres enforces activity kinds with a `CHECK` constraint.

> **Warning:** **Text is not filtered.** A doc body and a memory sentence go up as written, so a path you typed travels with the row. Exception: Slate replaces keys, tokens and passwords it recognises with `[secret]` in every memory before storing it, and in docs an agent writes. A doc you type yourself is not checked, and neither is an artifact or widget an agent publishes (`publish_artifact`, `publish_widget`): they carry code.

## Artifacts and widgets

**Live artifact.** A tool-published `live` artifact asks the Slate window for docs, memories and sessions of its own project, read-only. Its policy blocks every connection, image, form and window to any address, and WebRTC, frames and resource hints are removed. One route remains: a script from cdnjs, jsDelivr or unpkg, whose host sees the address the doc asks for. A teammate's live artifact never reads your store. See [Artifacts](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/artifacts.md#live-artifacts).

**Widget.** A widget runs with no origin and no network (no requests, images, fonts, scripts, WebRTC, resource hints or frames) and reads what its tab shows. A write needs a permission you granted once; a memory or doc write shows its words each time before saving. A memory a widget saves is held until you release it and is never shared with a team. What a widget wrote reaches an agent quoted as data. Its data stays on this computer, and a teammate's widget never reads your store.

| Permission | What it allows | Limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `github.read` | Read-only GitHub reads with your own `gh` sign-in, from four fixed kinds of address; the widget never sees the token | 12 a minute |
| MCP read | A tool you allowed for that widget and ticked read-only. Pinned to its definition (a changed tool asks again); arguments checked against its schema; only servers of the widget's own workspace. The widget never sees an address, token or the server's error words | 20 a minute per server |
| `github.act` | Only ask to approve, request changes on, comment on or label a pull request in your own lists, with words you type yourself. A card names the account that will act, every time; writes go through a fixed list of four GitHub addresses; each action is written down | 5 an hour per widget, 20 for all widgets |

Every release tests the no-network claim in the built Slate app: a hostile widget tries every way out, and listeners on the release Mac must hear nothing. See [Widgets](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/widgets.md).

## Who can see and write

- **One author per doc**, enforced in the database and at local write paths. Teammates read, never modify.
- **Postgres decides who sees what.** Row Level Security is the whole access boundary; a non-member gets an empty result. An isolation test suite must pass before anything built on it ships.
- **Your machine keeps your teammates' names.** To verify their docs offline, each shared workspace's member list (display name, email, picture link) is stored in `machine.db`, only for people you already share with. Leaving removes it; an export does not carry it.

## Switching off and erasing

- **Switch off:** **Settings → Workspaces** → the workspace's **Sharing** switch. It asks, stops publishing and withdraws what was published; your store is untouched. Cloud rows are blanked and every member's copy drops them at the next sync. Switching on again republishes.
- **Move out:** moving a doc back to Personal takes it off the server at the next pass.
- **Erase my work** tombstones every row you authored there (blanked, final). Members' copies drop them at the next sync, and sharing again does not bring them back. This is the Article 17 request. It needs you to be an editor or the owner: a viewer or a former member is told so, and nothing is reported as erased. If any row is still shared afterwards, Slate says how many.

> **Warning:** Withdrawal removes the doc from the cloud, not from anyone's memory of it. Reversible, but not retroactive.

---

# Security Details

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security/security-details.md

Protections around Slate's local server, the files it writes and your databases, and what it does not do. To report a vulnerability, see [Privacy & Security](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security.md#reporting-a-vulnerability).

## Contents

- [Keys and tool configs](#keys-and-tool-configs)
- [The local server](#the-local-server)
- [Workspace isolation](#workspace-isolation)
- [Encryption and the webview](#encryption-and-the-webview)
- [Writes, backups and restore](#writes-backups-and-restore)

## Keys and tool configs

**No API keys.** Model providers are the agent CLIs (any of the 16) you already signed in to.

**Nothing is written into another tool's config until you connect one.**

- Most tools: Slate edits the tool's MCP config and, where the tool takes hooks, installs recall hooks beside it.
- Claude Code and Codex: Slate runs the tool's own plugin install, then removes its own MCP entry once the plugin supplies the server, so nothing is listed twice.
- Connect one tool yourself, from setup's **Connect** step or **[Connect → Agents](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/connect.md)**. Then Slate keeps tools you install later registered too.
- Launch auto-connect never reaches Claude Desktop: it gets Slate when you turn Claude Code on and keeps it when you turn Claude Code off.
- Until you connect a tool, auto-connect is off and no file outside Slate's data directory is touched. Turning it off removes what Slate put there and stays off across restarts.

**Every write copies the original aside first.** Slate keeps the five newest copies of each file it rewrote and sweeps the rest at launch. Only its own go: a `<file>.bak` or `<file>.bak-20260101-120000` you made stays.

**Sign-in never touches the renderer.** Cloud sign-in opens your system browser and returns to a loopback address on Slate's server, which does the code exchange. No code, token or password passes through the UI. The session lands in a `0600` file outside the database.

## The local server

**The workspace port only answers the app.** The server listens on loopback. A web page you visit can POST to a localhost port (CORS only stops it reading the reply), so the server refuses any request whose `Origin` is not Slate's webview and any request to a non-loopback hostname (DNS rebinding). `Origin` proves nothing about a non-browser program, so every request also presents a token minted each run into a `0600` file (`slate-server-token`) in the app-data folder, never in a folder you moved the workspace to. The app window gets it from Slate; another process only by reading that file, which only your user can.

Three cases carry no header: a CORS preflight from the app window (runs nothing), the live event stream (cannot set headers, so the token is in its address), and the two sign-in redirect landings (cloud account, work gateway). Each acts only on a sign-in Slate started, once.

**The auto-capture port is authenticated.** With auto-capture on, a loopback port lets git hooks and shell scripts push a note into Memory. The server rejects requests that do not look like local tooling (which stops a browser), and anything that writes must present the server token (which stops other processes, since only your account reads the file). Captured notes are ranked by recall and can reach later AI sessions, hence the guard. To drive it yourself, send the token as an `x-slate-token` header, read from `slate-server-token`. One port and one token per machine.

**Validated tool arguments.** Every MCP argument is checked against a Zod schema first. A wrong or missing type is rejected, nothing is coerced, an undeclared argument is dropped.

## Workspace isolation

Each workspace stays in its own file and Slate refuses to mix them.

- A server request must name its workspace; one that does not is refused, not filed into Personal.
- Slate's own code cannot open a workspace file without naming it.
- An agent session works in the workspace of the first folder it names and is refused another workspace's folder.
- Each file records its workspace, so a misplaced file does not open as another workspace.
- Sessions shows every workspace at once, and so does the `live_sessions` tool: an agent in any workspace sees every running session, with its title, last reply, goal and folder. `recall_workspaces` and `workspace_doc` read the cloud copy of every workspace you belong to. Nothing else crosses workspaces.
- A test plants a marker in one workspace and asks every part of the server and every agent read for it from another. It must never come back.

## Encryption and the webview

**Slate encrypts nothing at rest.** `workspace.db`, shared workspace files, `machine.db` and their WAL sidecars are unencrypted. Confidentiality rests on your OS's full-disk encryption (FileVault, BitLocker, LUKS) and file permissions. There is no SQLCipher build, key or passphrase. Anyone with the decrypted volume and your user's read access can read every workspace. **If you need application-level encryption at rest, Slate does not meet that today.** The cloud session and work gateway sign-in files are unencrypted too, but `0600` and outside every database.

**Webview CSP.** The Tauri webview runs under an enforced Content Security Policy, so the renderer cannot reach arbitrary network origins.

## Writes, backups and restore

- **Transactions.** Every change is a SQLite transaction; WAL mode lets reads continue during writes.
- **Backups.** Slate copies a database aside before any schema migration and keeps the last three per store. Leaving or deleting a workspace forever also keeps a copy.
- **Restore.** **Settings → Workspaces → (the workspace) → Storage → Restore a backup** lists them. It applies at the next launch, and the workspace it replaces is kept too. If a connected agent still has the workspace open, the restore is refused; quit those tools and retry.

---

# Your Data & Export

Source: https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/data-and-export.md

Everything (docs, captured sessions, memories, decisions, automations, settings) lives in SQLite files on your machine: `workspace.db` (Personal), one per shared workspace, and `machine.db` (this computer). There is no proprietary container and no cloud copy unless you share a [workspace](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md) or join one. Sharing publishes what is in that workspace, except what [Workspace Sharing, Precisely](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security/sharing.md) says is never sent.

## Where the file lives

| Platform | Path |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/app.slate.workspace/workspace.db` |
| Linux | `$XDG_DATA_HOME/app.slate.workspace/` (`~/.local/share/` when unset) |
| Windows | `%APPDATA%\app.slate.workspace\` |

To keep Personal elsewhere (an external drive or another folder on this computer), move it in **Settings → Workspaces → (the workspace) → Storage**. Slate restarts by itself and makes the copy at the next launch, before anything has the file open, checks it (integrity check, row counts, write-ahead mode) and only then points at it. While the move waits, agents and hooks refuse to open the workspace, so nothing writes between the two files. Backups go with it; the app, MCP server and capture hooks follow. Slate refuses a folder that a sync service owns (iCloud Drive, including Desktop and Documents when iCloud syncs them; Dropbox, OneDrive and Google Drive roots) and a network drive: the database cannot run safely there. If the drive is not connected, or the file that records where Personal went cannot be read (empty after a power cut, for example), nothing opens a different empty workspace in its place: the app shows its missing-workspace screen (also when the drive goes away while Slate is open), hooks skip quietly and agents are told the workspace is not connected. If the folder is there but macOS will not let Slate open it (Documents or Desktop with access turned off in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Files and Folders), the screen says so and names that setting instead, with no **Start empty here**: the workspace is most likely still there, and agents are told the same. **Start empty here** sets the old copy at the default location aside, dated, and starts a really empty workspace; when the moved one is back, **Use a workspace from another folder** in Storage points Slate at it. The local API tokens stay in the app-data folder. `SLATE_DB_PATH` points one launch at another file (for testing).

## Where to find all of this

Open **Settings → Workspaces**, click the workspace, then **Storage**. The dialog has up to three tabs: **General** (sharing, name, colour, the remove buttons including **Delete workspace forever**), **Members** (shared workspaces) and **Storage**. Only Personal can be relocated; shared workspaces are replicas in Slate's data folder. **Delete workspace forever** leaves no copy: the store and its upgrade backups are removed, with no way back. Export it first if you may want it.

## How big it is

The row under the path shows size on disk and the dead space removed rows left. SQLite never shrinks a file itself, so Slate rewrites it at launch when enough is worth returning. **Reclaim** does it now (shown only when enough can be returned).

## Exporting

**Settings → Workspaces → (the workspace) → Storage** exports in one click a copy of the file (`workspace.db` for Personal, `workspaces/<id>.db` for a shared one), with no conversion. The same screen opens the folder.

## The format is open

Open `workspace.db` in any SQLite browser:

| Table | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `page` | The universal unit: docs, documents, `mission` docs, captured sessions |
| `memory` | Persistent knowledge with status and text |
| `routine` | Automations: what runs on a schedule or on an event, with its steps |
| `artifact`, `artifact_version` | Published docs and widgets, with every version |
| `task`, `task_step` | Agent runs and their steps |
| `task` | The lines on your Tasks list |
| `setting` | Workspace settings |
| `activity` | Commits, branch events and session records captured for this workspace |
| `audit` | The append-only log of workspace events |

Doc bodies are block JSON, and Slate converts docs to and from Markdown.

## Durability

* **WAL mode.** Reads continue while the server writes.
* **Pre-migration backup.** Slate backs up the database before any schema migration.
* **A way back from an update.** The backups sit in a `backups/` folder next to the workspace file, named like `workspace-pre-v170.db`. Slate keeps the last three per workspace. To go back to an older version of Slate, restore one in **Settings → Workspaces → (the workspace) → Storage → Restore a backup**, then install the older version. Without that, an older version refuses to open a workspace a newer one has changed, and says so.
* **No backup, nothing lost.** If Slate cannot write the backup (a full disk, for example), it holds back any update step that could lose data. It tells you, and finishes the update at the next launch that can make the backup.
* **Stray workspace files are moved, never removed.** At startup Slate moves an empty `workspaces/<id>.db` that belongs to no workspace you joined into `backups/`, only when it holds nothing beyond a brand-new database. Any other file stays.

The file is standard SQLite at a known path, so you can back it up, move it or read it years from now with other tools.

## What the export does not contain

**Your cloud session** sits outside the database, in a `0600` file in the app-data folder that stays there when you move Personal, so an export never carries a live refresh token.

Everything else is in the file. Before you share an export, know that:

* **A shared workspace's export contains your teammates' work too.** Sync pulls their docs, memories, activity and artifacts into your copy.
* **Moving a doc into a shared workspace is a move, not a copy.** It leaves your Personal file.
* **A project's memory settings travel with it.** They, and where you said a memory goes, are in the same file.

## See also

* [Privacy & Security](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/privacy-and-security.md)
* [Workspaces](https://liozelmalem-star.github.io/slate-releases/docs/features/workspaces.md)
